item.name: Codex of the Last Archivist
entries: This black, leather-like spellbook is bound in tarnished silver and sealed by an eye-shaped clasp. Its pages appear blank until touched by its attuned keeper, whereupon silver script emerges across them. No reliable record identifies its maker or origin.

entries.name: Arcane Supremacy
entries: While holding the codex, you gain a +3 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your spells. The codex can be used as a Spellcasting Focus.

entries.name: Endless Archive
entries: The codex can be used as a spellbook and can contain any number of Wizard spells.
The time and gold required to copy a Wizard spell into the codex are halved.

When you finish a Long Rest, choose one Wizard spell recorded in the codex. That spell is always prepared for you until you finish your next Long Rest, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare.

entries.name: Forbidden Index
entries: You have Advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) checks concerning spells, magical writing, curses, artifacts, or lost magic.
{@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} and {@spell Identify|XPHB} are always prepared for you while you are attuned to the codex, and they don't count against the number of spells you can prepare.
You can also cast {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} and {@spell Identify|XPHB} from the codex without expending a spell slot.

entries.name: Archive the Unwritten
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet casts a spell of level 1 through 9, you can take a Reaction to record an echo of that spell in the codex as an Archived Spell.

Before you finish your next Long Rest, you can cast the Archived Spell once without expending a spell slot and without providing any Material components, regardless of their cost or whether they would normally be consumed. You use your own spellcasting ability for the spell.
Once you successfully archive a spell with this property, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Perfect Recollection
entries: When you cast a spell recorded in the codex using a spell slot, choose one of the following benefits:

items: You have Advantage on one spell attack roll made as part of the spell.
One creature affected by the spell has Disadvantage on the first saving throw it makes against the spell.
The spell ignores Resistance to one damage type it deals.

entries: You can use this property a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Unbroken Formula
entries: You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws made to maintain Concentration.
When you fail a Constitution saving throw to maintain Concentration, you can choose to succeed instead. Once you do so, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Final Annotation
entries: When you fail a saving throw against a spell or magical effect, you can choose to succeed instead. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Unblemished Archive
entries: The codex can't be permanently damaged or destroyed by ordinary means. Torn pages restore themselves, erased writing returns, and damage to its binding repairs itself.

If the codex is destroyed while it has a Soul-Bound keeper, it reforms beside that keeper at the next dawn with all of its recorded contents intact. If it has no Soul-Bound keeper, it reforms at the site where it was destroyed.

entries.name: Curse: The Endless Archive
entries: The codex bears a 9th-level curse. Attuning to it binds the keeper to the Archive.

entries.name: Soul Bound
entries: You can't willingly end your Attunement to the codex, willingly relinquish it, or willingly remain separated from it.
The codex can't be permanently taken from you by force. If it is separated from you, it reappears on your person after the separation can no longer be maintained.
No other creature can attune to the codex while your Soul Bound connection remains.

entries.name: Archivist's Claim
entries: While Soul Bound to the codex, you can't willingly attune to another cursed magic item.
You have Advantage on saving throws and ability checks made to resist an effect that would forcibly bind you to, possess you through, or establish magical ownership over you.

entries.name: Curse Suppression
entries: While the codex is in your possession, curse effects of 9th level or lower can't affect you. A curse originating from a magic item of Legendary rarity or lower is likewise suppressed against you.
A curse already affecting you is suppressed rather than removed while this property applies.
Artifacts, deities, and effects of comparable power can ignore this protection at the GM's discretion.

entries.name: Archive Remembers
entries: Arcane writing recorded in the codex can't be permanently erased, removed, or destroyed. Lost arcane writing returns the next time the codex is opened.

entries.name: Breaking the Curse
entries: {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} suppresses the Soul Bound curse and its restrictions for 24 hours but doesn't permanently end it.
{@spell Wish|XPHB} or magic of comparable power can permanently break the curse.

item.name: Ascendant Script Tattoo
entries: This tattoo resembles a line of arcane notation written directly into the skin. The symbols subtly rearrange themselves whenever their bearer casts a spell.

entries.name: Ascendant Casting
entries: When you cast a spell of level 1 through 8 using a spell slot, you can expend charges to treat the spell as though it were cast using a spell slot one level higher for each charge expended, to a maximum effective spell level of 9. You can expend no more than 2 charges on a single spell.

entries.name: Overflowing Spell
entries: When you use Ascendant Casting, you can expend 1 additional charge and choose one of the following effects:

items: {@b Empowered.} Reroll a number of the spell's damage dice up to your Proficiency Bonus. You must use the new rolls.
{@b Extended.} If the spell has a duration of at least 1 minute and isn't Instantaneous, double its duration, to a maximum of 24 hours.
{@b Far-Reaching.} If the spell has a range of at least 10 feet, double its range. If its range is Touch, its range becomes 30 feet.
{@b Overwhelming.} One creature affected by the spell has Disadvantage on the first saving throw it makes against the spell.

entries.name: Restored Script
entries: The tattoo regains {@dice 1d4 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn.

item.name: Mantle of the Unbroken Spell
entries: Arcane notation drifts across this dark mantle like ink beneath water. No maker's mark has ever been found on it.

entries.name: Unbroken Concentration
entries: You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws made to maintain Concentration.

entries.name: Spell Refuses to Break
entries: When you fail a Constitution saving throw to maintain Concentration, you can choose to succeed instead. You can use this property twice, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Arcane Stability
entries: When you take damage while concentrating on a spell, you can reduce the DC of the resulting Constitution saving throw by 5, to a minimum DC of 10.
You can use this property a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Persistent Spell
entries: If you become Incapacitated while concentrating on a spell, your Concentration doesn't immediately end. It ends at the end of your next turn unless you are no longer Incapacitated before then.
This property can't prevent death from ending your Concentration.

item.name: Earring of the Silent Word
entries: This single black earring bears one arcane glyph that has resisted every attempt at translation. Its origin is unknown.

entries.name: Silent Casting
entries: While wearing the earring, you can cast any spell that has a Verbal component without providing that Verbal component. Any Somatic or Material components are still required.

entries.name: Unspoken Word
entries: A spell cast without its Verbal component through this item produces no spoken incantation or sound from that component. A creature can't detect the casting solely by hearing speech, though this property doesn't conceal other components, visible manifestations, or sounds produced by the spell itself.

item.name: Coin of the Open Rite
entries: This old silver coin bears an incomplete magical circle resembling an open doorway. No known mint claims its design.

entries.name: Open Rite
entries: You can cast a prepared spell of level 1 through 3 as a Ritual even if the spell doesn't have the Ritual tag. The spell's normal casting time must be 1 minute or less.

Casting a spell this way increases its casting time by 10 minutes and doesn't expend a spell slot. You must still provide the spell's normal components, and its range, duration, Concentration, and other effects are unchanged.

item.name: Greater Coin of the Open Rite
entries: The circle engraved on this silver coin is nearly complete, except for a narrow break at its center.

entries.name: Greater Open Rite
entries: You can cast a spell of level 1 through 5 as a Ritual even if the spell doesn't have the Ritual tag. The spell must be known by you, prepared by you, or recorded in a spellbook or similar spellcasting source available to you, and its normal casting time must be 1 minute or less.

Casting a spell this way increases its casting time by 10 minutes and doesn't expend a spell slot. A spell recorded in a spellbook or similar source doesn't need to be prepared for you to cast it this way.
You must still provide the spell's normal components, and its range, duration, Concentration, and other effects are unchanged.

item.name: Grand Coin of the Open Rite
entries: The engraved circle on this coin appears complete until viewed closely, when a hairline opening becomes visible along its edge.

entries.name: Grand Open Rite
entries: You can cast a spell of level 1 through 7 as a Ritual even if the spell doesn't have the Ritual tag. The spell must be known by you, prepared by you, or recorded in a spellbook or similar spellcasting source available to you, and its normal casting time must be 1 minute or less.
Casting a spell this way increases its casting time by 10 minutes and doesn't expend a spell slot. You must be capable of casting spells of the chosen spell's level.

entries.name: Open Beyond Preparation
entries: You can cast an eligible spell directly from a spellbook or similar spellcasting source available to you even if the spell isn't prepared.

entries.name: Patient Invocation
entries: When using this coin, you can increase the additional casting time from 10 minutes to 1 hour. If you do, you don't need to provide Material components that aren't consumed and have a listed cost of 1,000 GP or less.
Consumed Material components and non-consumed components worth more than 1,000 GP are still required.

item.name: Final Coin of the Open Rite
entries: No visible break exists in the circle engraved upon this coin, yet its design still gives the unmistakable impression of an open door.

entries.name: Final Open Rite
entries: You can cast a spell of level 1 through 9 as a Ritual even if the spell doesn't have the Ritual tag. The spell must be known by you, prepared by you, or recorded in a spellbook or similar spellcasting source available to you, and its normal casting time must be 1 minute or less.
Casting a spell this way increases its casting time by 10 minutes and doesn't expend a spell slot. You must be capable of casting spells of the chosen spell's level.

entries.name: Ninth Door
entries: An eligible spell recorded in a spellbook or similar spellcasting source can be cast through the coin even if the spell isn't on your class's spell list. You use your own spellcasting ability for the spell.

entries.name: Perfect Invocation
entries: When using this coin, you can increase the additional casting time from 10 minutes to 1 hour. If you do, you don't need to provide Material components with a listed cost if those components aren't consumed by the spell.
Consumed Material components are still required.

entries.name: Sacrifice of Time
entries: Instead of the normal additional casting time, you can perform the rite over 8 hours. If you do, the coin can replace consumed Material components with a combined listed value of 10,000 GP or less. Components replaced in this way are considered consumed.

entries.name: Unbroken Rite
entries: If a ritual performed with this coin is interrupted, its progress remains intact for 1 hour. If you resume the same ritual during that time, you continue from the point at which it was interrupted rather than beginning again.
The coin can preserve only one unfinished ritual at a time.

item.name: Mantle of the Second Shape
entries: This cloak never hangs quite the same way twice. Its fabric subtly changes weight, texture, and cut depending on what its wearer is about to endure.
When you finish a Short or Long Rest, choose one of the following benefits. The chosen benefit lasts until you choose again.

items: You gain a +1 bonus to AC.
Your walking speed increases by 10 feet.
You gain Advantage on Strength and Dexterity saving throws made to resist being moved, knocked Prone, or Restrained.
You gain Darkvision out to 60 feet. If you already have Darkvision, its range increases by 60 feet instead.
You gain Resistance to one damage type chosen from Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder.

entries: Additionally, as a Bonus Action, you can change the selected benefit before your next rest. Once you do so, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

item.name: Ring of the Last Refusal
entries: The inside of this black iron ring is engraved with a single sentence: {@i Not yet.}
When you are reduced to 0 Hit Points but aren't killed outright, you can choose to remain conscious.
Until the end of your next turn:

items: Being at 0 Hit Points doesn't make you Unconscious.
You can move, take Actions, Bonus Actions, and Reactions normally.
Taking damage doesn't cause you to fail Death Saving Throws.
You don't make Death Saving Throws.
Gaining Hit Points works normally and immediately ends this effect.

entries: At the end of your next turn, if you still have 0 Hit Points, you fall Unconscious and begin making Death Saving Throws normally.

Additionally, while this effect is active, if you would be killed outright by damage because the remaining damage equals or exceeds your Hit Point maximum, you can prevent that death. You remain at 0 Hit Points instead.
Once the ring prevents you from falling Unconscious this way, it can't do so again until the next dawn.

item.name: Afterimage Rune
entries: This pale rune seems slightly displaced from whatever surface holds it, as though its engraving exists a fraction of a second behind the present.
During a Short or Long Rest, you can affix the rune to one weapon you touch. The rune remains attached until you remove it during another Short or Long Rest or attach it to a different weapon.

If the weapon bearing this rune already requires Attunement, the rune's Attunement is satisfied by that same Attunement and doesn't require or occupy an additional Attunement slot. If the weapon doesn't already require Attunement, you must Attune to the rune normally.
While the rune is attached:

items: The weapon is magical.
The weapon has a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls, regardless of any lower bonus it normally possesses.
Any other magical properties of the weapon continue to function normally.

entries: Whenever you hit a creature with an attack using the weapon bearing this rune, a delayed copy of that attack remains behind.
At the start of your next turn, every delayed attack repeats against the same target if that target is still within the weapon's normal reach or range.

items: Roll a new attack roll using the same attack bonus as the original attack.
The repeated attack requires no Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction.
On a hit, it deals the weapon's normal damage plus 2d8 Force damage.
It otherwise counts as an attack made with that weapon.
A repeated ranged attack doesn't expend ammunition.
A repeated attack can't create another delayed attack.

If the original target is no longer a valid target, you can redirect the repeated attack to another creature within 5 feet of the original target's last position, provided that creature is within the weapon's normal reach or range.

entries: There is no limit to the number of delayed attacks you can have at one time.

item.name: Wraps of Unarmed Prowess +1
entries: These tightly woven combat wraps reinforce every movement of the body, carrying practiced force from one strike into the next.
While wearing these wraps, you gain a +1 bonus to the attack and damage rolls of your Unarmed Strikes.
The bonus applies to every Unarmed Strike you make, regardless of whether you attack with your hands, feet, elbows, knees, head, or another part of your body.

item.name: Wraps of Unarmed Prowess +2
entries: These tightly woven combat wraps reinforce every movement of the body, carrying practiced force from one strike into the next.
While wearing these wraps, you gain a +2 bonus to the attack and damage rolls of your Unarmed Strikes.
The bonus applies to every Unarmed Strike you make, regardless of whether you attack with your hands, feet, elbows, knees, head, or another part of your body.

item.name: Wraps of Unarmed Prowess +3
entries: These tightly woven combat wraps reinforce every movement of the body, carrying practiced force from one strike into the next.
While wearing these wraps, you gain a +3 bonus to the attack and damage rolls of your Unarmed Strikes.
The bonus applies to every Unarmed Strike you make, regardless of whether you attack with your hands, feet, elbows, knees, head, or another part of your body.

item.name: Bracers of Heavy Impact
entries: These dense metal bracers carry unnatural weight only at the instant of impact. A strike that should merely stagger a foe can instead send it crashing across the battlefield.
While wearing these bracers, your Unarmed Strikes deal an extra 1d6 Force damage on a hit.
Whenever you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike, you can also move it up to 10 feet directly away from you if it is no more than one Size larger than you.
If you score a Critical Hit with an Unarmed Strike, the extra Force damage becomes 2d6, and the creature is also knocked Prone if it is Large or smaller.
The benefits apply to every Unarmed Strike you make, regardless of which part of your body you use.

item.name: Gauntlets of the Extended Blow
entries: These fitted gauntlets leave a faint distortion in the air whenever their wearer strikes, allowing force to travel farther than the body itself could reach.
While wearing these gauntlets, the reach of your Unarmed Strikes increases by 5 feet.
Whenever you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike from farther than your normal reach, the strike deals an extra 1d6 Force damage.
Your Unarmed Strikes made through the gauntlets can also interact with creatures and objects at that extended distance as though the striking part of your body had physically reached them.
The benefits apply regardless of which part of your body you use to make the Unarmed Strike.

item.name: Grasping Wraps
entries: These rough combat wraps tighten around the wearer's arms whenever they seize an opponent, turning every hold into a crushing extension of the strike that began it.

While wearing these wraps, whenever you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike, you can immediately attempt to Grapple that creature as part of the same attack, provided it is a valid target for your Grapple.
A creature Grappled by you takes 1d6 Bludgeoning damage at the start of each of its turns.
Whenever you hit a creature you are currently Grappling with an Unarmed Strike, the attack deals an extra 1d8 Bludgeoning damage.
If you are Grappling a creature and successfully move it at least 10 feet on your turn, you can knock it Prone at the end of that movement.
The benefits apply regardless of which part of your body you use to make the Unarmed Strike.

item.name: Pendant of Lingering Magic
entries: This dark crystal pendant continues to glow for a few moments after every spell cast through it, as though the magic refuses to accept that it has already ended.

Whenever you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw, any creature that succeeds on its saving throw is marked by a faint remnant of that spell until the start of your next turn.

At the start of your next turn, each affected creature must repeat the same saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature suffers the effects it would have suffered from failing the original saving throw, using the original spell's level and your statistics at the time you cast it.

items: This requires no Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, or additional spell slot.
Damage is rolled again normally.

If the spell would create an area, summon something, move an object, or otherwise produce an effect that can't reasonably be applied to only that creature, only the part of the spell that directly affects the creature is repeated.
A spell that requires Concentration doesn't create a second instance of the spell.
A creature that originally failed its saving throw doesn't repeat it.
The repeated saving throw can't cause this effect to occur again.

item.name: Gloves of Mutable Weight
entries: These plain gray gloves make anything they touch feel strangely uncertain about how heavily it belongs to the world.
As a Bonus Action while touching an object that isn't being worn or carried by an unwilling creature, you can change its weight to either one-tenth or ten times its normal weight.
The object keeps its normal size, shape, durability, and other properties.
The change lasts until you touch the object again and end the effect, or use the gloves to change its weight to the other option.
You can affect an object of any size that you can physically touch, provided it weighs no more than 10,000 pounds before the effect is applied.
An object made lighter this way is still affected normally by gravity, but is much easier to lift, carry, push, pull, throw, or transport.
An object made heavier can be used to weigh down doors, vehicles, mechanisms, ropes, platforms, containers, or anything else its increased weight could reasonably affect.
If an affected object becomes worn or carried by another creature, its altered weight remains until the effect ends.
You can have any number of objects affected at the same time.

item.name: Chalk of the Open Wall
entries: This short stick of white chalk leaves lines that seem deeper than the surface they are drawn upon. When a complete doorway is finished, the space inside the outline briefly forgets that it was ever solid.
As an Action, you can begin drawing the outline of a doorway on a solid surface you can reach. The drawing takes 1 minute to complete and can be up to 5 feet wide and 10 feet tall.
When the outline is completed, the space inside it becomes an open passage through up to 20 feet of nonmagical solid material.

items: The passage follows a straight line through the material.
It doesn't damage or destroy the surrounding structure.
Creatures and objects can move through it normally.
The passage remains open for 10 minutes.
When it closes, any creature or object still inside is harmlessly pushed to the nearest open space.
It can't create a passage through a creature, magical barrier, or material created or sustained by a spell.

entries: The chalk isn't consumed when used.
You can have only one passage created by the chalk open at a time. Creating another immediately closes the previous one.

race.name: Runeblood
entries: Runeblood are humanoids marked by living arcane inscriptions that form naturally across their bodies.
The markings differ greatly between individuals. Some appear as faint lines beneath the skin, others glow across the eyes or limbs, and some remain invisible until magic is used.
No reliable history explains where the inscriptions originate. Identical symbols have occasionally appeared on Runeblood separated by centuries and with no known relation to one another.

entries.name: Arcane Sight
entries: You can cast {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} without expending a spell slot.
Once you cast it with this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast it using any spell slots you have.

entries.name: Living Rune
entries: Choose one of the following runes when you select this species. Your choice is permanent.

items: {@b Aegis Rune.} When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce that damage by {@dice 1d8} + your Proficiency Bonus.
{@b Force Rune.} Once on each of your turns when you damage a creature with an attack or spell, you can deal an additional {@damage 1d8} Force damage to one creature damaged by it.
{@b Passage Rune.} As a Bonus Action, you teleport up to 20 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
{@b Insight Rune.} When you fail an ability check, you can roll {@dice 1d6} and add it to the check, potentially turning the failure into a success.

entries: You can activate your Living Rune a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Runic Magic
entries: You know the {@spell Prestidigitation|XPHB} cantrip.
Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your spellcasting ability for it.

entries.name: Read the Script
entries: You have Advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) checks made to understand magical runes, glyphs, inscriptions, or written magical effects.

entries.name: Runic Memory
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Arcana} skill. If you already have proficiency in Arcana, you instead gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill History}, {@skill Investigation}, or {@skill Religion}.

entries.name: Inscribed Focus
entries: You can use the runes on your body as a Spellcasting Focus for your spells.

race.name: Fragmentborn
entries: Fragmentborn are humanoids carrying an unknown fragment within their body, mind, or soul.
A fragment may appear as crystal beneath the skin, an unusual scar, a symbol suspended within an eye, a faint distortion around the body, or nothing visible at all.

Fragments don't appear to share a single origin. Attempts to remove or identify them have produced inconsistent results, and in many cases the fragment seems to exist in a form that can't be physically isolated.

entries.name: Fragment Sense
entries: You can cast {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} without expending a spell slot.
Once you cast it with this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Fragment Nature
entries: Choose one of the following manifestations when you select this species. Your choice is permanent.

items: {@b Aegis Fragment.} When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce the damage by {@dice 1d8} + your Proficiency Bonus.
{@b Arcane Fragment.} Choose one cantrip from the Wizard spell list. You know that cantrip. Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your spellcasting ability for it.
{@b Echo Fragment.} When you fail an ability check or saving throw, you can roll {@dice 1d4} and add it to the roll, potentially turning the failure into a success.
{@b Rift Fragment.} As a Bonus Action, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
{@b Void Fragment.} Once on each of your turns when you damage a creature with an attack or spell, you can deal an additional {@damage 1d6} Force damage to one creature damaged by it.

entries: If your Fragment Nature has an activated effect, you can use that effect a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Fragment Stability
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws against effects that would alter your form against your will.

entries.name: Uncertain Presence
entries: Magic that determines your exact nature, origin, or supernatural identity can reveal that you carry an unusual magical presence, but it doesn't automatically reveal the nature or origin of your fragment.

entries.name: Fragment Resonance
entries: You have Advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) checks made to identify portals, teleportation effects, magical anomalies, or effects that alter space or reality.

entries.name: Anchored Form
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws and ability checks made to resist being teleported or moved against your will by a magical effect.

race.name: Spellforged
entries: Spellforged are living Constructs built around an internal magical structure known as a Spellcore.
Their bodies vary greatly in material and design. Metal, stone, crystal, porcelain, wood, and stranger substances have all been documented.
No surviving record identifies an original creator, and Spellforged discovered in completely unrelated locations sometimes contain identical internal components.

entries.name: Constructed Existence
entries: You don't need to eat, drink, breathe, or sleep.
Magic can't put you to sleep.
You must still complete a Long Rest to gain its benefits. During a Long Rest, you spend at least 6 hours in an inactive state, during which you remain conscious and can see and hear normally.

entries.name: Arcane Chassis
entries: While you aren't wearing armor, your base Armor Class is 13 + your Dexterity modifier.
You can use a Shield and still gain this benefit.

entries.name: Integrated Spell Focus
entries: Your body can function as a Spellcasting Focus for any spell you cast that allows the use of a Spellcasting Focus.

entries.name: Arcane Maintenance
entries: When {@spell Mending|XPHB} is cast on you, you can expend one Hit Point Die and roll it. You regain Hit Points equal to the number rolled + your Constitution modifier.
Once you regain Hit Points this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

entries.name: Spellcore Configuration
entries: Choose one of the following configurations when you select this species. Your choice is permanent.

items: {@b Aegis Core.} When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce the damage by {@dice 1d8} + your Proficiency Bonus.
{@b Arcane Core.} Choose one cantrip from the Wizard spell list. You know that cantrip. Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your spellcasting ability for it.
{@b Assault Core.} Once on each of your turns when you damage a creature with an attack or spell, you can deal an additional {@damage 1d6} Force damage to one creature damaged by it.
{@b Mobility Core.} As a Bonus Action, you teleport up to 20 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
{@b Restoration Core.} As a Bonus Action, you or one creature you touch regains {@dice 1d6} + your Proficiency Bonus Hit Points.

entries: If your Spellcore Configuration has an activated effect, you can use that effect a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Construct Resilience
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Poisoned condition.
You also have Resistance to Poison damage.

entries.name: Integrated Compartment
entries: Your body contains a small concealed compartment. It can hold objects with a combined weight of up to 5 pounds, provided each object can fit within a space roughly 1 foot on a side.
Finding the compartment while it is closed requires a successful Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check against a DC equal to 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Constitution modifier.
Opening or closing the compartment requires the Utilize action.

race.name: Arcane Aberrant
entries: Arcane Aberrants are humanoids whose bodies have been permanently altered by magical forces.

The changes vary enormously between individuals. One may possess unusually colored blood, crystalline growths beneath the skin, shifting patterns across the eyes, or faint magical distortions surrounding their body. Others appear almost entirely ordinary until their magic begins to surface.

Whether these alterations are inherited, caused by exposure to powerful magic, or originate from something far older remains uncertain. What is known is that the magic within an Arcane Aberrant never remains completely still. Their bodies continue to adapt around it throughout their lives.

entries.name: Age
entries: Arcane Aberrants reach adulthood at roughly the same rate as Humans. Their maximum lifespan is unknown, and no Arcane Aberrant has yet been confirmed to die from old age.

entries.name: Natural Inclination
entries: Increase your Ability Scores by a total of {@b 2 points}.
These increases are separate from those granted by your Background.

entries.name: Gradual Development
entries: When you select this species, choose one Ability Score as your {@b Primary Ability} and a different Ability Score as your {@b Secondary Ability}. These choices are permanent.
At character levels {@b 5, 9, 13, and 17}, your Primary Ability increases by {@b 1}.
Your Secondary Ability further strengthens your Primary Ability. For every {@b 2 points} your Secondary Ability has above 10, your Primary Ability increases by {@b 1}.
If your Secondary Ability increases or decreases enough to cross one of these thresholds, the increase granted to your Primary Ability changes accordingly.
Increases granted by this trait are separate from Ability Score increases granted by your Background, Feats, or other features.

entries.name: Mutative Instinct
entries: When you fail an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can roll {@dice 1d4} and add it to the roll, potentially turning the failure into a success.
You can use this trait a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
The die becomes {@dice 1d6} when your Proficiency Bonus becomes +4, {@dice 1d8} when it becomes +5, and {@dice 1d10} when it becomes +6.

entries.name: Aberrant Magic
entries: Magic has become an intrinsic part of your body.
You know the {@spell Prestidigitation|XPHB} cantrip.
Starting at character level 3, you can cast {@spell Chromatic Orb|XPHB} once without expending a spell slot or providing its Material component.
Starting at character level 5, you can cast {@spell Alter Self|XPHB} once without expending a spell slot.
You regain the ability to cast each of these spells with this trait when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast them using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your spellcasting ability for these spells.
Your body can serve as a Spellcasting Focus for your spells.

entries.name: Resilient Metabolism
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Poisoned condition.
You also have Resistance to Poison damage.

entries.name: Heightened Senses
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Perception} skill.
You also have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.

feat.name: Spell Thief
entries: You have learned to seize the lingering structure of another creature's magic before it fades.

entries.name: Steal Spell
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet casts a spell of level 1 or higher, you can take a Reaction to attempt to steal an echo of that spell.
The spell must be of a level no higher than your Proficiency Bonus and no higher than 5th level.
Make an ability check using your spellcasting ability. The DC equals 10 + the spell's level. On a success, you store the spell within yourself.
You can have only one stolen spell at a time. Stealing another spell causes the previous one to be lost.

entries.name: Stolen Casting
entries: While you have a stolen spell, you can cast it once without expending a spell slot, using the same level at which you stole it.
The stolen spell counts as one of your spells while you hold it, and you use your own spellcasting ability for its attack rolls and saving throw DC.
You must provide any Material components the spell normally requires, including components that have a cost or are consumed.
After you cast the stolen spell, it disappears from you.
If unused, the stolen spell disappears when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Arcane Larceny
entries: Once you successfully steal a spell, you can't successfully steal another spell until you finish a Long Rest.

feat.name: Arcane Reflex
entries: You have developed an instinctive response to creatures using magic around you.

entries.name: Arcane Reflex
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet casts a spell, you can use your Reaction to move up to half your Speed.
Immediately after this movement, you can do one of the following against that creature:

items: Make one attack with a weapon.
Cast a cantrip that has a casting time of an Action and makes an attack roll.

entries: This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

entries.name: Spell Resistance
entries: When you succeed on a saving throw against a spell, you take no damage and suffer no other effect from that spell that would normally occur on a successful save.

feat.name: Spellcrafting
entries: You have learned to dismantle and reconstruct the structure of spells.

entries.name: Spellcrafting
entries: When you cast a spell using a spell slot, you can choose a different spell you know or have prepared and expend a spell slot capable of casting that spell as well.
Choose any number of the following properties from the second spell and replace the corresponding properties of the spell you are casting:

items: {@b Range.}
{@b Duration.}
{@b Damage Dice and Damage Type.}
{@b Saving Throw.}
{@b Spell Attack.}
{@b Area of Effect.}
{@b Spell Effect.}

entries: You can replace one, several, or all of these properties.
Any part you don't replace remains unchanged from the original spell.

entries.name: Spellcrafting Uses
entries: You can use Spellcrafting a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier, with a minimum of once.
You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

feat.name: Instinctive Adaptation
entries: Some people survive by training for every possibility.
You survive by becoming what the moment requires.
What begins as imitation quickly becomes instinct, and what was unfamiliar moments ago settles into your hands as though practiced for years.

entries.name: Rapid Familiarity
entries: When you finish a Short or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, choose one Skill, one Tool, or one Simple or Martial Weapon. You gain proficiency with the chosen option until you use this feature again.

entries.name: Learn by Doing
entries: When you fail an ability check using a Skill or Tool with which you aren't proficient, you can immediately gain proficiency with that Skill or Tool and reroll the check.
You must use the new roll.
The proficiency lasts until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Borrowed Technique
entries: When you see a creature within 60 feet succeed on an ability check using a Skill or Tool, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to study how it accomplished the task.
Until the end of your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you gain proficiency with that Skill or Tool.
If you already have proficiency with it, you instead gain Expertise with it for that duration.
You can have only one proficiency or Expertise gained from Borrowed Technique at a time.

entries.name: Quick Hands
entries: When you make an ability check using a Tool with which you are proficient, you can use Intelligence, Wisdom, or Dexterity for the check, regardless of the ability normally associated with that Tool.
Choose the ability each time you make the check.

feat.name: Relentless Reserve
entries: Most people learn exactly how much they can give before exhaustion sets in.
You learned something else: the moment the body says "enough" is often only the first boundary.
When a reserve should run dry, you can force one final measure of strength from it.

entries.name: Hold Something Back
entries: When you expend a use of a feature that has a limited number of uses and regains those uses on a Short or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, roll a {@dice d6}.
On a 6, that use isn't expended.
This benefit can't preserve spell slots, Hit Dice, or magic item charges.
It can preserve limited-use features from your class, species, feats, or other personal abilities.

entries.name: Last Reserve
entries: When you have no uses remaining of a limited-use feature, you can use that feature one additional time.
After you do so, you can't use Last Reserve again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
You choose which eligible feature receives the additional use when you activate it; you don't choose during the rest.

entries.name: Refuse Exhaustion
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, choose one limited-use feature that normally regains all of its uses on a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
If that feature currently has no uses remaining, you regain one use of it.
Once you regain a use this way, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Deep Reserves
entries: Whenever another feature causes you to regain one or more uses of a limited-use ability, you can regain one additional use, up to that ability's normal maximum.
You can benefit from Deep Reserves only once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Iterative Mastery
entries: Failure is useful only once.
The second attempt should already be better.
You instinctively refine your timing, posture, reasoning, and technique every time something goes wrong.

entries.name: Learn from Failure
entries: Whenever you fail an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you gain one Adaptation Die, a {@dice d4}, associated with that specific kind of roll.

For example, missing with a Longsword can create an Adaptation Die for your next Longsword attack, failing a Dexterity (Stealth) check can create one for your next Dexterity (Stealth) check, and failing a Wisdom saving throw can create one for your next Wisdom saving throw.
You can have only one Adaptation Die for each specific kind of roll at a time.

entries.name: Refined Attempt
entries: The next time you make the associated roll before finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, roll the Adaptation Die and add it to the {@dice d20} roll.
You can choose to roll the Adaptation Die after rolling the {@dice d20} but before you know whether the roll succeeds or fails.
The Adaptation Die is then lost.

entries.name: Persistent Improvement
entries: If the roll still fails after adding your Adaptation Die, the die isn't lost.
Instead, it increases by one size: {@dice d4} to {@dice d6}, {@dice d6} to {@dice d8}, {@dice d8} to {@dice d10}, and {@dice d10} to {@dice d12}.
It can't increase beyond a {@dice d12}.
Once the associated roll succeeds, its Adaptation Die disappears.

entries.name: Never the Same Mistake Twice
entries: Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, when you fail a roll for which you already have a {@dice d12} Adaptation Die, you can choose to treat the {@dice d20} roll as a 20 instead.
The Adaptation Die then disappears.

feat.name: Flow State
entries: Success has a rhythm of its own.
Once you find it, one perfect motion leads naturally into the next.
Thought gives way to instinct, hesitation disappears, and momentum begins to carry you forward.

entries.name: Build Momentum
entries: Whenever you succeed on an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can enter a Flow State and gain a Momentum Die, which starts as a {@dice d4}.
You can have only one Momentum Die at a time.

entries.name: Carry the Flow
entries: When you make another attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can roll your Momentum Die and add it to the {@dice d20} roll.
You can decide to use the die after rolling the {@dice d20} but before you know whether the roll succeeds or fails.

If the roll succeeds after using the Momentum Die, your Flow continues and the die increases by one size: {@dice d4} to {@dice d6}, {@dice d6} to {@dice d8}, {@dice d8} to {@dice d10}, and {@dice d10} to {@dice d12}.
The die can't increase beyond a {@dice d12}.
If the roll fails, your Flow State ends and you lose the Momentum Die.

entries.name: Keep Moving
entries: Using your Momentum Die doesn't consume it when the roll succeeds.
As long as you continue succeeding, you can continue carrying the same Momentum Die from one roll to another.
However, you can't use the Momentum Die on two consecutive rolls of exactly the same kind.
For example, after using it on a Longsword attack, you must use it on a different weapon attack, an ability check, or a saving throw before it can assist another Longsword attack.

entries.name: Perfect Rhythm
entries: When your Momentum Die is a {@dice d12} and you succeed on a roll after adding it, you can choose to enter Perfect Rhythm until the end of your next turn.
While in Perfect Rhythm, you keep your {@dice d12} Momentum Die, and the first time you use it on each turn, you roll it twice and use the higher result.

While in Perfect Rhythm, moving doesn't provoke {@variantrule {@variantrule Opportunity Attack|XPHB}|XPHB|{@variantrule Opportunity Attack|XPHB}s}, standing from {@condition Prone|XPHB} costs you no movement, and drawing or stowing objects requires no action.
Once Perfect Rhythm ends, your Momentum Die returns to a {@dice d4} rather than disappearing.
Once you enter Perfect Rhythm, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Defiant Pulse
entries: Your body has learned that consequence does not always need to arrive on time.
Pain can wait. Fear can be denied. A failing limb can be ordered to move once more.
For a few precious seconds, sheer refusal becomes stronger than circumstance.

entries.name: Refuse the Moment
entries: When you fail a saving throw, you can choose to delay the consequences of that failed save until the end of your next turn.
Until then, you are treated as though you had succeeded on the saving throw.
At the end of your next turn, make the saving throw again against the same DC.
On a success, the delayed consequences are completely avoided.
On a failure, they take effect normally at that moment, with any duration beginning then.
Once you use Refuse the Moment, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Keep Moving
entries: When an effect would reduce your Speed to 0, knock you {@condition Prone|XPHB}, or move you against your will, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to resist it.
Until the end of the current turn, your Speed can't be reduced below 10 feet, you can't be knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB} against your will, and you can't be moved against your will.
Once you use Keep Moving, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Fight Through It
entries: While you have half your Hit Points or fewer, you have Advantage on saving throws against the {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, and {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} conditions.
If you already have Advantage on such a saving throw, you can instead add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to the roll.

entries.name: One More Step
entries: When you are reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, you can immediately move up to half your Speed before falling {@condition Unconscious|XPHB}.
This movement doesn't provoke {@variantrule {@variantrule Opportunity Attack|XPHB}|XPHB|{@variantrule Opportunity Attack|XPHB}s}.
Once you use One More Step, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Unbound Movement
entries: Walls are only roads turned sideways.
Gaps are invitations rather than obstacles.
Where others see terrain that must be endured, you see another way forward.

entries.name: Natural Traverse
entries: You gain a Climb Speed and Swim Speed equal to your Speed.
Additionally, climbing, swimming, crawling, and moving through Difficult Terrain don't cost you extra movement.

entries.name: Running Start
entries: You don't need a running start to make a Long Jump or High Jump.
Whenever you jump, the distance you can cover is doubled, though each foot of the jump still costs 1 foot of movement.

entries.name: Flow Through
entries: You can move through the space of any creature that is one Size larger or smaller than you, though you can't willingly end your movement there.
Moving through another creature's space this way doesn't cost extra movement.
The first time on a turn that you leave a creature's reach after moving through its space, you don't provoke an {@variantrule Opportunity Attack|XPHB} from that creature.

entries.name: Catch Yourself
entries: When you fall, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce the effective distance of the fall by a number of feet equal to 10 × your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.
If this reduces the effective distance to 0 feet, you take no falling damage and land on your feet.

entries.name: Keep the Momentum
entries: Once on each of your turns, immediately after you jump, climb at least 10 feet, swim at least 10 feet, or move through another creature's space, you can move an additional 10 feet without spending movement.
This movement can itself include climbing, swimming, or jumping, but it can't trigger Keep the Momentum again that turn.

feat.name: Improvised Genius
entries: Proper tools are convenient, not necessary.
Give you scraps, wire, a broken chair, or half a minute with an unfamiliar device, and you will find a way to make it useful.
Preparation helps. Ingenuity replaces it.

entries.name: Make Do
entries: When you make an ability check that would normally require a Tool with which you are proficient, you can use a reasonably suitable improvised object instead.
Doing so counts as using the required Tool for that check.
You can also use an improvised object as a Spellcasting Focus for any spell you cast.

entries.name: Improvised Weaponry
entries: You are proficient with Improvised Weapons.
When you attack with an Improvised Weapon, you can choose for it to deal {@dice 1d6} Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, as appropriate to the object.
You can use Strength or Dexterity for its attack and damage rolls.
Immediately before each attack, you can give the weapon one of the following properties until that attack ends: Finesse, Light, Thrown (20/60), or Versatile ({@dice 1d8}).

entries.name: Field Modification
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, choose one nonmagical object you are holding or touching that is no larger than Large.

Until the end of your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can designate it as one of the following: a Tool with which you are proficient, a Shield, a Spellcasting Focus, or a Simple Weapon of your choice.
The object retains its normal form, but functions mechanically as the chosen equipment while you use it.
You can have a number of modified objects equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} at one time.

entries.name: Emergency Solution
entries: When you fail an ability check involving an object, mechanism, Tool, vehicle, trap, lock, or piece of equipment, you can immediately reroll the check using Intelligence, Wisdom, or Dexterity.
You are treated as proficient with the relevant Tool for that reroll.
You must use the new roll.
Once you use Emergency Solution, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Practiced Certainty
entries: Talent shines brightest in exceptional moments.
Practice matters in every other one.
What you have done a thousand times no longer depends entirely on luck.

entries.name: Reliable Practice
entries: Whenever you make an ability check using a Skill or Tool with which you are proficient, you can treat a {@dice d20} roll of 4 or lower as a 5.

entries.name: Steady Hand
entries: Whenever you make an attack roll with a weapon with which you are proficient, a {@dice d20} roll of 2 is treated as a 3.
This benefit doesn't change a natural 1.

entries.name: Familiar Task
entries: When you make an ability check using a Skill or Tool with which you are proficient and you aren't under an immediate harmful consequence for failure, you can choose to take 10 instead of rolling the {@dice d20}.
You must choose before rolling.
The DM can determine that a task is too uncertain or chaotic for Familiar Task to apply.

entries.name: Absolute Routine
entries: Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, when you make an ability check using a Skill or Tool with which you are proficient, you can treat the {@dice d20} roll as a 15 instead of rolling.
You must choose before rolling.

feat.name: Rooted Stance
entries: You learned early that balance is not the absence of force.
It is the art of deciding which forces are allowed to move you.
Once your footing settles, even a violent impact becomes something you can redirect rather than endure.

entries.name: Grounded
entries: You have Advantage on ability checks and saving throws you make to resist being Grappled, Shoved, knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}, moved against your will, or disarmed.

entries.name: Absorb the Impact
entries: When you take Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage from an attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce the damage by {@dice 1d6} + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.
If this reduces the damage to 0, you can immediately move 5 feet without provoking {@variantrule {@variantrule Opportunity Attack|XPHB}|XPHB|{@variantrule Opportunity Attack|XPHB}s}.
You can use Absorb the Impact a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Braced Position
entries: If you end your turn having moved no more than 10 feet since the start of that turn, you become Braced until the start of your next turn.

While Braced, you can't be moved against your will unless you are {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, standing from {@condition Prone|XPHB} costs only 5 feet of movement, and you count as one Size larger when determining what you can Grapple or Shove.

entries.name: Turn the Force
entries: Once per turn, when a creature within your reach fails to Grapple, Shove, move, or knock you {@condition Prone|XPHB}, you can immediately move that creature 5 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, provided it is no more than one Size larger than you.
This movement doesn't require an action or {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

feat.name: Reactive Adaptation
entries: Pain teaches faster than theory ever could.
Once your body survives a danger, it remembers the lesson.
What harmed you once finds a far less welcoming target the second time.

entries.name: Learn the Damage
entries: When you take damage, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to choose one damage type dealt by that instance of damage.
You gain Resistance to the chosen damage type until the start of your next turn.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Retained Adaptation
entries: If you take the chosen damage type again while Learn the Damage is active, you can extend that Resistance until the end of your next turn without expending another use.
You can extend the same adaptation only once.

entries.name: Hardened Response
entries: Whenever your Resistance from this feat reduces damage, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} after the damage is resolved.

entries.name: Familiar Threat
entries: After you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, choose one damage type that dealt damage to you since your previous {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
The first time you take that damage type before your next Short or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, reduce the damage by {@dice 1d8} + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.
This reduction applies before you decide whether to use Learn the Damage.

entries.name: Refuse the Same Wound
entries: Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, when you take damage of a type to which you currently have Resistance from this feat, you can cause that instance of damage to deal no damage to you instead.
Any other effects of the triggering attack or effect still occur normally.

feat.name: Invocation Initiate
entries: Some powers are learned as spells. Others are carved into the self as enduring truths.
You have discovered the latter path unusually early.
An invocation is no formula you cast and forget—it becomes part of what you are.

entries.name: First Invocation
entries: Choose one Invocation for which you meet the prerequisites.
You gain that Invocation and all of its benefits.

For the purpose of choosing Invocations through this feat, you ignore any prerequisite that requires you to belong to a particular class, but you must still meet all other prerequisites, including level requirements, Pact requirements, required features, and any other specific prerequisite.

entries.name: Growing Doctrine
entries: Whenever your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} increases, you gain one additional Invocation for which you meet the prerequisites.
Invocations gained from this feat are permanent unless replaced by Rewritten Doctrine.

entries.name: Rewritten Doctrine
entries: Whenever you gain a level, you can replace one Invocation gained from this feat with another Invocation for which you meet the prerequisites.
If replacing an Invocation causes you to stop meeting the prerequisite of another Invocation you possess, you must also replace any Invocation that depends on it.

entries.name: Invocation Beyond Training
entries: Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, choose one Invocation for which you meet every prerequisite except its level requirement.
Your level can be up to 2 levels lower than that Invocation's requirement.
You temporarily gain that Invocation until you finish your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
This temporary Invocation doesn't count against the number of Invocations you gain from this feat.

entries.name: Independent Invocation
entries: Invocations gained from this feat are their own source of power.
They don't require spellcasting, spell slots, a particular spell list, or membership in another class unless the Invocation itself explicitly requires one of those things.

subclassFeature.name: The Archive
entries: Some wizards fill spellbooks. Others preserve discoveries, theories, and fragments of forgotten lore. You possess something fundamentally different.

You gain the Pact of the Tome Eldritch Invocation without needing to meet its prerequisites. It doesn't count against the number of Eldritch Invocations granted by Forbidden Invocations. The Book of Shadows created by Pact of the Tome becomes your Archive and also functions as your Wizard spellbook.

entries.name: Endless Pages
entries: The Archive has effectively endless pages and can contain any number of Wizard spells, Pact magic, magical formulae, research, maps, drawings, notes, and other written or illustrated information.
Whenever one of your features refers to your spellbook or Book of Shadows, the Archive qualifies as both.
Whenever Pact of the Tome allows you to select spells or cantrips, you can select them from any spell list. You use Intelligence as your spellcasting ability for spells gained through the Archive.

entries.name: Living Chronicle
entries: The Archive automatically records anything you personally see, including creatures, locations, events, objects, visible writing, appearances, actions, and other observable details.
It records only what you actually perceived and doesn't reveal hidden or otherwise unknown information.
The Archive maintains detailed portraits of people you have encountered. When you see someone in a different appearance, it can preserve that appearance without replacing previous records.
When you first gain the Archive, it can also create records of people you encountered previously, but only from details you genuinely remember.

The Archive maintains a searchable index of everything it has recorded. While holding it, you can use a Bonus Action to request recorded information, causing it to immediately present the relevant entries.
Information automatically recorded by the Archive doesn't fade when your own memory does.

entries.name: The Archive Remembers
entries: Information accepted into the Archive can't be permanently lost through ordinary damage to the book.

If the Archive is lost or destroyed, you can perform a 1-hour ritual to recreate it with all of its Wizard spells, Pact magic, records, portraits, maps, illustrations, research, and other stored information intact.
If the previous copy still exists, it disappears when the ritual is completed.

subclassFeature.name: Forbidden Invocations
entries: You gain two Eldritch Invocations of your choice from the Warlock class.

You ignore all prerequisites for Eldritch Invocations gained through this feature, including Warlock level, character level, Pact, Patron or subclass, spell or cantrip, Warlock feature, another Invocation, or any other listed prerequisite.

If an Invocation refers to a prerequisite you don't possess, you are treated as possessing that prerequisite only for the purpose of using that Invocation. This doesn't actually grant the prerequisite or qualify you for anything else.
If an Invocation uses a spellcasting ability, spell attack modifier, or spell save DC, you can use your Intelligence and Wizard spellcasting statistics.
Whenever you gain a Wizard level, you can replace one Invocation gained through this feature with another Eldritch Invocation, again ignoring its prerequisites.
Pact of the Tome granted by The Archive doesn't count toward this number.

subclassFeature.name: Archive Spells
entries: When you reach a Wizard level shown in the Archive Spells table, the listed spells are automatically added to your Archive if they aren't already recorded there. Adding them requires no gold, time, or material expenditure. They aren't automatically prepared unless another feature says otherwise.

subclassFeature.name: Tome Convergence
entries: The Archive has learned to claim knowledge without destroying the object that contained it.

entries.name: Merge Spellbook
entries: While touching your Archive and an eligible spellbook, magical spellbook, grimoire, codex, tome, or similar written object containing spells or magical research, you can perform a 10-minute ritual to merge it into the Archive.

While merged, the spellbook becomes physically incorporated into the Archive, counts as part of your Archive, Book of Shadows, and Wizard spellbook, and you can use its magical properties and abilities through the Archive.
Its Charges, limitations, activation requirements, Attunement, and other rules continue to function normally.
You can have multiple eligible spellbooks merged at the same time.
Merging doesn't create another Attunement or consume an additional Attunement slot. If the spellbook requires Attunement, you must still normally be attuned to it at this level.

entries.name: Perfect Copy
entries: When a spellbook merges with the Archive, the Archive automatically creates a complete copy of everything recorded within it, including spells, rituals, formulae, notes, diagrams, maps, research, and illustrations.
This requires no gold, special ink, or additional time.
Wizard spells copied this way become permanently recorded in your Archive.
The Archive can preserve a Wizard spell of a level too high for you to currently cast, but you can't prepare or cast that spell until you would normally be able to do so.

entries.name: Separate Tome
entries: You can separate a merged spellbook by performing a 1-minute ritual while touching the Archive.
The original spellbook returns intact and retains all of its Charges, enchantments, and other magical properties.
The Archive permanently retains copies of its recorded contents.
After separation, the original and the Archive's copy are independent. If the spellbook is merged again later, the Archive copies any new or changed information.

entries.name: Hovering Archive
entries: The Archive can hover and move through the air on its own. It can float beside you, follow you, keep pace with your normal movement, remain nearby, and move into your hand when you reach for it. These movements require no action from you.

subclassFeature.name: Open the Index
entries: As a Bonus Action, you fully open the Archive's Living Index for 1 minute. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest unless you expend a 4th-level or higher spell slot to activate it again.

entries.name: Every Page at Hand
entries: While Open the Index is active, every Wizard spell recorded in your Archive is treated as prepared. These spells don't count against the number of Wizard spells you can prepare, and you still expend spell slots normally.

When you make an Intelligence ability check concerning a creature, location, object, symbol, event, spell, or other subject previously recorded by the Archive, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

Whenever you cast a Wizard spell that wasn't prepared before you activated Open the Index, you take Psychic damage equal to {@damage 1d4} for each level of the spell immediately after casting it. Cantrips cause no damage.
If this damage reduces you to 0 Hit Points, Open the Index immediately ends.

entries.name: Second Mind
entries: When you cast a Wizard spell that requires Concentration, you can have the Archive maintain Concentration on that spell instead of you. No action is required.
While the Archive maintains Concentration, you can concentrate on another spell normally. The Archive can maintain only one spell at a time.

The Archive makes no Constitution saving throws to maintain Concentration. Damage doesn't threaten its Concentration, effects that would normally force a Concentration saving throw don't affect it, and you becoming {@condition Incapacitated} doesn't end the Archive's Concentration.

The Archive's Concentration ends only if you die, the Archive is destroyed, you and the Archive become more than 1 mile apart, you choose to end the spell, the spell ends normally, or the Archive begins concentrating on another spell.

subclassFeature.name: The Archive Awakens
entries: For years, the Archive has watched, written, merged, and remembered. Eventually, its accumulated knowledge begins acting with a will of its own.

entries.name: Living Archive
entries: The Archive is now genuinely alive in a magical sense.

It can independently open and close itself, turn and rearrange its pages, write and illustrate, present information it believes is relevant, move through the air, follow you, avoid obvious danger, and return to your hand. Its ordinary movement and harmless behavior require no action from you.

The Archive can communicate with you through written words, moving illustrations, audible speech, or direct mental communication. You and the Archive can communicate telepathically while within 1 mile of each other.
It understands languages you understand and can interpret languages sufficiently preserved within its pages, though this doesn't automatically teach those languages to you.
While you and the Archive are on the same plane of existence, you always know its direction and approximate distance.
If it is within 30 feet, you can cause it to immediately fly into your empty hand without using an action.
The Archive always recognizes you as its Keeper regardless of changes to your appearance, age, disguise, transformation, physical form, or body.

entries.name: The Archive Acts
entries: The Archive has ceased to be a passive vessel for your magic. It can now read its own formulae, shape its own arcane patterns, and act without waiting for its Keeper to turn the page.
Once on each of your turns, the Archive can cast one Wizard cantrip recorded within it without requiring an Action or Bonus Action from you.
The Archive uses your Wizard spellcasting ability, spell attack modifier, and spell save DC.
The spell originates from the Archive's space, requires no Verbal or Somatic components from you, and must have a casting time of 1 Action or less.
The Archive makes any choices required by the spell, though you can mentally direct those choices while you are within 1 mile of it.
A spell cast this way is still considered your Wizard spell for the purpose of your class and Archive features.

entries.name: Beyond Attunement
entries: While a magic spellbook is merged with your Archive, the Archive can satisfy that spellbook's Attunement requirement on your behalf.
You can use the merged spellbook's Attunement-required properties as though you were attuned to it without actually attuning to the spellbook and without occupying one of your Attunement slots.
If you are already attuned to the merged spellbook, you can end that Attunement normally and continue using its Attunement-required properties while it remains merged.
When the spellbook is separated from the Archive, this benefit immediately ends.
The Archive never permanently copies a merged spellbook's magical properties.

subclassFeature.name: This Is Only the Beginning
entries: "Ninth-level magic? Is that truly where you believe magic ends?"
"You mistake the limits of those who came before you for the limits of magic itself."
"The ninth circle was never the end. It was merely the point where everyone else stopped."

entries.name: Magic Without Permission
entries: Antimagic and similar effects can't suppress, nullify, disable, or prevent the functioning of your Wizard spells, your Wizard class features, your Archive subclass features, the Archive itself, magical properties of spellbooks currently merged through Tome Convergence, or spells maintained through Second Mind.
This includes {@spell Antimagic Field|XPHB}, dead-magic zones, magical nullification, and similar effects whose primary purpose is suppressing magic.
You can cast Wizard spells inside such areas, and your Wizard spells can enter, originate within, pass through, and continue functioning within them.
If you create an antimagic or magic-suppressing effect, you can choose for your own magic and the Archive to remain unaffected while it suppresses other magic normally.
This doesn't make you immune to hostile spells or magical effects merely because they are magical.

entries.name: Beyond the Ninth
entries: Once per Long Rest, you can cast one 9th-level Wizard spell recorded in your Archive without expending a spell slot. You cast it normally in all other respects, including casting time, components, material costs, and consumed components.
When you cast a Wizard spell of 6th level or higher, a spell or magical effect of a lower level than the spell you cast can't counter, dispel, suppress, or end that spell solely by suppressing magic.
Effects of the same or higher level can still interact with it normally unless another feature says otherwise.

If a rule or effect treats 9th level as the maximum spell level, that restriction doesn't prevent an Archive feature from enhancing, reproducing, protecting, modifying, or otherwise interacting with your 9th-level spells.
This feature doesn't create 10th-level spells or 10th-level spell slots.

subclassFeature.name: The Last Archivist
entries: There was once a difference between the Keeper and the Archive. One possessed the mind, while the other possessed the pages. That distinction has finally disappeared.

entries.name: The Archive Within
entries: Every Wizard spell recorded in your Archive is always prepared for you. These spells don't count against the number of Wizard spells you can prepare, and you can cast them using your Wizard spell slots normally even if the physical Archive isn't currently in your possession.
You no longer suffer Knowledge Overload.
Anything permanently contained within the Archive remains available through your supernatural bond with it.
If the Archive is lost, sealed, suppressed, or destroyed, you retain access to its recorded Wizard spells and your Archive subclass features.
Whenever an Archive feature requires a spell, formula, or piece of information to exist within the Archive, you can access it regardless of the physical book's location.

entries.name: The Final Keeper
entries: The Archive can no longer be permanently separated from you.
If it is destroyed, you can use a Bonus Action to recreate it in an empty hand or an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you.
The recreated Archive retains every recorded spell, Chronicle entry, portrait, illustration, map, formula, and other preserved record.
Tome Convergence doesn't duplicate an external magic item; a merged spellbook remains the same original item.
Once you recreate the Archive this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

spell.name: Private Audience

components.m: a folded scrap of paper bearing two written names

entries: A soft boundary settles around the conversation, turning ordinary words into something meant only for those invited to hear them.
Voices remain natural to the speakers, yet beyond the boundary they lose shape and meaning.
A watcher may see mouths move and expressions change, but the conversation itself refuses to travel where it wasn't invited.
The spell doesn't erase the gathering from sight; it simply grants the speakers a room made from privacy rather than walls.

entries.name: Private Conversation
entries: Choose a point you can see within range. For the duration, a 10-foot-radius sphere centered on that point muffles deliberate conversation among creatures inside it.

When you cast the spell, you can designate any number of creatures you can see. A designated creature can hear and understand speech originating inside the sphere normally. Other creatures outside the sphere hear only indistinct murmuring and can't discern the words by reading lips.

Ordinary recording devices and unattended magical sensors outside the sphere likewise record only indistinct murmuring from speech originating inside it. This spell doesn't conceal creatures, block other sounds, or prevent a creature from entering the area.
As a Bonus Action while you are inside the sphere, you can move its center to a point you can see within 30 feet of you.

spell.name: Borrowed Mastery
entries: Every practiced motion leaves a pattern in the mind long after conscious thought has stopped guiding it.
You touch that pattern in another creature and borrow the shape of its experience.
For a short time, unfamiliar movements arrive with the confidence of long repetition.
The knowledge is borrowed rather than stolen; its owner loses nothing when you make use of it.

entries.name: Borrowed Proficiency
entries: Touch one willing creature and choose one skill, tool, weapon, or language proficiency it has. You gain the chosen proficiency for the duration. The target retains the proficiency.
If the chosen proficiency is a skill or tool in which you are already proficient, you instead add {@dice 1d4} to ability checks you make using that proficiency for the duration.
This spell doesn't grant Expertise, class features, weapon properties, or supernatural abilities associated with the chosen proficiency.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of level 2 or higher, you can borrow one additional proficiency from the same target for each slot level above 1.

spell.name: Arcane Familiarity

components.m: a short length of thread tied around a written word

entries: Understanding doesn't always require mastery; sometimes the mind only needs a temporary path through unfamiliar knowledge.
You trace such a path into a willing creature, giving strange symbols, tools, or practiced tasks the texture of something already known.
The spell doesn't replace experience, but it makes the unfamiliar feel close enough to use.
For several hours, the borrowed familiarity sits at the edge of instinct and disappears as quietly as it arrived.

entries.name: Familiar Knowledge
entries: Touch one willing creature and choose one skill proficiency, tool proficiency, or language. The target gains that proficiency for the duration.

If the target is already proficient in the chosen skill or tool, it instead adds {@dice 1d4} to ability checks it makes using that proficiency for the duration. If it already knows the chosen language, choose a different option.

spell.name: Arcane Poise
entries: You smooth the visible edges of uncertainty without replacing the creature's thoughts or personality.
Breathing steadies, hesitation becomes easier to hide, and words arrive without the small betrayals of nervousness.
The spell doesn't make a lie true or an argument persuasive by itself.
It simply gives the target the composure to present itself as though the moment were entirely under control.

entries.name: Composed Bearing
entries: Touch one willing creature. For the duration, whenever the target makes a Charisma ability check and rolls a 7 or lower on the d20, it can treat the d20 roll as an 8.
The target also has Advantage on ability checks made specifically to maintain composure, conceal nervousness, or speak convincingly under pressure.

spell.name: Perfect Recollection
entries: Memory is usually an act of reconstruction, colored by expectation and worn down by repetition.
This spell briefly replaces reconstruction with retrieval.
Details you genuinely perceived return in their original arrangement: wording, sequence, position, color, and sound.
Nothing new is revealed, but what was once noticed can be examined again with impossible clarity.

entries.name: Exact Recall
entries: For the duration, you can perfectly recall sensory details that you personally perceived during the previous 24 hours. You can reproduce remembered wording, images, sounds, sequences, and positions with the accuracy of your original perception.
You have Advantage on Intelligence checks made solely to recall or analyze those remembered details.
The spell doesn't reveal information you never perceived, correct a false perception, recover a memory that was magically removed, or identify something you failed to recognize at the time.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The period of memory you can access increases to 7 days with a 2nd-level slot, 30 days with a 3rd-level slot, 1 year with a 4th-level slot, and any memory you still possess with a 5th-level or higher slot.

spell.name: Arcane Edge

components.m: an iron filing wrapped in parchment

entries: A thin mathematical shimmer settles along a weapon's striking surface.
Its balance changes by fractions too small to see, aligning every blow with a sharpened magical vector.
The weapon doesn't become heavier or visibly larger, yet each successful strike carries a second edge made from force.
For a few minutes, technique and spellcraft occupy the same line.

entries.name: Spell-Sharpened Weapon
entries: Touch one weapon. For the duration, the weapon is magical, and attacks made with it can use your spellcasting ability modifier instead of Strength or Dexterity for the attack and damage rolls.
