On a hit, the weapon deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Force damage.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The extra Force damage increases by {@damage 1d6} for each slot level above 1.

spell.name: Mystic Aegis

time.condition: which you take when you or a creature you can see within 30 feet is hit by an attack or fails a saving throw

entries: A defense need not be a wall; sometimes the smallest correction is enough to turn catastrophe aside.
You cast a brief lattice of force around a creature at the instant danger finds it.
The lattice tightens around the threat already in motion, then remains as a faint protective geometry for a few heartbeats.
Its purpose is not to make the target untouchable, but to give it one more chance to endure.

entries.name: Reactive Aegis
entries: Choose the triggering creature. If the trigger was an attack, the target gains a +3 bonus to AC against that attack, potentially causing it to miss. If the trigger was a failed saving throw, the target adds {@dice 1d4} to that saving throw, potentially turning it into a success.
Until the start of the target's next turn, it also gains a +1 bonus to AC and saving throws.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When cast with a slot of level 2 or higher, the lingering bonus to AC and saving throws increases by 1 for every two slot levels above 1, to a maximum of +4.

spell.name: Vortex
entries: You pinch space into a brief rotational collapse around a creature.
Dust, loose cloth, and nearby debris twist inward before the distortion snaps shut.
The pull is violent but fleeting, dragging the target toward the center of the impossible spiral.
What remains afterward is only displaced air and the memory of motion.

entries.name: Collapsing Spiral
entries: Choose one creature you can see within range. It must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 2d10} Force damage and is pulled up to 15 feet toward a point you choose within 5 feet of it. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn't pulled.
A creature can choose to fail the saving throw.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@damage 1d10} for each slot level above 1.

spell.name: Shared Concentration
entries: Concentration is usually a private burden, a single mind holding a spell's structure against interruption.
You expose that structure for a heartbeat and place it into another willing mind.
The spell itself doesn't change hands; only the responsibility for keeping it intact does.
Once the transfer is complete, your thoughts are free while another creature carries the unbroken formula.

entries.name: Transfer Concentration
entries: Choose one willing creature you can see within range. If you are concentrating on a spell, you can transfer Concentration on that spell to the target.

The spell retains its original spellcasting ability, spell save DC, spell attack modifier, targets, choices, remaining duration, and all other statistics. The target doesn't need to know or be able to cast the spell.

The target now follows the normal rules for maintaining Concentration on that spell, and your Concentration on it ends without ending the spell. You can immediately concentrate on another spell normally.

spell.name: Arcane Reversal

time.condition: which you take when you succeed on a saving throw against a spell that targets only you, or when a spell attack misses you

entries: A spell that fails to seize you still possesses momentum, intent, and a path through the world.
Rather than allowing that structure to collapse, you catch it at the instant of failure.
With a sharp redirection, the hostile formula leaves its original path and seeks a new legal target.
You don't recast the magic; you merely refuse to let its missed opportunity go to waste.

entries.name: Redirect Spell
entries: Choose another creature you can see that would be a valid target for the triggering spell if the spell originated from your space. The triggering spell is redirected to that creature.

The original caster's spellcasting ability, spell save DC, spell attack modifier, spell level, and other statistics are unchanged. The spell isn't cast again, and no additional spell slot or components are used.
This spell can't redirect a spell that targets more than one creature, creates an area of effect, targets an object, or has a range of Self.

spell.name: Arcane Backlash
entries: You lace a creature's spellcasting with a hostile resonance that waits for magical structure to pass through it.
The mark is quiet until the victim reaches for a spell.
Then the resonance turns the act of casting against its source, striking through the same mental channels needed to sustain magic.
The more powerful the attempted spell, the more violently the backlash answers.

entries.name: Backlash Mark
entries: Choose one creature you can see within range. It must make an Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, it is marked for the duration.
Whenever the marked creature casts a spell of level 1 or higher, it takes {@damage 1d8} Force damage plus Force damage equal to twice the level of the spell it cast.
If this damage causes the creature to make a saving throw to maintain Concentration, it has Disadvantage on that saving throw.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The Force damage increases by {@damage 1d8} for each slot level above 2.

spell.name: Borrowed Moment

time.condition: which you take when a creature you can see within 60 feet starts its turn

entries: A turn is only a small allotment of possibility, but possibility can be stolen.
You hook one piece of an unfolding moment and pull it away before the creature can spend it.
The stolen fragment arrives in your own future as motion, speed, or an opening to act.
For an instant, initiative stops being an order and becomes something negotiable.

entries.name: Steal a Moment
entries: The triggering creature must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, choose one of the following resources: its Action, its Bonus Action, or an amount of its movement equal to its Speed.

The creature loses the chosen resource for the current turn. Before the end of your next turn, you gain the corresponding resource once: one additional Action, one additional Bonus Action, or additional movement equal to the amount stolen.
An Action gained from this spell can be used normally, including to cast a spell of level 1 or higher. Any unused stolen resource disappears at the end of your next turn.

spell.name: Deferred Wound

time.condition: which you take when a creature you can see within 30 feet takes damage

entries: You don't heal the wound; you refuse to allow the injury to finish happening yet.
For a few seconds, cuts remain unopened, burns hold their heat without consuming flesh, and impacts wait outside the body.
Every new injury joins the same suspended account.
When the delay ends, the body must finally pay everything that time was forced to hold.

entries.name: Deferred Damage
entries: Choose the creature that took the triggering damage. Reduce that triggering damage to 0 and record the amount and damage type that was prevented.
Until the end of the target's next turn, whenever it would take damage, reduce that damage to 0 and record the prevented amount and its damage type.
At the end of the target's next turn, it takes all recorded damage at once, preserving the original damage types and amounts. Healing received before that moment doesn't reduce the recorded damage.
Resistance, Immunity, Vulnerability, and other damage modifications are applied when each instance of damage is originally deferred and aren't applied a second time when the recorded damage is taken.

spell.name: Gravity Tilt
entries: You don't increase gravity; you persuade it that a different direction is down.
The target's balance becomes meaningless as the world seems to rotate without moving.
Walls become floors, open air becomes a fall, and every loose object suddenly agrees with the new orientation.
The effect persists only while your spell holds the false direction in place.

entries.name: Personal Down
entries: Choose one creature you can see within range and one direction. The creature must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, that direction becomes down for the target for the duration.

At the start of each of the target's turns, it falls up to 20 feet in that direction unless something stops the fall. A collision can cause falling damage as normal, treating the distance traveled before the collision as the fall distance.
At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the saving throw, ending the spell on itself on a success.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The maximum distance the target falls at the start of each turn increases by 10 feet for each slot level above 2.

spell.name: Forgotten Presence

components.m: ash from a burned name or portrait

entries: A person leaves traces everywhere: a remembered face, a written name, an image, a pattern of references that says they were here.
You loosen those traces without removing the person who created them.
At first the world merely becomes uncertain; stronger castings can make records and recollections fail together.
The spell doesn't rewrite history. It makes the evidence of identity increasingly difficult for the world to hold.

entries.name: Fading Identity
entries: Touch one willing creature. For the duration, creatures other than you have Disadvantage on ability checks made solely to remember, identify, or connect the target to a past encounter unless they are currently observing the target.
Ordinary notes, labels, and records that identify the target remain present, but a creature searching them has Disadvantage on ability checks made to locate or connect those records to the target.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The spell gains the following cumulative effects when cast with higher-level slots:

items: {@b 3rd Level.} Casual memories of the target's name and appearance become vague unless deliberately refreshed by observing the target or an identifying record.

{@b 4th Level.} Ordinary written references, portraits, photographs, and similar identifying records become blurred, incomplete, or contextless for the duration; the underlying objects aren't destroyed.
{@b 5th Level.} Ordinary recordings and stored identifying data are affected in the same way, and creatures can't gain Advantage on checks to identify the target from such evidence.
{@b 6th Level.} Divination spells of 5th level or lower that are used solely to identify or locate the target from its identity fail to gain useful identifying information.
{@b 7th Level.} Memories that directly identify the target become inaccessible while the spell lasts, though a creature still remembers the events themselves with the target's identity indistinct.
{@b 8th Level.} Magical and ordinary identifying records of the target are suppressed for the duration unless protected by an Artifact, deity, or magic of comparable power.
{@b 9th Level.} All preceding effects apply, and the spell lasts Until Dispelled.

spell.name: Trait Exchange
entries: Bodies solve problems in different ways: fins answer water, wings answer distance, claws answer stone, and unfamiliar senses answer darkness.
You draw one such physical solution from a willing body and rewrite it into another.
The change is visible, producing whatever temporary anatomy is necessary for the borrowed capability.
Nothing is created from theory alone; one creature must surrender the trait while another carries it.

entries.name: Exchange Physical Capability
entries: Choose two willing creatures you can see within range. Choose one eligible physical capability possessed by one creature, the donor. The donor loses that capability for the duration, and the other creature, the recipient, gains it.

Eligible capabilities include a Climb, Swim, Burrow, or Fly Speed; Darkvision; Blindsight out to no more than 30 feet; the ability to breathe underwater or in a specific natural environment; a natural adaptation that lets the donor survive ordinary extreme heat or cold; a natural weapon; or a natural body feature used for movement.

The recipient develops temporary anatomy appropriate to the borrowed trait. If the trait is a natural weapon, the recipient uses its own Strength or Dexterity, as appropriate, for the attack and damage rolls and uses the weapon's original damage die, damage type, reach, and physical form. Special riders aren't transferred unless they are inseparable from the physical structure of the weapon.
Either participant can take a Bonus Action to end the exchange for itself, returning the trait to the donor and ending that transferred capability.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: You can transfer one additional eligible capability between the same two creatures for each slot level above 2.

spell.name: Borrowed Shelter
entries: You weave protection as a set of interchangeable answers rather than a single shield.
The pattern can harden against weapons, brace the body, steady the mind, or fold distance into cover.
Because the shelter is borrowed from possibility rather than fixed form, you can reweave it as danger changes.
The spell's strength lies in being the right defense a heartbeat before it is needed.

entries.name: Choose a Shelter
entries: Choose one willing creature you can see within range and choose one of the following shelters:

items: {@b Bulwark.} The target gains a +2 bonus to AC.
{@b Endurance.} Choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Radiant, or Thunder. The target gains Resistance to the chosen damage type.
{@b Steady Mind.} The target has Advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws.
{@b Sure Body.} The target has Advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saving throws.
{@b Covering Veil.} The target has Half Cover against ranged attacks and effects that originate more than 10 feet away from it.

entries.name: Reweave
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can change the shelter affecting one target of the spell to another option.

entries.name: Emergency Shift
entries: When a target of the spell is hit by an attack or fails a saving throw, you can take a Reaction to change that target's shelter before the triggering attack or saving throw is resolved. The new shelter applies to the triggering event if relevant.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: You can target one additional willing creature for each slot level above 2. Each target can have a different shelter. Reweave and Emergency Shift affect only one target at a time.

spell.name: Spell Graft
entries: You treat a spell as a transferable structure rather than a private piece of training.
The formula takes root in another willing mind, carrying with it just enough understanding to be used.
For a while, the recipient can reach for magic it may never have studied and may not normally be able to learn.
The graft is temporary, but while it lasts the borrowed formula behaves as though it belongs there.

entries.name: Graft a Spell
entries: Touch one willing creature and choose one cantrip or level 1 spell that you know or have prepared. The target knows that spell for the duration, even if it has no Spellcasting feature or the spell isn't on any of its spell lists.
The target uses your spellcasting ability, spell attack modifier, and spell save DC for the grafted spell and follows the spell's normal casting rules and components.

The target can cast the grafted spell once without expending a spell slot. A free casting waives Material components that have no listed cost, but Material components with a listed cost are still required and are consumed normally if the spell says so.

After the free casting is used, the target can cast a grafted spell of level 1 or higher only by expending one of its own spell slots of an appropriate level. A grafted cantrip can be cast any number of times while the spell lasts.

You retain the chosen spell. You can maintain only one Spell Graft at a time. Either you or the target can end the graft at any time without using an action; casting this spell again also ends your previous graft.

items: {@b 2nd Level.} Cantrip or level 1 spell; duration 1 hour.
{@b 3rd Level.} Spell of level 2 or lower; duration 4 hours.
{@b 4th Level.} Spell of level 3 or lower; duration 8 hours.
{@b 5th Level.} Spell of level 4 or lower; duration 24 hours.
{@b 6th Level.} Spell of level 5 or lower; duration 3 days.
{@b 7th Level.} Spell of level 6 or lower; duration 7 days.
{@b 8th Level.} Spell of level 7 or lower; duration 30 days.
{@b 9th Level.} Spell of level 8 or lower; duration Until Dispelled.

spell.name: Affliction Relay
entries: An affliction is more than a condition; it is a relationship between an effect and the creature forced to bear it.
You seize that relationship and reroute it.
Blindness can jump from one set of eyes to another, fear can abandon its first victim, and restraints can reform as spectral equivalents around a new body.
The spell doesn't imitate an affliction. It moves, inherits, or severs the original burden.

entries.name: Choose an Affliction
entries: Choose one creature you can see within range that is affected by one instance of the Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Frightened, Grappled, Poisoned, or Restrained condition. Choose one of the following options.

entries.name: Transfer
entries: Choose a second creature within 30 feet of the first creature. The second creature must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the chosen condition ends on the original creature and affects the second creature instead.

The transferred condition retains its original source, remaining duration, saving throw DC, repeat-save timing, ending conditions, and other rules. If the original condition depended on a physical connection that can't literally move, an equivalent spectral restraint or connection manifests for the transferred condition.

entries.name: Take
entries: You can choose yourself as the second creature. If you do, no saving throw is required; the chosen condition ends on the original creature and affects you instead.

entries.name: Sever
entries: Instead of transferring the condition, make an ability check using your spellcasting ability. The DC equals 10 + the level of the spell or magical effect causing the condition. If the effect has no level, the GM assigns it a level from 1 to 9 based on its power. On a success, the chosen condition ends.

entries.name: Borrowed Origin
entries: A transferred affliction remains the same effect for the purpose of immunity, suppression, removal, and interactions with its original source.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When cast with a 3rd-level slot, you can also relay the Incapacitated condition; with a 4th-level slot, Paralyzed; with a 5th-level slot, Stunned; and with a 6th-level or higher slot, Petrified.

spell.name: Mirror Wound

time.condition: which you take when a creature you can see within 60 feet takes damage

entries: Pain creates a shape in the instant it enters a body.
You catch that shape before it settles and reflect part of it into another living vessel.
With consent, the burden can be divided precisely; without it, the second body can resist becoming the mirror.
The wound remains real throughout. Only its ownership changes.

entries.name: Mirror the Damage
entries: Choose the creature that took the triggering damage and one other creature you can see within range.

entries.name: Share
entries: If both creatures are willing, divide the triggering damage between them in any proportion. The total amount and the original damage types remain unchanged.

entries.name: Take
entries: If you are the second creature, you can take any amount of the triggering damage without making a saving throw, reducing the original creature's damage by the same amount.

entries.name: Reflect
entries: If the second creature is unwilling, it must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, you can transfer up to half the triggering damage, rounded up, from the original creature to the second creature. On a successful save, no damage is transferred.

entries.name: Separate Defenses
entries: Resistance, Immunity, and Vulnerability apply separately to each creature when that creature takes its portion of the damage.

entries.name: No Recursion
entries: Damage created or transferred by Mirror Wound can't trigger another casting of Mirror Wound.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell with a slot of level 3 or higher, the maximum amount you can transfer using Reflect increases by 10 damage for each slot level above 2 and can exceed half the triggering damage.
When cast with a 5th-level or higher slot, you can divide transferred damage among up to two secondary creatures. Each unwilling secondary creature makes its own Constitution saving throw.

spell.name: Sealed Agreement

components.m: a written agreement bearing the mark or signature of every participant

entries: A promise becomes dangerous when magic is allowed to remember its exact wording.
You bind a voluntary agreement into a seal that watches only the clauses its participants knowingly accept.
The spell doesn't compel anyone to sign or force obedience in advance.
Instead, it ensures that a deliberate breach has a consequence none of the participants can pretend they never accepted.

entries.name: Participants and Terms
entries: Choose any number of willing creatures within range that can understand the agreement. Every participant must knowingly and willingly accept the same written terms throughout the casting. If any participant withdraws consent before the casting ends, that creature isn't bound.

The agreement can contain any number of ordinary clauses, but you designate up to three of them as Sealed Clauses. A creature breaches a Sealed Clause only when it knowingly performs an act that clearly violates that clause. Ambiguous, impossible, or involuntary conduct doesn't count as a breach.

entries.name: Breach Consequence
entries: For each Sealed Clause, choose one of the following consequences when you cast the spell. When a bound creature knowingly breaches that clause, the chosen consequence affects that creature for the remaining duration of the agreement unless the consequence says otherwise:

items: {@b Sealed Movement.} All of the breaching creature's Speeds are halved.

{@b Restless Torment.} Whenever the breaching creature attempts to finish a Short Rest or Long Rest, it must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, magical torment prevents it from gaining any benefits from that rest. It makes this saving throw separately for each rest it attempts.

{@b Withering Judgment.} When the creature breaches the clause, and again at each dawn while this consequence remains, it takes {@damage 6d10} Necrotic damage. This damage ignores Resistance and Immunity to Necrotic damage. Each time the creature takes this damage, its Hit Point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. This reduction lasts until this consequence ends.

{@b Arcane Retribution.} Choose Psychic or Force when you create the agreement. When the creature breaches the clause, it takes {@damage 8d6} damage of the chosen type. At each dawn while this consequence remains, the breaching creature and every creature within 10 feet of it take {@damage 2d6} damage of the chosen type.

{@b Arcane Vulnerability.} The breaching creature takes a penalty to saving throws against spells and magical effects. The penalty equals the level of the spell slot used to cast Sealed Agreement minus 1: -2 with a 3rd-level slot, -3 with a 4th-level slot, -4 with a 5th-level slot, -5 with a 6th-level slot, -6 with a 7th-level slot, -7 with an 8th-level slot, and -8 with a 9th-level slot.

entries.name: Spell Clause
entries: Instead of one normal breach consequence, you can designate a Spell Clause. Choose a spell of level 1 or lower that you know or have prepared, has a casting time of an Action or Bonus Action, and can target a single creature. If a participant breaches that clause, the chosen spell is cast on that participant at the next dawn as though you cast it using the same spellcasting ability used for Sealed Agreement. Any costly or consumed Material components required by the chosen spell must be provided during the casting of Sealed Agreement.
A participant can't be affected by more than one Spell Clause from the same Sealed Agreement at a single dawn.

entries.name: Ending the Agreement
entries: The agreement ends early for every participant if every currently bound participant willingly agrees to end it while within 30 feet of one another.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When cast with a 4th-level slot, the duration becomes 1 year. When cast with a 5th-level or higher slot, the duration becomes Until Dispelled.

spell.name: Permanency

m.text: special inks worth 1,000 GP, which the spell consumes

entries: Most spells are written with an ending built into their structure.
You spend an hour finding that final line and replacing it with a self-sustaining loop.
The altered magic no longer waits for concentration or the passing of its original duration.
What remains is not indestructible magic, but a spell that now expects to continue until something deliberately ends it.

entries.name: Make a Spell Permanent
entries: Touch a creature, object, or point affected by a spell you cast that has a duration other than Instantaneous and that is still active for the entire casting of Permanency. The affected spell's duration becomes Until Dispelled and it no longer requires Concentration.

Permanency doesn't change the spell's targets, area, damage, saving throws, activation requirements, or other effects. If the spell contains an effect that can normally be ended early by the caster, that option remains.

entries.name: Suppression
entries: An antimagic effect suppresses a spell made permanent by this spell but doesn't end the permanent spell. The spell resumes when the suppression ends unless it was otherwise dispelled or ended.

entries.name: Permanent Limit
entries: You can have a maximum number of spells made permanent by your castings of Permanency equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier. If you would exceed this limit, choose one of your existing permanent spells; that spell immediately ends before the new one becomes permanent.

spell.name: Void Needle
entries: You pull a hair-thin flaw in space between two fingers.
The flaw launches like a needle, leaving no trail until it punctures its target.
Where it strikes, the wound in space lingers for one dangerous heartbeat.
The first creature to disturb that scar discovers that emptiness can cut twice.

entries.name: Needle and Scar
entries: Make a ranged spell attack against one creature in range. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d12} Force damage.

A spatial scar remains in the target's space until the start of your next turn. The first creature other than the original target that enters that space or starts its turn there takes {@damage 1d6} Force damage, and the scar disappears.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The initial damage increases by one {@damage 1d12} at levels 5 (2d12), 11 (3d12), and 17 (4d12). The scar damage increases by one {@damage 1d6} at the same levels (2d6, 3d6, and 4d6).

spell.name: Riftlash
entries: You draw a short tear in space and snap it forward like a whip.
The first cut hurts, but the rift leaves the target's position improperly stitched.
Any meaningful movement tugs that damaged geometry open again.
Even teleportation cannot avoid paying for crossing the frayed edge.

entries.name: Spatially Frayed
entries: Make a melee spell attack against one creature within range. On a hit, it takes {@damage 1d12} Force damage and becomes Spatially Frayed until the start of your next turn.
The first time the frayed target moves 5 feet or more before the effect ends, it takes {@damage 1d8} Force damage. This includes willing movement, forced movement, and teleportation.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The initial damage increases by one {@damage 1d12} at levels 5, 11, and 17. The movement damage increases by one {@damage 1d8} at the same levels.

spell.name: Ready Hand
entries: Your empty hand closes around the outline of whatever simple tool the moment demands.
Weight and shape gather from a brief fold in space until the imagined object becomes solid.
The conjuration favors practical things rather than treasures: equipment, implements, ammunition, and working sets.
When another shape is needed, the same matter quietly reforms instead of disappearing.

entries.name: Conjured Equipment
entries: Conjure one handheld tool, piece of simple equipment, set of ammunition, or working set of ordinary practical objects of your choice. The conjured matter can weigh up to 10 pounds and must fit within a 3-foot cube.

The object functions as a real example of its kind but can't serve as a costly Material component or be sold as genuine permanent goods. As a Bonus Action, you can reform it into another eligible object. It vanishes when the spell ends.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: At level 5, the weight limit becomes 25 pounds and the space becomes a 5-foot cube. At level 11, the weight limit becomes 100 pounds and you can maintain two conjured objects at once. At level 17, the weight limit becomes 500 pounds, the space becomes a 10-foot cube, and you can maintain three objects at once.

spell.name: Matter Tune
entries: You adjust one ordinary property of matter without changing what the object fundamentally is.
A surface can grip like rough stone, slide like ice, harden, soften, seal, float, insulate, or conduct.
The alteration is subtle enough to remain useful outside combat and flexible enough to be rewritten as circumstances change.
You aren't creating new material; you are retuning the behavior of what is already there.

entries.name: Tune Matter
entries: Touch one object or continuous portion of material that fits within a 5-foot cube. Choose one mode: Grip, Slip, Harden, Soften, Seal, Float, Insulate, or Conduct.

items: {@b Grip.} The affected surface strongly resists sliding and provides secure handholds and footing.
{@b Slip.} The affected surface becomes extremely slick and difficult to grip.
{@b Harden.} Flexible or fragile material becomes rigid and substantially harder to bend or deform.
{@b Soften.} Rigid material becomes flexible enough to bend, fold, or compress without immediately breaking.
{@b Seal.} Small seams, pores, and ordinary leaks in the affected material close.
{@b Float.} The affected material becomes buoyant enough to float in water unless held under by substantially greater weight.
{@b Insulate.} The material becomes a strong ordinary insulator against heat and electricity.
{@b Conduct.} The material becomes a strong ordinary conductor of heat and electricity.

entries: As a Bonus Action while touching the affected material, you can change its mode.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The maximum affected space increases to a 10-foot cube at level 5, a 20-foot cube at level 11, and a 40-foot cube at level 17.

spell.name: Pinprick Gate
entries: You open two openings so small that space barely notices they exist.
Light, sound, fingers, tools, and tiny objects can pass from one pinprick to the other without crossing the distance between them.
With practice, the openings widen enough to become a genuine working passage.
The gate never becomes a doorway for whole bodies, but it can make distance irrelevant to careful hands.

entries.name: Linked Gates
entries: Create two linked circular portals in unoccupied spaces you can see within range. Each portal is 1 inch in diameter, and the two portals can be no more than 60 feet apart.

A creature adjacent to either portal can see and hear through the other, pass appropriately sized objects through it, reach a body part through it, and treat the opposite portal as the point of origin for a spell or other effect that can physically pass through the opening.
As a Bonus Action, you can move either portal to another unoccupied space you can see, provided both portals remain within the spell's allowed range and separation.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: At level 5, range becomes 60 feet, maximum separation 120 feet, and diameter 3 inches. At level 11, range becomes 150 feet, separation 300 feet, and diameter 6 inches. At level 17, range becomes 500 feet, separation 1,000 feet, and diameter 1 foot.

spell.name: Skyhook
entries: You place an invisible point of impossible purchase in empty air.
Rope, chain, gear, or a desperate falling hand can catch on the point as though it were bolted into stone.
The hook has no visible support because the spell anchors it to position rather than material.
For climbers and explorers, a single reliable point in the wrong place can be more useful than a ladder.

entries.name: Invisible Anchor
entries: Create an invisible fixed anchor at a point you can see within range. The anchor can support up to 200 pounds before it fails and the spell ends for that anchor.
A rope, chain, cord, or similar line can be attached to the anchor. If a creature within 5 feet of an anchor falls while holding or attached to such a line, the anchor can catch the fall normally.
You can maintain a number of Skyhooks at once equal to your Proficiency Bonus; creating another causes the oldest to vanish.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The weight each hook can support increases to 500 pounds at level 5, 1,000 pounds at level 11, and 2,000 pounds at level 17.

spell.name: Counterweight
entries: You change how strongly the world counts an object's weight without changing its size or substance.
A burden can become strangely light in the hands, or a small object can press down with multiplied heaviness.
The object keeps its shape, momentum, and identity while gravity negotiates a different price for moving it.
The alteration is simple, but leverage makes simple changes powerful.

entries.name: Alter Weight
entries: Touch one object and choose Lighten or Burden. With Lighten, the object weighs one-quarter its normal weight. With Burden, it weighs four times its normal weight. The spell doesn't change the object's size or carrying capacity.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: At level 5, Lighten reduces weight to one-eighth and Burden multiplies it by 8. At level 11, the values become one-sixteenth and ×16. At level 17, they become one-thirty-second and ×32.

spell.name: Tracefire
entries: A line of controlled fire follows your gesture without behaving like an ordinary flame.
It can guide, signal, mark, outline, fuse, rewrite, or briefly burn without becoming an uncontrolled blaze.
The flame remembers the path you gave it and remains where it was traced.
Its value lies as much in precise work and communication as in harm.

entries.name: Trace a Flame
entries: Trace a line of magical fire up to 30 feet long along a surface or through the air. Choose one mode when you create the line:

items: {@b Guide.} The line provides clear visible guidance along its route.
{@b Signal.} The line flashes or changes intensity in a simple repeating pattern you choose.

{@b Burn.} One creature whose space the line crosses must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 1d12} Fire damage on a failed save or half as much on a success. A creature can be damaged only once by each casting.
{@b Mark.} The line leaves a harmless visible mark where it touches a surface.
{@b Outline.} The line clings to the outline of an object or opening it crosses.
{@b Fuse.} The line can fuse together a narrow seam in material that ordinary heat could reasonably join.
{@b Rewrite.} As an Action, you can redraw or reposition the existing line within range.

entries: The flame doesn't spread unless the Burn mode directly ignites a readily flammable unattended substance.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: Burn damage increases by {@damage 1d12} at levels 5, 11, and 17.

spell.name: Handprint
entries: You leave an invisible magical impression that remembers a simple physical interaction.
A latch being pulled, a page being turned, a button being pressed, or a lever being moved can be stored as a tiny piece of motion.
Later, the mark can repeat that interaction without a visible hand present.
The spell is less a servant than a recorded gesture waiting to be replayed.

entries.name: Recorded Interaction
entries: Touch an object that fits within a 5-foot cube and perform one simple physical interaction with it that could normally be completed with one hand and doesn't require an attack roll, saving throw, or ability check. An invisible Handprint records that interaction.

While you are within 60 feet of the mark, you can take a Bonus Action to cause it to repeat the recorded interaction. When you create the mark, you can instead define a simple observable trigger that causes the interaction to occur automatically.
You can reset a triggered Handprint by touching it. A Handprint can perform its interaction silently if the interaction itself can reasonably be performed without noise.
You can maintain a number of Handprints at once equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: At level 5, the affected object can fit within a 10-foot cube and your remote range becomes 120 feet. At level 11, those values become a 20-foot cube and 300 feet. At level 17, they become a 40-foot cube and 1,000 feet.

spell.name: Palmforge
entries: Your palm becomes a tiny workshop where material yields to intention.
Edges sharpen, holes open, surfaces flatten, pieces join, and rigid forms bend into practical shapes.
The process is controlled rather than violent and leaves no shower of sparks or discarded waste.
You are not creating matter; you are persuading existing matter to accept a different arrangement.

entries.name: Reshape Material
entries: Touch an object or continuous piece of material that fits within a 1-foot cube. You can reshape it using one of the following operations: Shape, Fit, Join, Separate, Bore, Edge, Texture, or Reform.

The spell can make practical alterations such as bending a bracket, opening a clean hole, joining compatible pieces, separating a seam, creating a cutting edge, changing surface texture, or restoring a previously shaped portion. It can't create a complex functioning mechanism whose internal design you don't understand.
When the spell ends, you can choose for the object's current shape to remain instead of reverting.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The affected size increases to a 3-foot cube at level 5, a 5-foot cube at level 11, and a 10-foot cube at level 17.

spell.name: Forceplate
entries: A square of translucent force snaps into existence where you indicate.
It has no hinges, legs, or frame, yet it can serve as a step, brace, shelf, shield, or pressure surface.
The plate is small enough to be precise and strong enough to matter.
Its usefulness comes from treating empty air as a place where solid geometry can temporarily exist.

entries.name: Create Forceplate
entries: Create a flat plane of force up to 2 feet on a side at a point you can see within range. It can support up to 300 pounds and can be oriented in any direction.
The plate is solid and can act as a small surface, brace, or barrier. As a Bonus Action, you can move it up to 30 feet to a point you can see and change its orientation.

As a Reaction when an unattended object or willing creature within 5 feet of the plate would fall or collide with a surface, you can move the plate up to 5 feet to catch or brace it, provided the weight limit isn't exceeded.
You can dismiss the plate at any time without using an action.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: At level 5, a plate can be up to 3 feet on a side and support 1,000 pounds. At level 11, a plate can be up to 5 feet on a side and support 5,000 pounds, and you can maintain two Forceplates at once. At level 17, a plate can be up to 10 feet on a side and support 20,000 pounds, and you can maintain three Forceplates at once. If you can maintain more than one plate, each can be moved, oriented, and dismissed independently.

spell.name: Pocket Fold
entries: You crease a tiny pocket into space and leave its opening hanging where a hand can reach it.
Objects disappear through the fold without traveling anywhere visible.
The storage space is shallow but obedient, following the opening when you reposition it.
With experience, you learn to open the same pocket from more than one place at once.

entries.name: Folded Storage
entries: Create a small extradimensional opening at a point you can see within range. The pocket can contain up to 20 pounds of objects and no more than 1 cubic foot of volume.
A creature adjacent to the opening can store or retrieve one object as a Bonus Action. As a Bonus Action, you can move the opening up to 30 feet to another point you can see.
If the pocket is overloaded, the excess object falls from the opening and isn't stored. When the spell ends, all stored contents fall harmlessly from the opening's last location.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: At level 5, capacity becomes 50 pounds and 2 cubic feet. At level 11, 200 pounds and 8 cubic feet, and you can maintain a second opening into the same pocket. At level 17, capacity becomes 1,000 pounds and 40 cubic feet, and you can maintain up to three openings.

spell.name: Greenhand

components.m: a seed, leaf, or piece of a living plant

entries: You ask living plant matter for a practical shape and accelerate only the growth needed to provide it.
Vines become lines, roots become braces, leaves become filters, and stems become temporary tools.
The magic can also preserve a small piece of growth as a genuine young plant.
Greenhand is less about commanding nature than giving growth a clear job for a little while.

entries.name: Shape Living Growth
entries: Choose living plant matter within range and create one of the following forms: Vine, Ladder, Brace, Mat, Probe, Filter, Patch, Sprout, or Regrow.

items: {@b Vine.} Grow a flexible plant line that can be used as rope.
{@b Ladder.} Grow climbable stems and grips along a surface.
{@b Brace.} Reinforce or prop a small object or opening with roots and stems.
{@b Mat.} Create a woven surface of roots, moss, or leaves over an area.
{@b Probe.} Extend a thin root or vine into a narrow opening you can reach.
{@b Filter.} Grow a dense layer of plant matter able to strain ordinary debris from air or water.
{@b Patch.} Temporarily close a small tear, hole, or seam with living growth.
{@b Sprout.} Create a healthy young plant from suitable living plant material. This plant remains when the spell ends.
{@b Regrow.} As a Bonus Action, reshape one temporary growth created by this casting into another eligible form.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The maximum useful length or largest dimension of the temporary growth becomes 20 feet at level 5, 40 feet at level 11, and 80 feet at level 17.

spell.name: Mercybrand
entries: You write a small radiant sign onto a creature, but the sign can mean judgment or mercy depending on how you invoke it.
The same light that burns an enemy can guide an ally, absorb a blow, or become a final reserve of courage.
Each brand is a promise that the marked creature won't disappear from your attention.
The magic remains flexible until you decide how that promise should be spent.

entries.name: Judgment
entries: Make a ranged spell attack against one creature in range. On a hit, it takes {@damage 1d12} Radiant damage and bears your Mercybrand until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Mercy
entries: Instead of attacking, you can place a Mercybrand on one willing creature in range for the duration.

entries.name: Use a Mercybrand
entries: You can use a brand you placed in one of the following ways:

items: {@b Guard.} When the branded creature takes damage, you can take a Reaction to end the brand and reduce the damage by {@dice 1d8} + your spellcasting ability modifier.
{@b Rally.} As a Bonus Action, end the brand. The creature gains {@dice 1d6} Temporary Hit Points.
{@b Beacon.} You always know the direction of a branded creature while it is within 1 mile of you, and you know if it reaches 0 Hit Points.
{@b Signal.} You can cause the brand to glow, dim, or pulse in a simple pattern without using an action.
{@b Transfer.} As a Bonus Action, move the brand to a willing creature within 5 feet of the branded creature.

entries: You can have Mercybrands on multiple creatures, but a creature can bear only one Mercybrand from you at a time.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: Judgment damage increases by {@damage 1d12} at levels 5, 11, and 17. Guard's reduction and Rally's Temporary Hit Points each gain one additional die of their listed size at those levels.

spell.name: Warden's Grasp
entries: A spectral hand forms from condensed force, equally capable of striking and doing careful work.
It can catch, brace, carry, shove, hold, relay, or simply remain where a second pair of hands would be useful.
The hand is a warden rather than a servant, built to control space and prevent things from going where they shouldn't.
When violence is necessary, the same fingers close into a precise forceful blow.

entries.name: Strike
entries: Make a ranged spell attack against one creature within range. On a hit, it takes {@damage 1d12} Force damage. Immediately after the attack, you can move one unattended object weighing 10 pounds or less that is within 10 feet of the target up to 10 feet.

entries.name: Manifest Hand
entries: Instead of making the attack, manifest a spectral hand at a point within range for the duration. It can support up to 30 pounds.
As a Bonus Action, you can move the hand up to 30 feet and have it perform a simple physical task such as handle an object, brace something, carry a light object, hold a rope, or relay an item.
As a Reaction, you can command the hand to catch a falling unattended object or willing creature within 5 feet of it, provided its weight limit isn't exceeded.
You can also use the hand to shove or hold fast a light unattended object when physically reasonable. You can reform a destroyed or dismissed hand as a Bonus Action while the spell lasts.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: Strike damage increases by {@damage 1d12} at levels 5, 11, and 17. The hand's weight capacity becomes 100 pounds at level 5, 300 pounds at level 11, and 1,000 pounds at level 17.

spell.name: Voidstride
entries: You step into the smallest possible absence between one position and the next.
There is no flash or tunnel, only a brief impression that your outline skipped a piece of distance.
Space closes before anything can follow the route you used.
With experience, the missing step grows longer while remaining just as effortless.

entries.name: Short Teleport
entries: Teleport up to 10 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The teleport distance becomes 15 feet at level 5, 20 feet at level 11, and 30 feet at level 17.

spell.name: Death Recall
entries: Death ends a creature's future, but for a moment its body still remembers what it was capable of doing.
You call that final physical record forward without restoring life or creating undeath.
The corpse rises only long enough to spend one impossible turn using fragments of the abilities it possessed before death.
Then the borrowed continuity collapses and the body returns to exactly what it is: a corpse.

entries.name: Stolen Turn
entries: Choose one corpse you can see within range. Immediately after your turn ends, the corpse takes one Stolen Turn under your control, using the statistics and capabilities it possessed immediately before it died, subject to the limits below. The corpse isn't revived and doesn't become Undead.

entries.name: Level 1: Last Motion
entries: The corpse can move up to half its Speed, take the Attack action to make one ordinary attack it possessed in life, and perform one simple object interaction. It can use inherent riders that are inseparable from that ordinary attack. It can't use a Bonus Action, Reaction, spell, Multiattack, Recharge action, Legendary Action, or other special action.

entries.name: Level 5: Lesser Reconstruction
entries: The corpse can use its full Speed and movement modes, Multiattack or another ordinary combat Action it possessed, Bonus Actions, and one Reaction during the Stolen Turn. The spell temporarily repairs major bodily damage and can restore one missing limb or equivalent structure for the duration of the Stolen Turn.

entries.name: Level 11: Greater Reconstruction
entries: The corpse can use special actions, Recharge abilities, breath weapons, supernatural movement, teleportation, and transformations it possessed in life. It can cast its cantrips and spells up to a spell level equal to half the highest spell level it could cast in life, rounded up, using its original spellcasting ability, spell attack modifier, and spell save DC. A spell slot required for a spell cast during the Stolen Turn is treated as available for that casting. The spell reconstructs anatomy necessary for those abilities.

entries.name: Level 17: Perfect Reconstruction
entries: The corpse can use its full capabilities from immediately before death, including Actions, Bonus Actions, one Reaction, spells, innate spells, limited-use abilities, and Legendary Actions when their normal timing permits. Temporary resources supplied by this spell exist only for the Stolen Turn.

entries.name: Concentration and Return to Death
entries: If the corpse casts or activates something that requires Concentration, the corpse maintains that Concentration using its original Constitution saving throw modifier. That Concentration ends when Death Recall ends.
At the end of the Stolen Turn, every temporary reconstruction and resource created by this spell disappears and the corpse returns to death.

spell.name: Glacier Fang
entries: Frost gathers along a weapon in a narrow ridge shaped like a translucent fang.
The cold bites after the weapon does, stealing a little momentum from anything struck.
Away from combat, the same controlled chill can smother a small flame or lock exposed water into ice.
The enchantment clings briefly even if the weapon leaves your hand.

entries.name: Frozen Weapon
entries: Touch one weapon. For the duration, attacks made with it deal an extra {@damage 1d4} Cold damage.
Once on each turn when the weapon deals this extra damage to a creature, that creature's Speed is reduced by 5 feet until the start of the attacker's next turn.
As a Bonus Action while holding the affected weapon, you can extinguish one ordinary flame no larger than a torch within 5 feet of the weapon or freeze a small amount of exposed water it touches.
If you stop holding the weapon, the spell remains on it until the end of your next turn before ending.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The extra damage becomes {@damage 2d4} at level 5, {@damage 3d4} at level 11, and {@damage 4d4} at level 17. The Speed reduction becomes 10 feet at level 11 and 15 feet at level 17.

spell.name: Fatehook

time.condition: which you take when a creature you can see within 30 feet makes an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw

entries: You catch a tiny loose thread in the probability surrounding a creature's attempt.
A favorable tug can turn an almost into an enough; a hostile tug can make certainty slip.
The spell doesn't show you the future or guarantee an outcome.
It simply hooks one possibility and gives it a little more or less weight.

entries.name: Boon or Bane
entries: Roll {@dice 1d4}. Choose Boon or Bane. With Boon, add the number rolled to the triggering roll. With Bane, subtract it.
If you choose Bane against an unwilling creature, that creature can make a Wisdom saving throw. On a success, Fatehook has no effect on its roll.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The die becomes {@dice 1d6} at level 5, {@dice 1d8} at level 11, and {@dice 1d10} at level 17.

spell.name: Ghostwalk
entries: The target's body becomes slightly less committed to being solid.
Edges blur, carried objects lose their weight against walls, and matter can overlap matter without becoming fully ethereal.
Passing through solid structures remains slow and deliberate because the body must continuously negotiate with the material around it.
The spell always remembers where the nearest safe open space was, preventing a careless passage from becoming a tomb.

entries.name: Partial Spectral Form
entries: Choose one willing creature you can see within range. For the duration, the target and everything it is wearing or carrying can move through creatures and solid objects. Moving through such matter costs 1 extra foot of movement for each foot traveled.
The target can't move through more than 15 continuous feet of solid matter during a single passage.

entries.name: Ethereal Reach
entries: The target can reach a hand or held object through a solid barrier as part of an interaction, provided the depth of solid matter doesn't exceed the spell's current passage limit.

entries.name: Living Passage
entries: Moving through another creature doesn't damage or displace either creature, and the spaces occupied by creatures are treated as Difficult Terrain for the target.

entries.name: Distort Through Openings
entries: The target can squeeze through openings substantially smaller than its body if its carried equipment can pass with it in spectral form.

entries.name: Look Beyond
entries: By placing part of its face through a barrier within the passage limit, the target can see and hear from the opposite side.

entries.name: Safe Return
entries: If the spell would end while the target is inside a solid object or creature, the target is immediately moved by the shortest route to the nearest unoccupied space it can occupy.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The maximum continuous depth of solid matter becomes 30 feet at level 5, 60 feet at level 11, and 120 feet at level 17.

spell.name: Rewind

components.m: a small hourglass filled with silver sand

entries: With a single command, you force one creature backward through the moments it has just lived.
Wounds close in reverse, spent strength returns, expended magic gathers back into the body, and the creature is dragged back to where it stood only moments before.
Even death can be undone if it occurred within the brief span your magic can reach.
Yet the world around the creature remains unchanged. Every attack it made, every spell it cast, and every consequence it caused remains behind—the creature alone is rewound.

entries.name: Rewind
entries: Choose one creature you can see within range, or the corpse of a creature that died within the period this spell can rewind.
Choose either the start of the target's previous turn or the start of the turn before its previous turn. The target is returned to exactly the state it possessed at the chosen point.

This includes the target's location, Hit Points, Temporary Hit Points, conditions, spell slots, expended Hit Dice, expended class features, species features, and other limited-use abilities, Actions, Bonus Actions, Reactions, movement, magic item charges it expended, ammunition and other expendable resources it used, Material components it consumed, Concentration, physical form, missing or destroyed body parts, and equipment and carried objects it possessed at that moment.
If the target's former space is occupied or otherwise impossible for it to occupy, it appears in the nearest unoccupied space it can safely occupy.

entries.name: The World Remains Changed
entries: Only the target is rewound. Nothing the target did after the chosen point is undone.

Damage it dealt remains. Creatures it killed remain dead. Healing it provided remains. Conditions it inflicted or removed remain changed. Objects it damaged, destroyed, created, or moved remain as they are. Spells it cast remain in effect for their normal remaining durations. Creatures it summoned remain. Information it revealed remains known. Creatures it moved or teleported remain in their new locations.

Resources restored to the target return even though the effects created by spending those resources remain. For example, an expended spell slot, magic item charge, consumed Material component, or limited-use feature can return without undoing the spell or effect it produced.

entries.name: Death Rewound
entries: If the target died after the chosen point and was alive at that point, it returns to life as part of the rewind. The target doesn't need to be willing.
If the target was dead at the chosen point, the spell restores it to that dead state instead.

spell.name: Sovereign Edict
entries: Your presence becomes the center of an unquestionable decree.
With a word, you impose a single law upon the space surrounding you, and the world itself refuses to permit its violation.
The decree moves wherever you move, surrounding allies and enemies alike—yet you decide whose actions are bound by your authority.
Within your dominion, resistance is possible. Defiance is not always.

entries.name: Sovereign Aura
entries: A 30-foot Emanation surrounds you for the duration and moves with you.
When you cast the spell, choose one Edict from the options below.

Whenever a creature other than you enters the Emanation for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, you can choose whether that creature is subject to the Edict. You make this choice separately for each creature.
You are never restricted by your own Edict. A creature ceases to be subject to the Edict when it leaves the Emanation.

entries.name: Defy the Edict
entries: Whenever a subject creature would violate the chosen Edict, it makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a successful save, it can perform that action or receive that effect normally. On a failed save, the prohibited action or effect fails, and any Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, spell slot, charge, or other resource it would have spent isn't expended.
A creature makes this saving throw each time it would violate the Edict.

entries.name: No Passage
entries: A subject creature can't willingly leave the Emanation. Teleportation, planar travel, or any other effect it willingly uses to move itself outside the Emanation is also prohibited.
If you move far enough that a subject creature would fall outside the Emanation, the creature isn't dragged with you; the Edict doesn't prevent you from moving away from it.

entries.name: No Violence
entries: A subject creature can't willingly deal damage to another creature. This includes weapon attacks, spells, features, and other effects whose direct result would deal damage to another creature.
It can still attack objects, move, defend itself, heal, or use effects that don't deal damage to another creature.

entries.name: No Restoration
entries: A subject creature can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.
It can still cast or use an effect that restores Hit Points to another creature, provided the subject creature doesn't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points from that effect.

entries.name: No Transformation
entries: A subject creature can't willingly change its form, size, or physical shape through a spell, feature, or magical effect.
A transformation already active when the creature becomes subject to the Edict isn't ended.

entries.name: No Spellcasting
entries: A subject creature can't cast spells of 6th level or lower. Spells of 7th level or higher can be cast normally.

spell.name: Severance

components.m: a length of silver thread cut cleanly in two

entries: Every bond leaves a thread behind—between spell and victim, master and servant, memory and identity, bearer and artifact.
You perceive those invisible connections and draw an unseen edge across them.
Magic collapses, curses lose their claim, memories rewrite themselves around what has vanished, and bonds once thought permanent simply cease to exist.
Nothing is truly beyond the blade. Some connections merely require a sharper spell.

Choose one creature you can see within range. An unwilling target must make a Charisma saving throw. A willing creature can choose to fail the saving throw. On a failed save, choose up to three connections involving the target from the options below and sever them immediately. If an option has multiple valid instances, each instance counts as a separate connection unless that option states otherwise.

entries.name: Concentration
entries: Choose one spell or effect on which the target is concentrating. The target's Concentration on that effect immediately ends.

entries.name: Summoning
entries: Choose one creature magically summoned, conjured, or called by the target. The magical connection sustaining that creature is severed, and the chosen creature immediately disappears.
It returns to whatever state or place is appropriate for the effect that brought it forth, if applicable. If no such state or place exists, it simply ceases to be present.

This happens even if the summoning effect would normally allow the creature to remain after losing contact with its summoner. The spell or feature that produced the creature doesn't necessarily end for any other summoned creatures it created unless you separately sever those connections.

entries.name: Control
entries: Choose one magical connection through which the target controls another creature or another creature controls the target. This can include a Charm, possession, domination, supernatural command, compelled behavior, magical obedience, or a similar effect that directly controls another creature.

That connection ends immediately. If the effect affects multiple creatures, only the chosen connection involving the target is severed unless ending that connection necessarily ends the entire effect.

entries.name: Telepathic Link
entries: Choose one magical telepathic, sensory, emotional, or communication connection involving the target. That connection immediately ends.
Neither side can continue communicating, perceiving, sharing senses, or exchanging information through that connection.

entries.name: Shared Effect
entries: Choose one ongoing magical effect that directly links the target to another creature. This can include an effect that shares damage, transfers Hit Points, redirects harm, exchanges senses, shares conditions or resources, causes one creature to suffer or benefit when the other does, or otherwise magically connects the states of two creatures.
That connection ends.

entries.name: Planar Bond
entries: Choose one magical connection binding the target to a particular plane, location, creature, or object. The chosen connection is severed.
This doesn't transport the target, destroy either end of the connection, or reverse anything that already happened because of that bond.

entries.name: Remote Effect
entries: Choose one ongoing spell or magical effect that the target can command, direct, manipulate, or control from a distance. The target permanently loses its connection to that effect.
If the effect can continue independently, it remains but can no longer be controlled by the target. If the effect can't exist without that connection, it ends.

entries.name: Spell or Curse
entries: Choose one ongoing spell, curse, or magical effect affecting the target. You sever that effect from the target.
If the effect also affects other creatures, objects, or areas, it ends only for the target unless the effect can't continue without the target's connection to it.

This option can sever curses, magical diseases or afflictions, magical transformations, magical restraints, seals, wards attached to the target, magical buffs or debuffs, ongoing spell effects, effects with a duration of Until Dispelled, and permanent magical effects.
The casting of Severance must be sufficiently powerful to cut the chosen effect, as described under Severance Power.

entries.name: Attunement
entries: Choose one magic item to which the target is attuned. The target's Attunement to that item immediately ends.

The item itself isn't damaged, destroyed, or otherwise altered. This connection can be severed even if the item's curse or properties normally prevent its bearer from willingly ending Attunement, provided the casting of Severance is sufficiently powerful.

Ending Attunement doesn't automatically end unrelated effects that the item already created unless you separately sever those effects. Attunement to an Artifact requires a sufficiently powerful casting of this spell.

entries.name: Memory
entries: Choose one memory or one connected group of memories possessed by the target concerning a clearly defined creature, place, event, period of time, relationship, agreement, experience, or subject. The chosen memories are permanently severed from the target.

The target doesn't merely experience an empty gap. Instead, Severance creates plausible false memories to replace whatever was removed. The surrounding memories are altered only as much as necessary to make the target's remembered past feel natural, continuous, and internally consistent.

The target might remember being alone when another creature was actually present, meeting someone else instead, reaching a destination by another route, learning information from another plausible source, making a choice for a different reason, surviving an event without remembering who actually helped, or an uneventful period of time in place of something significant.
Severance favors the smallest plausible reconstruction necessary to conceal the removed memories. These false memories don't alter reality.

Physical evidence, written records, magical records, possessions, injuries, portraits, and the memories of unaffected creatures remain unchanged. If the target later encounters evidence contradicting its reconstructed memories, it can realize that something is inconsistent, but doing so doesn't automatically restore the severed memories.
The target can learn the forgotten information again and form new memories normally. Magically protected or otherwise exceptionally resistant memories may require a higher-level casting of Severance.

entries.name: Identity
entries: You sever the target's identity from the memories of every other creature that currently remembers the target as an individual. This counts as one connection, regardless of how many creatures are affected.

Every affected creature permanently forgets the target's identity and all personal memories specifically connecting that identity to its experiences. This can include the target's name, aliases, face, voice, mannerisms, personality, relationships, conversations, shared experiences, friendships, rivalries, promises, conflicts, affection, hatred, and role in remembered events.
The target retains its own memories.

entries.name: Reconstructed Identity
entries: The memories removed through Identity don't leave obvious gaps. Instead, Severance creates individualized false memories for every affected creature, reconstructing their past in whatever plausible way requires the fewest changes.

Different creatures don't necessarily receive the same replacement history. One creature might remember escaping danger alone, another might remember being rescued by an unidentified stranger, someone taught by the target might remember learning from books or another teacher, and a former companion might remember traveling with the same group but never remember the target being among them.
Someone who loved the target might remember that period of life differently, with the relationship removed or plausibly attributed elsewhere.
The spell doesn't create knowledge a creature couldn't plausibly have possessed. It reconstructs recollection using information and possibilities consistent with that creature's experiences.

entries.name: Evidence Remains
entries: Identity doesn't alter reality or physical evidence. Written records, portraits, signatures, letters, possessions, monuments, magical records, historical documents, and other evidence of the target's actions remain unchanged.

An affected creature can rediscover the target's existence through surviving evidence. If it encounters the target again, it doesn't recognize the target through the severed memories but can meet them anew, learn about them, and form entirely new memories normally.

entries.name: Seamless Reconstruction
entries: False memories created by Memory or Identity aren't ongoing illusions and don't require Severance to remain active. Once created, they become part of the affected creature's memories.

They don't disappear in an Antimagic Field, don't end if Severance is later dispelled, and aren't automatically revealed by Detect Magic. They can conflict with surviving physical evidence and can later be altered, removed, or replaced by sufficiently powerful memory-affecting magic.

entries.name: Violent Severance
entries: After successfully severing the chosen connections, you can make the Severance clean or violent. A clean Severance deals no damage.

If you choose a violent Severance, the target takes {@damage 4d10} Force or Psychic damage, your choice, for each connection successfully severed. The damage is dealt after all chosen connections are severed.
Only the primary target of Severance takes this damage. Creatures whose memories are altered by Identity aren't damaged.

entries.name: Cut Either Side
entries: Severance doesn't care who created the chosen connection. You can use it to free an ally from an enemy's curse, break possession, end unwanted Attunement, remove an enemy's control over a summon, cut another creature's Concentration, sever a bond maintained by a third party, remove beneficial magic from an enemy, or remove harmful magic from an ally.
The spell affects the connection itself, not its ownership.

entries.name: Severance Power
entries: Not every connection can be severed by every casting of this spell. The level of the spell slot used to cast Severance determines how powerful a connection it can cut.
For an effect created by a spell, the slot used to cast Severance must be at least as high as the level of that spell.
For magical effects that have no spell level, the DM determines the minimum level of Severance necessary based on the effect's power and source.

Ordinary curses, magic item effects, supernatural bonds, memories, Attunement, and similar connections can normally be severed by the spell's base 7th-level casting unless something specifically makes them more powerful.

items: {@b 8th Level.} You can sever up to four connections. You can sever spells and effects of 8th level or lower, as well as connections that normally resist ordinary methods of removal. This includes exceptionally powerful curses, effects that specifically prevent themselves from being removed, magically protected memories, Attunement that can't normally be willingly ended, connections created or sustained by an Artifact, curses or magical effects created by an Artifact, and Attunement to an Artifact. Severance doesn't destroy, damage, suppress, or remove the inherent properties of an Artifact; it cuts only the specific connection or effect you choose. If you use Violent Severance after severing four connections, the maximum damage is {@damage 16d10}.

{@b 9th Level.} You can sever up to five connections. You can sever spells and effects of 9th level or lower and eligible connections regardless of protections that would normally prevent their removal. This includes permanent magical effects, Artifact connections, Artifact Attunement, divine curses, divine blessings, divine possession or control, magical bonds directly created by a deity, effects directly sustained by a deity, memories protected by magic of comparable power, and other connections originating from similarly transcendent supernatural sources. Severing a divine connection doesn't harm, weaken, banish, control, or otherwise affect the deity itself; only the chosen connection involving the target is severed. If you use Violent Severance after severing five connections, the maximum damage is {@damage 20d10}.

spell.name: Final Sanctuary
entries: You draw a boundary around a creature and declare that nothing beyond it may claim them.
Blades stop short. Curses lose their path. Hostile magic frays against an unseen edge, unable to complete the final step toward its target.
The protected creature is not hidden, unreachable, or removed from the world.
It is simply denied to hostile intent.

Choose one willing creature you can see within range. For the duration, hostile creatures can't directly affect the target unless they first succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. A creature makes this save each time it attempts to directly affect the protected target. On a failed save, the attempted effect fails against that target.

entries.name: Protected Against
entries: Final Sanctuary can prevent weapon attacks, spell attacks, damaging spells, harmful conditions, curses, forced movement, grapples and restraints, possession, Charm or domination, teleportation imposed by another creature, and any other hostile effect that directly targets or specifically includes the protected creature.
If an effect targets multiple creatures, it can still affect all other targets normally.

entries.name: Area Effects
entries: If a creature attempts to create an area of effect that would include the protected target, that creature must first make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC.

On a failed save, the creature can't place, aim, shape, or direct the effect in a way that would include the protected target. If possible, it must choose a different point, direction, area, or arrangement that excludes the protected target.

If the effect can't be used without including the protected target, the attempted use fails, and any Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, spell slot, charge, or other resource that would have been spent isn't expended.
On a successful save, the effect can include the protected target normally.

entries.name: Indirect Harm
entries: Final Sanctuary doesn't erase consequences already present in the environment. It doesn't prevent a collapsing building from falling, ordinary fire already burning, falling due to destroyed terrain, or being struck by an object that is no longer being magically or deliberately directed at the protected target.
However, if another creature deliberately creates or directs such a hazard specifically to harm the protected target, that creature must make the saving throw before doing so.

entries.name: The Target Can Still Act
entries: The protected creature can attack, cast spells, move, and otherwise act normally. Doing so doesn't end Final Sanctuary.

entries.name: Absolute Refuge
entries: If a creature succeeds on its saving throw against Final Sanctuary, it can affect the protected creature with that one effect only. It must save again for any later hostile action or effect.

spell.name: Grand Design

m.text: a sculpted figure depicting the intended transformation, worth at least 1,000 GP, which the spell consumes

entries: You do not borrow another shape for a moment.
You convince flesh, bone, blood, and living structure that another form is equally natural.
When the working is complete, there is no spell left clinging to the body and no transformation waiting to expire.
What you create becomes flesh. What you change becomes real.

Choose one willing creature you touch. You can choose yourself. Over the course of the casting, you permanently reshape the target's body. The target remains the same creature. Its creature type, personality, memories, class features, ability scores, and other game statistics remain unchanged except where an adaptation granted by this spell specifically changes them.
At 7th level, you can make any number of cosmetic alterations and choose two Major Adaptations.

entries.name: Cosmetic Alterations
entries: You can permanently alter any ordinary physical characteristic that doesn't itself provide a mechanical benefit, including height and weight, facial structure, body proportions, skin, fur, scales, feathers, hair, eye appearance, voice, sex characteristics, horns, fins, decorative tails, apparent age, and other comparable aspects of physical appearance.
Changing apparent age doesn't alter the target's actual age, lifespan, development, or the effects of aging.

entries.name: Repeated Transformation
entries: A creature can be affected by Grand Design any number of times, including the caster. Each casting is permanent and cumulative with previous castings.
Adaptations gained from a new casting don't replace adaptations gained from an earlier casting unless the caster specifically chooses to remove, replace, reshape, or upgrade one of them.
A creature can therefore accumulate additional adaptations through repeated castings of this spell over time.
The same adaptation doesn't normally stack with itself unless that adaptation specifically says it can be chosen more than once.
A later casting using an 8th- or 9th-level spell slot can add Greater or Perfect Adaptations to a creature that was previously altered by a lower-level casting.

entries.name: Major Adaptations
entries: The following adaptations are available when Grand Design is cast using a 7th-level spell slot or higher.

entries.name: Wings
entries: The target permanently grows functional wings and gains a Fly Speed equal to its Speed.

entries.name: Aquatic Adaptation
entries: The target gains a Swim Speed equal to its Speed and can breathe air and water. It also suffers no harmful effects from ordinary underwater pressure.

entries.name: Burrowing Adaptation
entries: The target gains a Burrow Speed equal to half its Speed through earth, sand, clay, and similar natural material. It can't burrow through solid stone or worked structures.

entries.name: Climbing Adaptation
entries: The target gains a Climb Speed equal to its Speed and can move across walls and ceilings without needing to use its hands.

entries.name: Natural Armor
entries: The target develops scales, plates, dense hide, crystalline tissue, barklike growth, or similar protection. While the target isn't wearing armor, its base AC is 13 + its Dexterity modifier.

entries.name: Natural Weapon
entries: The target develops one natural weapon, such as claws, fangs, horns, spines, a tail, or a reinforced limb. It is a Simple Melee weapon with which the target is proficient.
It deals {@damage 1d8} Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, chosen when the adaptation is created. The target can use Strength or Dexterity for its attack and damage rolls with the weapon.

entries.name: Enhanced Senses
entries: The target gains Darkvision 120 feet. If it already has Darkvision, its existing range instead increases by 60 feet.

entries.name: Elemental Resilience
entries: Choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison. The target permanently gains Resistance to the chosen damage type.
This adaptation can be chosen more than once, choosing a different damage type each time.

entries.name: Powerful Build
entries: The target counts as one Size larger when determining its carrying capacity and the weight it can push, drag, or lift.

entries.name: Compression
entries: The target can squeeze through spaces as though it were one Size smaller.

entries.name: Additional Limbs
