entries: The target grows one additional pair of arms, tentacles, or similarly functional appendages. They can hold, carry, manipulate, draw, stow, and interact with objects normally.
They don't grant additional Actions, Bonus Actions, Reactions, or attacks.

entries.name: Prehensile Tail
entries: The target develops a strong prehensile tail or comparable appendage. It can hold and manipulate objects, open doors, retrieve items, and perform other simple object interactions.
The appendage can't wield weapons, use a Shield, or perform Somatic components unless another feature allows it.

entries.name: Leaping Musculature
entries: The target's Long Jump and High Jump distances are tripled. It doesn't need to move 10 feet before making a running jump.
The first 20 feet of any fall are ignored when calculating its falling damage.

entries.name: Amphibious Skin
entries: The target can breathe air and water and can comfortably survive ordinary freshwater, saltwater, and deep-water environments. Unlike Aquatic Adaptation, this adaptation doesn't grant a Swim Speed.

entries.name: Environmental Adaptation
entries: Choose extreme heat or extreme cold. The target automatically succeeds on saving throws and ignores ordinary environmental penalties caused solely by the chosen environment.
This doesn't grant Resistance to Fire or Cold damage.

entries.name: Keen Senses
entries: Choose sight, hearing, or smell. The target has Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks relying on the chosen sense.
This adaptation can be chosen repeatedly for different senses.

entries.name: Venom Gland
entries: The target develops organs capable of producing dangerous venom. Once per turn when the target deals Piercing or Slashing damage with a natural weapon created by this spell, it can deal an additional {@damage 1d6} Poison damage.

entries.name: Adhesive Limbs
entries: The target can adhere to solid surfaces. It can remain attached to walls and ceilings without using its hands.

entries.name: Dense Frame
entries: The target can permanently increase its weight to as much as four times its normal weight without changing Size. It has Advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to resist being pushed, pulled, knocked Prone, or otherwise forcibly moved.

entries.name: Hollow Frame
entries: The target can permanently reduce its weight to as little as one-quarter normal. Falling damage it takes is reduced by an amount equal to five times its Proficiency Bonus.

entries.name: Extended Reach
entries: Choose one pair of limbs or one natural weapon created by Grand Design. Its reach increases by 5 feet.

entries.name: Echolocation
entries: The target gains Blindsight 10 feet while it can hear. This sense doesn't function while the target is Deafened.

entries.name: Photosynthetic Tissue
entries: If the target spends at least 1 hour in bright sunlight during a day, it requires only half as much food that day. This doesn't remove its need for water, air, or rest.

entries.name: 8th-Level Casting
entries: When you cast Grand Design using an 8th-level spell slot, choose three adaptations rather than two. Each choice can be a Major Adaptation or one of the following Greater Adaptations.

entries.name: Blindsight
entries: The target permanently gains Blindsight 60 feet.

entries.name: Greater Wings
entries: The target gains a Fly Speed equal to twice its Speed and can Hover. If it already possesses Wings from this spell, Greater Wings replaces that adaptation.

entries.name: Greater Burrowing
entries: The target gains a Burrow Speed equal to its Speed. It can burrow through natural earth normally and through solid natural stone at half speed. It still can't freely burrow through worked structures.

entries.name: Regenerative Flesh
entries: At the start of each of the target's turns, if it has at least 1 Hit Point and no more than half its Hit Points, it regains Hit Points equal to its Proficiency Bonus.

entries.name: Flexible Anatomy
entries: The target can compress its body enough to pass through an opening as narrow as 6 inches without squeezing. Objects too large to fit through the opening don't compress unless they are physically part of the transformed body.

entries.name: Greater Natural Weapon
entries: Choose one natural weapon created by Grand Design. Its damage die becomes {@damage 2d8} instead of {@damage 1d8}.

entries.name: Greater Resilience
entries: Choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison, Radiant, or Thunder. The target permanently gains Resistance to the chosen damage type.
This adaptation can be chosen repeatedly for different damage types.

entries.name: Mighty Frame
entries: The target can permanently become Large. Its equipment can be reshaped to accommodate its new body as part of the casting. Its statistics don't otherwise change merely because its Size changes.
If the target is already Large or larger, it can instead count as one additional Size larger when determining carrying, pushing, dragging, and lifting capacity.

entries.name: Tremorsense
entries: The target gains Tremorsense 60 feet while it and whatever it is detecting are in contact with the same ground or continuous solid surface.

entries.name: Elastic Anatomy
entries: The target can stretch its limbs and body far beyond their normal proportions. Its reach with unarmed strikes, natural weapons, and object interactions increases by 10 feet. It can extend or retract these structures freely.

entries.name: Chameleon Flesh
entries: The target can alter the color, pattern, and texture of its exterior to match its environment. It has Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
It can also take the Hide action while only Lightly Obscured by natural terrain or environmental features.

entries.name: Reactive Armor
entries: When the target takes Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison damage, it can use its Reaction to gain Resistance to that instance of damage.

entries.name: Venomous Arsenal
entries: Choose one natural weapon created by Grand Design. Once per turn when the target hits with that weapon, it deals an additional {@damage 2d8} Poison damage. When this adaptation is gained, you can choose Acid instead of Poison.

entries.name: Secondary Heart
entries: The target develops redundant circulatory organs. It has Advantage on Constitution saving throws against effects that would cause it to be Paralyzed, Stunned, or Unconscious.

entries.name: Redundant Organs
entries: The target's vital organs are duplicated or distributed through its body. It has Advantage on saving throws against Poison and Disease.
Destroying or removing a single ordinary vital organ does not by itself kill the target.

entries.name: Amphibious Metabolism
entries: The target can hold its breath for 1 hour. If it can already breathe underwater, it no longer needs to breathe while underwater.

entries.name: Thermal Vision
entries: The target gains Darkvision 180 feet. Within 60 feet, it can also perceive creatures through ordinary smoke, mist, steam, and similar atmospheric concealment by detecting heat differences.

entries.name: Shock-Absorbing Body
entries: The target gains Resistance to falling damage and damage caused specifically by collisions or crushing impacts.

entries.name: Reserve Metabolism
entries: The target can survive for 30 days without food and 7 days without water before suffering the normal effects of deprivation. This doesn't prevent Exhaustion from other sources.

entries.name: 9th-Level Casting
entries: When you cast Grand Design using a 9th-level spell slot, choose four adaptations. Each choice can be a Major Adaptation, Greater Adaptation, or one of the following Perfect Adaptations.

entries.name: Truesight
entries: The target permanently gains Truesight 60 feet.

entries.name: Perfect Flight
entries: The target gains a Fly Speed equal to twice its Speed and can Hover. It doesn't fall solely because it becomes Incapacitated while airborne.
If it possesses Wings or Greater Wings from Grand Design, this adaptation replaces them.

entries.name: Greater Regeneration
entries: At the start of each of the target's turns, if it has at least 1 Hit Point, it regains {@dice 2d10} Hit Points.
This replaces Regenerative Flesh rather than stacking with it.

entries.name: Deathless Organs
entries: The target's vital anatomy becomes extraordinarily redundant. It has Advantage on Death Saving Throws.
When it rolls a 19 or 20 on a Death Saving Throw, it gains the benefit normally gained from rolling a 20.
The destruction of an ordinary individual organ doesn't automatically kill it while enough of its body remains functional.

entries.name: Perfect Resilience
entries: Choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison, Radiant, or Thunder. The target permanently gains Immunity to the chosen damage type.
Any Resistance it possesses to that type from Grand Design is replaced by this Immunity. This adaptation can be chosen repeatedly for different damage types.

entries.name: Colossal Anatomy
entries: The target can permanently become Huge. Its equipment can be reshaped to accommodate its body as part of the casting. Its statistics don't otherwise change merely because of its Size.

entries.name: Mutable Flesh
entries: The target gains voluntary control over its alterations from Grand Design. As a Bonus Action, it can alter its cosmetic appearance and retract or manifest physical adaptations granted by this spell, such as wings, natural weapons, additional limbs, tails, horns, and similar external anatomy.
Retracting an adaptation doesn't remove it. The target can manifest it again with another Bonus Action.

entries.name: Perfect Adaptation
entries: Choose two Major Adaptations. Those two adaptations together consume only one adaptation choice from this casting.

entries.name: Universal Respiration
entries: The target no longer needs to breathe. It is therefore unaffected by ordinary suffocation, drowning, smoke inhalation, vacuum, or similar hazards that function solely by preventing respiration.

entries.name: Perfect Metabolism
entries: The target no longer needs ordinary food or water to survive. It can still eat and drink normally. This doesn't remove its need for rest.

entries.name: Perfect Senses
entries: The target gains Darkvision 300 feet, Blindsight 30 feet, and Tremorsense 60 feet.
If it already has one of these senses with a greater range, it retains the greater range.

entries.name: Distributed Mind
entries: The target's nervous system and cognitive functions become distributed throughout its body. It has Advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws against effects that would Charm it, Frighten it, Stun it, or control its actions.
Destroying or removing its head doesn't automatically kill it while enough of the rest of its body remains functional.

entries.name: Perfect Regrowth
entries: If the target loses a limb or other body part, that part naturally regrows after {@dice 1d6} hours, provided the target remains alive.
A severed body part held against its original location can instead reattach over the course of 1 minute.

entries.name: Internal Armory
entries: The target can retract any natural weapon created by Grand Design completely inside its body and manifest it again as a Bonus Action.
Whenever it manifests that weapon, it can change its damage type to Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing.

entries.name: Perfect Camouflage
entries: As a Bonus Action, the target can alter its exterior with such precision that it becomes Invisible until the start of its next turn, until it makes an attack roll, or until it casts a spell.
It can do this a number of times equal to its Proficiency Bonus and regains all expended uses when it finishes a Long Rest.

entries.name: Living Fortress
entries: The target's body becomes extraordinarily resistant to physical harm. While it isn't wearing armor, its base AC is 18. A Shield can modify this AC normally.

entries.name: Perfect Amphibian
entries: The target can survive comfortably in air, water, extreme ocean depths, and vacuum. It suffers no harm from ordinary environmental pressure or lack of atmospheric pressure.
This doesn't provide Resistance or Immunity to magical or supernatural pressure damage.

entries.name: Adaptive Immunity
entries: Whenever the target finishes a Long Rest, choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder. The target gains Immunity to the chosen damage type until it finishes its next Long Rest.
The chosen type can be changed after each Long Rest.

entries.name: Monstrous Reach
entries: Choose one pair of limbs or one natural weapon created by Grand Design. Its reach increases by 15 feet.

entries.name: Independent Limbs
entries: Additional limbs created by Grand Design become capable of extraordinarily precise independent coordination.
Once on each of the target's turns, it can perform one additional object interaction and can draw or stow up to two objects without using an Action.
This doesn't grant an additional Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, or attack.

entries.name: Perfect Compression
entries: The target can compress its body enough to pass through an opening as narrow as 1 inch, regardless of its Size.
Equipment physically incorporated into the target's transformed anatomy compresses with it. Separately carried objects do not.

entries.name: Ageless Body
entries: The target's body no longer physically deteriorates because of aging. Its chronological age continues to increase, but it no longer becomes physically weaker, frailer, or less healthy solely from age.
This adaptation doesn't prevent death from damage, disease, starvation, suffocation, or other causes.

entries.name: Naturalized Form
entries: The alterations created by Grand Design aren't an ongoing spell effect. Once the casting is complete, they become part of the target's actual body.

Dispel Magic can't remove them. An Antimagic Field doesn't suppress them. They don't require Concentration, don't disappear when the caster dies, and physical body parts created by the spell can be injured, severed, healed, or restored like natural body parts.
Magic that restores a lost natural body part can restore one created by this spell. The target is not considered transformed by an ongoing spell merely because its body was altered by Grand Design.
The spell doesn't automatically cause alterations to become hereditary. Whether descendants can inherit them depends on the creature's biology and the setting.

entries.name: Reversal and Further Modification
entries: Another casting of Grand Design can permanently remove, replace, reshape, or upgrade alterations previously created by the spell.
A Wish spell or similarly powerful effect can also restore a creature to an earlier physical form.
There is otherwise no automatic expiration to the transformation.

spell.name: Spellheart

m.text: a flawless gemstone worth at least 2,500 GP, which the spell consumes

entries: Some spells are learned. Others are memorized.
You take a formula and drive it deeper than either, engraving its pattern into the very structure of a living soul.
When the ritual ends, the magic no longer needs a page, a prepared thought, or even the caster who bestowed it.
The spell has become part of the creature itself.

Choose one willing creature you touch throughout the casting and one spell of 3rd level or lower that you know, have prepared, or have recorded in a spellbook you can use. The chosen spell becomes permanently embedded within the target.

entries.name: Innate Spell
entries: The target permanently gains the ability to cast the embedded spell without needing to prepare it or otherwise know it.
When the spell is embedded, choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. The target uses that ability as its spellcasting ability for the embedded spell.

If the target doesn't already have a spell save DC or spell attack modifier using that ability, its spell save DC equals 8 + its Proficiency Bonus + the chosen ability modifier, and its spell attack modifier equals its Proficiency Bonus + the chosen ability modifier.

entries.name: Casting the Embedded Spell
entries: The target can cast the embedded spell once without expending a spell slot and regains this free casting when it finishes a Long Rest. The free casting is cast at the spell's lowest level.
If the target has spell slots, it can also cast the embedded spell using those slots normally. The embedded spell can be upcast normally.

For example, if Spellheart embeds a 3rd-level spell and the target later expends a 6th-level spell slot to cast it, the spell is cast at 6th level and gains any benefits it normally receives from being cast using a higher-level slot.
The target doesn't need to possess the spell on any of its class spell lists to cast it this way.

entries.name: Components
entries: The target must provide the embedded spell's normal Verbal, Somatic, and Material components.
If a Material component has a cost, the target must provide it normally. If the component is consumed, it is consumed normally.

entries.name: Permanent Integration
entries: Spellheart isn't an ongoing magical effect after the ritual is completed. The embedded spell becomes a permanent innate magical capability of the target.
Dispel Magic can't remove it. An Antimagic Field can suppress the casting or effects of the embedded spell normally, but doesn't remove the target's ability to cast it.
The ability remains if the caster of Spellheart dies. Destroying or losing the original spellbook or other source of the embedded spell has no effect.
The target doesn't need to remain near the original caster and retains the embedded spell even if it later changes class or loses access to the spell list from which the spell originally came.

entries.name: Repeated Spellheart
entries: A creature can be affected by Spellheart any number of times. Each casting can embed another spell, and the effects of separate castings are cumulative.
A creature can't gain the same spell more than once from Spellheart. Repeatedly embedding the same spell doesn't grant additional free uses.
There is otherwise no inherent limit to the number of different spells a creature can permanently possess through Spellheart.
The caster can target themself with Spellheart.

entries.name: Replacing or Removing a Spell
entries: When you cast Spellheart on a creature that already possesses one or more spells from Spellheart, you can choose to permanently remove one embedded spell instead of adding a new one.
You can also replace one embedded spell with another spell valid for that casting.
A Wish spell or similarly powerful effect can also remove a spell embedded by Spellheart.

items: {@b 8th Level.} You can embed a spell of 5th level or lower. The target can use the embedded spell's free casting twice per Long Rest instead of once. Both free castings are made at the embedded spell's lowest level. When using a spell slot of its own, the target can still upcast the embedded spell normally.

{@b 9th Level.} You can embed a spell of 7th level or lower. The target can use the embedded spell's free casting three times per Long Rest. All three free castings are made at the embedded spell's lowest level. When using a spell slot of its own, the target can still upcast the embedded spell normally.

spell.name: Soul Anchor

m.text: a specially prepared vessel worth at least 5,000 GP, which the spell consumes when the anchor activates

entries: Death can claim a body only when there is nowhere else for the soul to return.
You prepare such a place in advance, fastening a living creature to a vessel that remembers exactly what it is meant to restore.
When death finally arrives, the bond tears the creature away from its ending and rebuilds what was lost.
The anchor waits for years if necessary. Death only determines when it is used.

Choose one willing living creature you touch and one object within your reach that will serve as its Soul Anchor. When the casting is completed, the target becomes permanently bound to that anchor until the bond is triggered or removed. The target can be you.

entries.name: The Anchor
entries: The chosen object becomes the target's Soul Anchor. It can be almost any nonliving object that can reasonably remain intact, such as a gemstone, statue, sealed urn, weapon, piece of jewelry, book, or specially constructed reliquary.
The anchor doesn't need to remain near the target. The target always knows whether its Soul Anchor still exists and what plane of existence it is on.

entries.name: When the Target Dies
entries: When the target dies, the Soul Anchor activates automatically.

The target's body disappears after 1 minute, along with everything it was wearing or carrying when it died. At the end of that minute, the target reappears alive in the nearest unoccupied space within 5 feet of the Soul Anchor.
The restored creature returns with all its Hit Points, has its missing body parts restored, retains all memories it possessed when it died, and returns with the equipment it possessed when it died.

The creature's spell slots, expended features, charges, and other resources remain exactly as they were when it died. Conditions or effects that ended only because the creature died don't automatically return unless their own rules say otherwise.
The Soul Anchor is then consumed, ending the spell.

entries.name: Forced Return
entries: The restoration doesn't require the creature to be willing at the moment of death.
Effects that normally require a soul to be free or willing to return don't prevent Soul Anchor from functioning.

If the creature's soul or consciousness has been trapped, imprisoned, consumed, or otherwise prevented from existing independently, the Anchor attempts to reclaim it as part of the restoration. A sufficiently powerful effect can still prevent this, as determined by the DM.

entries.name: Destruction of the Anchor
entries: If the Soul Anchor is destroyed before the target dies, the spell ends without triggering. Destroying the anchor doesn't harm the target.

entries.name: No Distance Limit
entries: The target and its Soul Anchor can be any distance apart, including on different planes of existence. Distance doesn't weaken the bond.

entries.name: Recasting Soul Anchor
entries: A creature can have only one Soul Anchor created by this spell at a time.
Casting Soul Anchor on a creature that already has one replaces the previous bond. The old anchor immediately ceases to function as a Soul Anchor but isn't otherwise harmed.

items: {@b 8th Level.} The Soul Anchor activates immediately when the target dies instead of after 1 minute. The target can also choose whether its equipment returns with it or remains where it died.

{@b 9th Level.} The Soul Anchor isn't consumed when it activates. After restoring the target, it becomes dormant until the target finishes 7 Long Rests, after which it can activate again. A 9th-level Soul Anchor can therefore restore the same creature repeatedly as long as the anchor itself survives.

spell.name: Martial Incarnation
entries: Spellcraft abandons quill and gesture for steel and discipline.
Armor closes around your body, weapons answer your grasp, and instincts never trained become immediate and natural.
For a fleeting span, magic compresses years of martial mastery into a single transformation.
With greater power, flesh becomes weapon, armor becomes legend, and the mage becomes war given form.
You transform yourself into a supernatural martial combatant and manifest magical armaments as part of the transformation.
This spell doesn't require Concentration.
When cast using a higher-level spell slot, you gain all benefits provided by lower-level castings unless a higher-level benefit explicitly replaces one of them.

entries.name: Martial Armament
entries: When you cast the spell, you can manifest up to two pieces of equipment, choosing separately from the following:

items: One Simple or Martial Melee Weapon.
One Simple or Martial Ranged Weapon.
One Shield.
One suit of Light Armor.
One suit of Medium Armor.
One suit of Heavy Armor.

entries: The equipment appears already held, worn, or equipped by you as appropriate.
Armor and Shields manifested by the spell are donned instantly.
Every weapon, suit of armor, and Shield created by this spell is magical from the moment it manifests.
All manifested equipment disappears when the spell ends.

entries.name: Incarnation Enhancement
entries: Every weapon, suit of armor, and Shield manifested by this spell gains a magical enhancement based on the spell slot used.
A manifested weapon adds the bonus to its attack and damage rolls.
Manifested armor adds the bonus to its AC.
A manifested Shield grants its normal +2 AC plus the Incarnation Enhancement.
Special Incarnate Armaments use the same Incarnation Enhancement.

entries.name: Martial Mastery
entries: For the duration, you have proficiency with all Simple Weapons, all Martial Weapons, Light Armor, Medium Armor, Heavy Armor, and Shields.
You ignore the Strength requirement of armor manifested by this spell.
You can use Strength, Dexterity, or your spellcasting ability for attack and damage rolls made with weapons manifested by this spell. You choose separately for each attack.

entries.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: You can use the Weapon Mastery property of every weapon manifested by this spell.
Whenever you manifest a weapon, you can replace its normal Mastery property with one of the following: Cleave, Graze, Nick, Push, Sap, Slow, Topple, or Vex.
For purposes of Martial Incarnation, you don't need to satisfy the normal weapon prerequisite for the chosen Mastery.

entries.name: Warrior's Form
entries: When you cast the spell, choose Strength or Dexterity.
If the chosen score is lower than 16, it becomes 16 for the duration.
You also gain Temporary Hit Points equal to 5 + your spellcasting ability modifier.
Any Temporary Hit Points remaining from this spell disappear when the spell ends.

entries.name: Living Weapon
entries: Your body itself can serve as one of your manifested weapons.
For the duration, your Unarmed Strikes are magical and deal {@damage 1d8} Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, chosen for each attack.
You can use Strength, Dexterity, or your spellcasting ability for their attack and damage rolls.
Your Unarmed Strikes add your Incarnation Enhancement to their attack and damage rolls and count as Martial Weapons for features granted by this spell.
Whenever you make an Unarmed Strike, you can give it one of these Masteries: Graze, Push, Sap, Slow, Topple, or Vex.
The strike can appear as an ordinary punch, kick, elbow, knee, headbutt, or another martial motion. The spell doesn't need to visibly transform your body unless you choose it to.

entries.name: Unarmored Incarnation
entries: While you aren't wearing armor, your base AC becomes 13 + your Dexterity modifier or spellcasting ability modifier + your Incarnation Enhancement.
Choose Dexterity or your spellcasting ability when you cast the spell.
You can use a Shield with this AC unless another feature specifically requires you to be completely unarmored and unshielded.

entries.name: 2nd-Level Slot — Complete Armament
entries: You can manifest up to three pieces of equipment.
The ability chosen for Warrior's Form becomes 17 if lower.
Choose one Fighting Style for the duration:

items: {@b Archery.} You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls made with Ranged weapons.
{@b Defense.} While wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.
{@b Dueling.} While wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.
{@b Great Weapon Fighting.} When you roll a 1 on a damage die for an attack made with a melee weapon you are wielding with two hands, treat the roll as a 2.
{@b Two-Weapon Fighting.} When you make the additional attack granted by fighting with two Light weapons, you can add your ability modifier to its damage.
{@b Unarmed Fighting.} Your Unarmed Strike damage becomes {@damage 1d10} while you aren't wielding a weapon or Shield.

entries.name: 3rd-Level Slot — Warrior Incarnate
entries: You can manifest up to four pieces of equipment.
The ability chosen for Warrior's Form becomes 18 if lower.
When you take the Attack action, you can attack twice instead of once.
Your Temporary Hit Points from the spell instead equal 10 + twice your spellcasting ability modifier.

entries.name: Martial Body
entries: Your Unarmed Strike damage becomes {@damage 1d10} whether or not you wield other equipment.
While you aren't wearing armor, you gain an additional +1 AC.
Standing from Prone costs only 5 feet of movement, and your jump distance doubles.

entries.name: Fluid Mastery
entries: Before each attack with a manifested weapon or Unarmed Strike, you can change its chosen Mastery property, no action required.

entries.name: Arcsteel Blade
entries: {@i Martial Melee Weapon}
{@b Damage:} {@damage 1d10} Slashing
{@b Properties:} Finesse, Versatile ({@damage 1d12})
Before each attack, you can choose for the blade to deal Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage.

entries.name: 5th Level — Adaptive Edge
entries: You can additionally choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage.
The blade visibly changes its structure to reflect its current damage type.

entries.name: 7th Level — Perfect Edge
entries: Its weapon damage becomes {@damage 2d10}.
After you know whether an attack hits, but before dealing damage, you can choose the attack's damage type.
The attack ignores Resistance to that damage type.

entries.name: 9th Level — Absolute Edge
entries: Its weapon damage becomes {@damage 4d8}.
You can choose any damage type before dealing damage.
Its attacks ignore Resistance, and Immunity to the chosen damage type is treated as Resistance.

entries.name: Warcaster Spear
entries: {@i Martial Melee Weapon}
{@b Damage:} {@damage 1d8} Piercing
{@b Properties:} Reach, Thrown (30/120), Versatile ({@damage 1d10})
Immediately after making a thrown attack with the spear, it returns to your hand.

entries.name: 5th Level — Piercing Flight
entries: Its thrown range becomes 120/360.
After hitting a target with a thrown attack, you can make another attack with the same throw against one creature directly behind the first target.

entries.name: 7th Level — Transfix
entries: Its weapon damage becomes {@damage 2d8}.
When you hit a creature, you can attempt to pin it to a surface within 10 feet behind it.
The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or have Speed 0 until it uses an Action to free itself.

entries.name: 9th Level — World Lance
entries: Its weapon damage becomes {@damage 4d8}, and its thrown range becomes Sight.
Once on each of your turns, when you throw the spear, it can continue through every creature and object intersecting a straight line from you. Make a separate attack roll against each target.

entries.name: Spellbow
entries: {@i Martial Ranged Weapon}
{@b Damage:} {@damage 1d10} Piercing
{@b Properties:} Heavy, Two-Handed
The weapon creates its own magical ammunition.

entries.name: 5th Level — Shaped Ammunition
entries: Before each attack, choose one:

items: {@b Piercing Arrow.} The attack ignores Half Cover.
{@b Burst Arrow.} On a hit, creatures of your choice within 5 feet of the target take damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
{@b Binding Arrow.} On a hit, the target's Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: 7th Level — Spellshot
entries: Its weapon damage becomes {@damage 2d10}, and its range becomes 300/1,200.
Before each attack, choose Piercing, Force, or Radiant damage.

entries.name: 9th Level — Arcane Ballista
entries: Its weapon damage becomes {@damage 4d8}, and its range becomes Sight.
You can apply two different Shaped Ammunition options to each attack.

entries.name: 4th-Level Slot — Martial Discipline
entries: You can manifest up to five pieces of equipment.
Choose one Martial Discipline for the duration:

items: {@b Assault.} Every time you hit with a weapon attack or Unarmed Strike, the attack deals an additional {@damage 1d8} damage of its damage type.
{@b Guardian.} While wielding a Shield, you gain an additional +1 AC. Creatures provoke Opportunity Attacks from you even when they take the Disengage action.
{@b Skirmisher.} Your Speed increases by 10 feet. Opportunity Attacks against you have Disadvantage.
{@b Executioner.} Your weapon attacks and Unarmed Strikes score a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20.
{@b Pugilist.} Whenever you hit with an Unarmed Strike, you can immediately attempt to Grapple or Shove the target as part of the same attack.
{@b Counterfighter.} When a creature within your reach misses you with a melee attack, you can use your Reaction to make one Unarmed Strike against it.
{@b Iron Body.} While wearing no armor and wielding no Shield, you gain an additional +2 AC.
{@b Flowing Form.} While you aren't wearing armor, your Speed increases by 15 feet. Moving through the space of a creature at least one Size larger than you doesn't cost extra movement.

entries.name: Bastion Plate
entries: {@i Heavy Armor}
{@b Base AC:} 18
You have Advantage on checks and saving throws made to resist being pushed, pulled, knocked Prone, or moved against your will.
Its Incarnation Enhancement is added normally.

entries.name: Aegis Shield
entries: {@i Shield}
The Shield grants its normal +2 AC plus its Incarnation Enhancement.
When you take damage, you can use your Reaction to reduce that damage by {@damage 1d10} + your spellcasting ability modifier.

entries.name: Skirmisher Mail
entries: {@i Medium Armor}
{@b Base AC:} 15 + Dexterity modifier, maximum +3
It doesn't impose Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
Your Speed increases by 5 feet.

entries.name: 5th-Level Slot — Veteran Armament
entries: There is no longer a limit on the number of weapons you can manifest. You can still maintain only one suit of armor and one Shield.
The ability chosen for Warrior's Form becomes 19 if lower.
You gain proficiency in Strength and Constitution saving throws.

entries.name: Veteran Strike
entries: Every time you hit with a manifested weapon or Unarmed Strike, the attack deals an additional {@damage 2d8} damage of the attack's damage type.
Veteran Strike replaces Assault's additional damage.

entries.name: Instant Arsenal
entries: Before or after any attack, you can replace one manifested weapon with another weapon available to this spell, no action required.

entries.name: Greater Living Weapon
entries: Your Unarmed Strike damage becomes {@damage 2d6}.
You can choose Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, or Force damage for each strike.

entries.name: Crushing Hold
entries: At the start of each of your turns, choose one creature you are Grappling.
It takes {@damage 2d8} + the ability modifier used for the Grapple as Bludgeoning or Force damage, your choice.

entries.name: Colossus Blade
entries: {@i Martial Melee Weapon}
{@b Damage:} {@damage 2d8}
{@b Properties:} Heavy, Two-Handed, Reach
Choose Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage whenever you manifest it.

entries.name: 7th Level — Titanic Reach
entries: Its damage becomes {@damage 2d10}.
Each time you hit with it during your turn, its Reach increases by 5 feet until the end of that turn.

entries.name: 9th Level — Colossal Sweep
entries: Its damage becomes {@damage 4d10}.
Once on each of your turns, instead of attacking a single target, you can make one attack roll and compare it against the AC of every creature of your choice within the weapon's current reach.
Each creature hit takes the attack's full damage.

entries.name: Twinblade
entries: {@i Martial Melee Weapon}
{@b Damage:} {@damage 1d8} Slashing
{@b Properties:} Finesse, Light
When you take the Attack action and attack with Twinblade, you can make one additional Twinblade attack as a Bonus Action.

entries.name: 7th Level — Accelerating Blades
entries: Its weapon damage becomes {@damage 2d6}.
Each consecutive Twinblade hit against the same creature during your turn gains a cumulative +1 bonus to its attack and damage rolls.

entries.name: 9th Level — Infinite Combination
entries: Its weapon damage becomes {@damage 3d6}.
The first additional Twinblade attack you make on each of your turns requires no Bonus Action.
Whenever you score a Critical Hit with Twinblade, you can immediately make one additional Twinblade attack.

entries.name: Siege Bow
entries: {@i Martial Ranged Weapon}
{@b Damage:} {@damage 2d8} Piercing
{@b Properties:} Heavy, Two-Handed
The weapon creates its own magical ammunition.
Its attacks deal double damage to objects and structures.

entries.name: 7th Level — Siege Charge
entries: When you hit, you can delay that attack's damage until the end of your turn.
Multiple delayed hits can be stored in the same target.
At the end of your turn, all stored Siege Charges detonate, dealing their stored damage separately.

entries.name: 9th Level — Fortress Breaker
entries: Its weapon damage becomes {@damage 4d10} Force or Piercing, chosen for each attack.
It deals triple damage to objects and structures.
It can directly damage magical barriers, Force constructions, conjured structures, and similar manifestations.

entries.name: 6th-Level Slot — Relentless Warrior
entries: The ability chosen for Warrior's Form becomes 20 if lower.
You gain Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.
When damage would reduce you to 0 Hit Points but not kill you outright, you can drop to 1 Hit Point instead. Once this occurs, it can't occur again during that casting.

entries.name: Adamant Body
entries: While you aren't wearing armor, you have Advantage on checks and saves made to resist being Grappled, Shoved, physically Restrained, or forcibly moved.

entries.name: Barehanded Deflection
entries: When you are hit by a weapon attack, you can use your Reaction to reduce its damage by {@damage 2d10} + your spellcasting ability modifier + your character level.
If this reduces the damage to 0 and the attacker is within your Unarmed Strike reach, you can immediately make one Unarmed Strike against it.

entries.name: Spellbreaker
entries: {@i Martial Melee Weapon}
{@b Damage:} {@damage 2d8} Force
{@b Properties:} Finesse
When you damage a creature that is concentrating, it has Disadvantage on its Constitution saving throw to maintain Concentration against that damage.
Spellbreaker can damage magical barriers, Force manifestations, and magical constructions.

entries.name: 7th Level — Interdict
entries: When a creature within your reach casts a spell, you can use your Reaction to attack it with Spellbreaker before the spell resolves.
On a hit, the creature makes a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC.
On a failed save, the spell fails, while the spell slot and any expended components are still consumed.

entries.name: 9th Level — Devour the Formula
entries: Its weapon damage becomes {@damage 4d8} Force.
Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature affected by a spell, you can attempt to end one spell affecting it as though using {@spell Dispel Magic}, using your spellcasting ability.
If you successfully end the spell, your next Spellbreaker hit before the end of your next turn deals an additional {@damage 3d10} Force damage.

entries.name: Juggernaut Plate
entries: {@i Heavy Armor}
{@b Base AC:} 19
Your Speed isn't reduced by this armor.
While wearing it, Difficult Terrain doesn't cost extra movement.
You count as one Size larger for carrying, pushing, dragging, and lifting.
You count as one Size larger when determining what creatures you can Grapple or Shove.

entries.name: Guardian Aegis
entries: {@i Shield}
In addition to its normal AC bonus and Incarnation Enhancement, creatures of your choice within 5 feet of you have Half Cover while you wield this Shield.

entries.name: 7th-Level Slot — Master of Arms
entries: When you take the Attack action, you can make three attacks instead of two.

entries.name: Master Strike
entries: Every time you hit with a manifested weapon or Unarmed Strike, the attack deals an additional {@damage 3d8} damage.
Master Strike replaces Veteran Strike.

entries.name: Master of Technique
entries: Whenever you hit with a manifested weapon, you can apply two different Weapon Mastery properties to the attack.
An individual Mastery can't be applied twice to the same attack.
Your Unarmed Strikes can likewise apply two different Masteries from their available list.

entries.name: Master of the Body
entries: Your Unarmed Strike damage becomes {@damage 2d8}.
Your Unarmed Strike reach increases by 5 feet.
Once during each of your turns, before or after an Unarmed Strike, you can move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

entries.name: Throw
entries: When you successfully Grapple or Shove a creature, you can instead throw it up to 20 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
The creature falls Prone.
If it collides with a creature or solid object, both take {@damage 3d8} Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Severing Edge
entries: {@i Martial Melee Weapon}
{@b Damage:} {@damage 2d10} Force
{@b Properties:} Finesse, Reach
Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature, you can sever one of the following until the start of your next turn:

items: A telepathic connection.
A magical tether.
A Shared Damage or Shared Hit Point connection.
A creature's connection to a summoned creature it controls.
A supernatural link allowing another creature to perceive through it.
A magical control connection between the target and another creature.

entries: If none applies, the attack instead deals an additional {@damage 3d10} Force damage.

entries.name: 8th Level — Deeper Severance
entries: Its weapon damage becomes {@damage 3d10} Force.
You can additionally interrupt possession, teleportation links, shared magical effects, supernatural command bonds, and other comparable active connections.

entries.name: 9th Level — Cut the Connection
entries: Its weapon damage becomes {@damage 4d10} Force.
A connection you sever remains interrupted until the end of your next turn instead of the start.

entries.name: Meteor Hammer
entries: {@i Martial Melee Weapon}
{@b Damage:} {@damage 2d10} Bludgeoning
{@b Properties:} Heavy, Two-Handed
Whenever you hit a Large or smaller creature, you can push it up to 10 feet.
On a Critical Hit, it also falls Prone.

entries.name: 8th Level — Meteor Impact
entries: Its damage becomes {@damage 3d10}.
You can push a creature up to 15 feet on every hit.

entries.name: 9th Level — Falling Heaven
entries: Its weapon damage becomes {@damage 4d12} Bludgeoning.
Once on each of your turns when you hit, choose a point on the ground within 10 feet of the target.
A 20-foot-radius shockwave erupts there. Other creatures in the area make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC.
On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 4d10} Bludgeoning damage, falls Prone, and is pushed 15 feet away from the impact. On a successful save, it takes half damage and suffers no other effect.

entries.name: Horizon Bow
entries: {@i Martial Ranged Weapon}
{@b Damage:} {@damage 2d10} Piercing
{@b Properties:} Heavy, Two-Handed
The weapon creates its own ammunition.
Its attacks ignore Half Cover and Three-Quarters Cover.
Long range doesn't impose Disadvantage.

entries.name: 8th Level — Beyond the Horizon
entries: Its range becomes Sight.
Cover short of Total Cover grants no benefit against its attacks.

entries.name: 9th Level — Unerring Horizon
entries: Its weapon damage becomes {@damage 4d10} Piercing or Force.
Once on each of your turns, you can make one Horizon Bow attack with Advantage, regardless of distance.

entries.name: 8th-Level Slot — Legendary Combatant
entries: You gain two Martial Disciplines instead of one.
You gain one additional Reaction each round, regained at the start of each of your turns.
That additional Reaction can be used only for an Opportunity Attack, a defensive feature granted by this spell, or a feature of this spell triggered by another creature attacking or moving.
Your weapon attacks and Unarmed Strikes score a Critical Hit on 19–20. If you have Executioner, they instead score a Critical Hit on 18–20.

entries.name: Legendary Strike
entries: Every hit with a manifested weapon or Unarmed Strike deals an additional {@damage 4d8} damage.
Legendary Strike replaces Master Strike.

entries.name: Legendary Panoply
entries: At any point during your turn, you can freely change your manifested weapons, manifested Shield, or manifested armor, no action required.

entries.name: Legendary Body
entries: Your Unarmed Strike damage becomes {@damage 3d8}.

While wearing no armor and wielding no Shield, you gain an additional +3 AC, Critical Hits against you become normal hits, you can't be knocked Prone against your will while conscious, and your Speed increases by another 10 feet.

entries.name: Empty-Hand Counter
entries: When a creature within your Unarmed Strike reach attacks you, leaves your reach, attempts to Grapple you, or attempts to move you against your will, you can use a Reaction to make one Unarmed Strike against it before the triggering effect resolves.
If the attack hits, you can immediately attempt to Grapple or Shove it.

entries.name: Riftblade
entries: {@i Martial Melee Weapon}
{@b Damage:} {@damage 3d8} Force
{@b Properties:} Finesse
You can make melee weapon attacks with Riftblade against a target you can see within 30 feet. The blade cuts the intervening distance rather than traveling through it.

entries.name: 9th Level — Spatial Dominion
entries: Its weapon damage becomes {@damage 4d8} Force, and its range becomes 120 feet.
Whenever you hit, choose one:

items: {@b Fold.} You appear in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the target.
{@b Displace.} Move the target up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
{@b Rend.} The target suffers a spatial wound until the start of your next turn. If it teleports during that time, it takes {@damage 4d10} Force damage immediately after arriving.

entries.name: Starfall Bow
entries: {@i Martial Ranged Weapon}
{@b Damage:} {@damage 3d8} Radiant or Force
{@b Properties:} Heavy, Two-Handed
Choose Radiant or Force damage for each attack.
The weapon creates its own ammunition.
Its attacks ignore Half Cover and Three-Quarters Cover, and long range doesn't impose Disadvantage.

entries.name: 9th Level — Celestial Barrage
entries: Its weapon damage becomes {@damage 4d8}.
Once on each of your turns when you hit, you can call down a barrage centered on the target.
Creatures of your choice within 20 feet of it make a Dexterity saving throw.
On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 4d12} Radiant or Force damage, your choice. On a success, it takes half damage.
The primary target isn't affected by this additional burst.

entries.name: Fortress Plate
entries: {@i Heavy Armor}
{@b Base AC:} 20
While wearing it, you have Advantage on Strength and Constitution saving throws.
You can't be moved against your will while conscious unless you choose to be.
Critical Hits against you become normal hits.

entries.name: Mirror Aegis
entries: {@i Shield}
When a creature within 60 feet misses you with an attack, you can use your Reaction to cause the Shield to retaliate.
The attacker takes {@damage 2d10} Force damage.

entries.name: 9th-Level Slot — Perfect Martial Incarnation
entries: Your Strength and Dexterity scores both become 22 if lower.
When you take the Attack action, you can make four attacks.
You gain all Martial Disciplines.

entries.name: Perfect Mastery
entries: Before or after making an attack roll with a manifested weapon, you can freely choose its Mastery properties.
When an attack hits, you can apply up to three different Mastery properties to it.
Your Unarmed Strikes can likewise apply up to three different available Unarmed Masteries.

entries.name: Perfect Panoply
entries: You can simultaneously maintain one suit of armor, one Shield, and any number of manifested weapons.
Weapons not currently wielded can remain suspended within your Martial Incarnation and appear directly in an empty hand whenever you wish, no action required.
Every manifested piece has a +6 Incarnation Enhancement.

entries.name: Apex Strike
entries: Every time you hit with a manifested weapon or Unarmed Strike, the attack deals an additional {@damage 5d8} damage.
Apex Strike replaces Assault, Veteran Strike, Master Strike, and Legendary Strike.

entries.name: Unbroken Warrior
entries: At the start of each of your turns, if you have at least 1 Hit Point, you regain {@damage 2d10} Hit Points.

entries.name: Perfect Technique
entries: Once on each of your turns when you miss with a weapon attack or Unarmed Strike, you can cause that attack to hit instead.

entries.name: Unyielding
entries: Whenever you fail a Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution saving throw, you can reroll it. You must use the new roll.

entries.name: Perfect Living Weapon
entries: Your Unarmed Strike damage becomes {@damage 4d8}.
Choose Bludgeoning, Force, Piercing, Radiant, Slashing, or Thunder damage for each attack.

entries.name: Perfect Empty Hand
entries: While wearing no armor and wielding neither a weapon nor Shield, your base AC becomes 18 + your Dexterity modifier or spellcasting ability modifier + your Incarnation Enhancement.
Your Speed increases by 30 feet.
Your Unarmed Strike reach increases by 10 feet.
You can move across liquids and vertical surfaces during your turn without falling during that movement.
You can't be forcibly moved or knocked Prone while conscious unless you choose to be.
You can Grapple creatures of any Size.
Your Unarmed Strikes ignore Resistance, and Immunity to their damage is treated as Resistance.

entries.name: Heavenbreaker
entries: Once on each of your turns, before making an Unarmed Strike, you can declare it a Heavenbreaker.
On a hit, the attack deals an additional {@damage 4d12} Force damage.
A Heavenbreaker ignores Resistance and Immunity to all damage dealt by the attack.
It can damage creatures, objects, structures, magical barriers, Force effects, supernatural manifestations, magical prisons, seals, conjured terrain, and similar effects.
It can damage something described as indestructible, immune to all damage, or normally incapable of taking damage.
It doesn't require any particular weapon, material, spell, damage type, Artifact, alignment, creature type, or other special method to harm its target.
Its damage can't be redirected to another target in place of the thing struck.

entries.name: Break the Unbreakable
entries: If the target has Hit Points, Heavenbreaker damages those Hit Points normally.
If something lacks AC or Hit Points specifically because it normally can't be damaged, Heavenbreaker makes it damageable.
The DM assigns it appropriate AC and Hit Points based on its scale and power, after which it can be destroyed through sufficient damage.
Heavenbreaker doesn't automatically destroy such a target; it makes destruction possible.

entries.name: Godslayer
entries: {@i Martial Melee Weapon}
{@b Damage:} {@damage 4d8}
{@b Properties:} Finesse, Reach
Before each attack, choose any damage type.
Godslayer's attacks ignore Resistance and Immunity to their damage.
They ignore requirements for a specific weapon, material, damage type, spell, alignment, Artifact, or other special means of harming a creature.
They can harm creatures that would otherwise be impossible to damage by conventional means.

entries.name: Mortal Principle
entries: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with Godslayer, choose one defensive feature possessed by that creature.
Until the start of your next turn, that feature doesn't function against you.

Examples include Regeneration, Damage Resistance, Damage Immunity, Legendary Resistance, damage reduction, a feature preventing death at 0 Hit Points, or a feature limiting how much damage the creature can take from an attack or turn.
The feature isn't removed from the creature and continues functioning against everyone else.

entries.name: Worldpiercer
entries: {@i Martial Ranged Weapon}
{@b Damage:} {@damage 4d8} Force
{@b Range:} Sight
{@b Properties:} Heavy, Two-Handed
Worldpiercer creates its own ammunition.

entries.name: Penetration
entries: Its projectile doesn't stop after striking its first target.
When you attack, choose a straight line extending from you through the original target.
Make a separate attack roll against every creature, object, barrier, and structure intersected by that line.
There is no inherent limit on the number of targets the projectile can strike.

entries.name: Worldline Shot
entries: Once on each of your turns, you can designate one Worldpiercer attack as a Worldline Shot.

For that attack, Resistance and Immunity don't reduce its damage, normally indestructible obstacles can be damaged, and the projectile continues along its line as long as it successfully penetrates or destroys enough of each obstacle to continue.
Worldpiercer doesn't simply ignore everything between you and your target. It shoots through it.

entries.name: Invincible Panoply
entries: {@i Heavy Armor}
{@b Base AC:} 21
With its +6 Incarnation Enhancement, its AC becomes 27.
While wearing it, Critical Hits against you become normal hits.
You can't be forcibly moved or knocked Prone while conscious unless you choose to be.
You have Advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saving throws.
You have Resistance to Force damage.
Your Speed can't be reduced below half its normal value.

entries.name: Absolute Aegis
entries: {@i Shield}
The Shield grants its normal +2 AC plus its +6 Incarnation Enhancement, for +8 AC total.
When you are hit by an attack or fail a Dexterity saving throw, you can use your Reaction and choose one:

items: {@b Deflect.} The triggering attack misses you instead.
{@b Shelter.} You succeed on the triggering Dexterity saving throw instead.

entries: Once you use either option, you can't use Absolute Aegis this way again until the start of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Gate
entries: You possess a key to doors that were never built.
You create a supernatural object called your Gate Key. It can take any form you choose—a key, coin, card, ring, shard, or similar Tiny object.
If the Gate Key is lost or destroyed, you can recreate it during a Short or Long Rest, causing the previous Gate Key to disappear.

entries.name: Open the Way
entries: As a Bonus Action while holding your Gate Key, choose an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet.
You create two linked gateways: one in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you and one at the chosen destination. Each gateway is a vertical opening up to 5 feet wide and 10 feet tall.
The gateways last until the start of your next turn. A creature or object entering one gateway immediately exits the other, preserving its direction and momentum.
Passing through a gateway isn't considered teleportation.

entries.name: Reach Through
entries: You can see and hear through either gateway.
You can make attacks, cast spells, interact with objects, and move through the gateways using normal movement.
Distance measured through the gateways is measured from one opening to the other as though the two openings were adjacent.

entries.name: Moving Gate
entries: Once on each of your turns while the gateways exist, you can move either gateway up to 10 feet to another unoccupied space you can see. This requires no action.

items: {@b Level 5.} The maximum distance of Open the Way increases to 60 feet.
{@b Level 11.} The maximum distance increases to 120 feet, and the gateways can also be horizontal.

{@b Level 17.} The maximum distance increases to 300 feet. You create three gateways instead of two, and any gateway can connect to either of the others. A creature entering a gateway chooses which other gateway it exits from.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Mirror
entries: Your reflection has learned that it need not remain on the other side of the glass.
You create a supernatural Pact Mirror, a Tiny reflective object whose appearance you choose, such as a hand mirror, polished coin, crystal shard, metal plate, or glass eye.
If it is lost or destroyed, you can recreate it during a Short or Long Rest, causing the previous Pact Mirror to disappear.

entries.name: Living Reflection
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can cause your reflection to step out of the Pact Mirror and appear in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet.

The reflection looks and sounds exactly like you, occupies its space, has your Size, is intangible, can't attack, manipulate objects, or directly affect creatures, and has a Speed equal to your Speed.
It can move through creatures and objects as Difficult Terrain and disappears if it ends its turn inside an object.
You can have only one Living Reflection at a time. It lasts until dismissed, you create another, you become Incapacitated, or it is more than 300 feet away from you.

entries.name: Borrowed Position
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can instantly exchange positions with your Living Reflection.
This movement isn't teleportation. Your body and the reflection simply exchange which position each occupies.
You can use Borrowed Position a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Mirror Casting
entries: When you cast a spell or use an ability that originates from you, you can choose for it to originate from your space or your Living Reflection's space.
You still make all attacks, choose all targets, and provide all components normally. Range is measured from the chosen origin.
The reflection itself isn't considered the caster or user of the effect.

entries.name: False Target
entries: When a creature you can see targets you with an attack, you can use your Reaction to exchange places with your Living Reflection immediately before the attack is resolved.
The attack then targets whichever of you now occupies your former space.
Because the reflection is intangible, an attack directed at it automatically misses unless the effect can affect incorporeal magical manifestations.
Using False Target expends one use of Borrowed Position.

entries.name: Through the Looking Glass
entries: While your Living Reflection exists, you can see and hear from its space in addition to your own.
You can perceive through it even if you don't have line of sight to it, provided it remains within 300 feet of you.

items: {@b Level 5.} Your Living Reflection can exist up to 1 mile from you.
{@b Level 11.} You can maintain two Living Reflections simultaneously. When using Borrowed Position or Mirror Casting, choose either reflection.
{@b Level 17.} You can maintain three Living Reflections, and once on each of your turns you can exchange positions with one of them without expending a use of Borrowed Position.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Arsenal
entries: You carry no arsenal upon your back. Steel, ammunition, and instruments of battle wait beyond ordinary space for the instant you call.
Every weapon entrusted to the Arsenal remembers your hand.
Disarm you, and another blade appears. Empty your quiver, and another arrow is already nocked.
So long as the Arsenal answers, you are never truly unarmed.
You possess a supernatural extradimensional armory called your Arsenal.

entries.name: Bound Arsenal
entries: During a Short or Long Rest, you can place any number of weapons, shields, ammunition, spellcasting focuses, and tools you are touching into the Arsenal.
You can also place an eligible object into the Arsenal as a Bonus Action while holding it.

An object stored there has no weight or bulk for you, is inaccessible to other creatures through ordinary means, doesn't age, rust, decay, or deteriorate while stored, retains its magical properties, charges, and other characteristics, and remains attuned to its current wielder if storing it wouldn't normally end that Attunement.
You always know every object currently stored in your Arsenal. There is no inherent limit to the number of eligible objects it can contain.

entries.name: Call to Hand
entries: Once on each of your turns, you can summon one stored object directly into an empty hand without using an action.
You can simultaneously return one eligible object you are holding to the Arsenal.
If you have no free hand, you can instead cause the summoned object to appear in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you.

entries.name: Instant Exchange
entries: Whenever you make an attack with a weapon from your Arsenal, you can return it and summon another stored weapon into the same hand before or after that attack, no action required.
You can therefore wield different weapons for different attacks made during the same turn.

entries.name: Unbroken Armament
entries: A weapon from your Arsenal recognizes you as its intended wielder. While you wield it, you are proficient with it and you can't be unwillingly disarmed of it unless you are Incapacitated.
If it leaves your grasp unwillingly, you can immediately return it to the Arsenal, no action required.
A weapon you throw can return to the Arsenal immediately after the attack resolves.
This doesn't override an Artifact or another item's property that specifically determines who can wield or possess it.

entries.name: Arsenal Ammunition
entries: Ammunition stored in the Arsenal can appear directly inside a weapon as part of loading or firing that weapon.
You don't need a free hand to retrieve ammunition from the Arsenal.
After ammunition from the Arsenal hits or misses, you can cause it to return to the Arsenal at the end of the turn if it still exists.

entries.name: Familiar Grip
entries: While wielding a weapon from your Arsenal, you can use Strength or Dexterity for its attack and damage rolls, regardless of which ability that weapon normally uses.
This doesn't change any other property of the weapon.

entries.name: Level 5 — Awakened Arsenal
entries: Every weapon in your Arsenal is considered magical while you wield it.
Whenever you summon a weapon using Call to Hand, you can immediately alter its handling until it leaves your grasp. Choose one of the following options:

items: {@b Swift.} If the weapon lacks the Finesse property, it gains Finesse.
{@b Far-Reaching.} If it is a melee weapon, its reach increases by 5 feet.
{@b Returning.} If it has the Thrown property, its normal and long ranges are doubled, and it returns to your hand immediately after the attack.
{@b Unburdened.} The weapon loses the Heavy property for you.

entries: You choose again whenever that weapon is summoned.

entries.name: Level 11 — Arsenal Without Pause
entries: You can summon or return any number of objects from your Arsenal during your turn, provided each exchange occurs immediately before or after you make an attack, cast a spell, or interact with an object.

You can summon or dismiss a Shield as part of these exchanges. Changing weapons never interferes with making multiple attacks. A weapon you summon is immediately ready to use, including loaded ammunition if appropriate.
You can summon a spellcasting focus from the Arsenal as part of casting a spell and return it immediately afterward.

entries.name: Arsenal Reach
entries: When you make a weapon attack, you can cause the weapon to emerge from the Arsenal at a point you can see within 30 feet of you.
Make the attack as though you occupied that point for determining the attack's reach and line of attack.
After the attack resolves, the weapon immediately returns to your Arsenal or your hand.
You can use Arsenal Reach once per turn.

entries.name: Level 17 — Endless Armory
entries: Once on each of your turns when you make an attack with a weapon from your Arsenal, you can make one additional weapon attack with a different stored weapon as part of the same Action.
This additional attack requires no Action or Bonus Action.

entries.name: Rain of Steel
entries: Once per Long Rest, you can use an Action to open the Arsenal around yourself.
Choose any number of creatures you can see within 60 feet, up to your Proficiency Bonus.
For each chosen creature, select a weapon currently stored in your Arsenal and make one weapon attack against that creature with the selected weapon.
A weapon can be used for only one of these attacks.
After all attacks resolve, every weapon used immediately returns to the Arsenal.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Vessel
entries: Magic need not be spent when it is cast. Some power can be caught, sealed, and taught to wait.

You create a supernatural container called your Pact Vessel. Its form is your choice: a bottle, lantern, gemstone, scroll case, orb, reliquary, card, ring, or another Tiny object capable of symbolically containing something.
If the Vessel is lost or destroyed, you can recreate it during a Short or Long Rest. Creating a new Vessel causes the previous one to disappear, but any magic stored within it is preserved.

entries.name: Seal a Spell
entries: When you cast a spell with a casting time of an Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction, you can choose to seal the spell inside your Pact Vessel instead of producing its normal effect.

The spell is cast normally: a spell slot is expended normally, Material components are provided and consumed normally, and any other resources required by the spell are expended normally. The spell produces no effect when sealed.
The Vessel can hold one sealed spell at a time. You can't seal a spell whose level is higher than the maximum shown by Deepening Vessel.

entries.name: Release the Spell
entries: While holding your Pact Vessel, you can release a sealed spell using the same type of action required by the spell's normal casting time.

When released, no spell slot is expended and no Material components are required again. You make all targeting and other choices at the moment of release, and range and area are measured from the releaser's current position.
The spell uses the same spellcasting ability, spell save DC, and spell attack bonus it had when sealed, and it counts as being cast by the creature that originally sealed it.
Once released, the spell disappears from the Vessel.

entries.name: Held Casting
entries: A sealed spell remains in the Vessel until it is released, replaced, or willingly erased. There is no time limit on how long it can remain sealed, and finishing a rest doesn't remove it.

entries.name: Pass the Vessel
entries: Another creature can hold your Pact Vessel and release a spell stored within it.
When it does so, the spell still uses the original caster's spellcasting statistics and treats the creature releasing it as the point of origin.
The creature doesn't need to know the spell or possess spellcasting.
If the spell requires Concentration, the creature that released the spell maintains that Concentration.

entries.name: Replace the Contents
entries: If you seal another spell while the Vessel already contains one, you can choose to erase the existing spell and replace it. The erased spell and resources originally spent to cast it aren't refunded.

entries.name: Level 5 — Greater Vessel
entries: You can seal spells of 2nd level or lower.
Your Vessel can now hold two spells simultaneously. When you seal a spell, choose which space within the Vessel contains it.

entries.name: Level 11 — Vault of Spells
entries: You can seal spells of 4th level or lower, and your Vessel can hold three spells simultaneously.
Additionally, when a creature you can see within 60 feet casts a spell of a level you can store, you can use your Reaction to attempt to capture it.
Make an ability check using your spellcasting ability against a DC equal to 10 + the spell's level. On a success, the spell is sealed inside an empty space in your Vessel instead of taking effect.
The original caster still expends the spell slot and any components normally.
Once you successfully capture a spell this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Level 17 — Endless Vessel
entries: You can seal spells of 6th level or lower, and your Vessel can hold five spells simultaneously.

items: {@b Swift Release.} Once on each of your turns, when you release a spell with a casting time of an Action, you can release it as a Bonus Action instead.
{@b Perfect Capture.} When you use your Reaction to capture a spell of 6th level or lower, you no longer make an ability check. The spell is automatically sealed if your Vessel has an empty space.
{@b Overflow.} If your Vessel is full when you successfully capture a spell, you can immediately erase one stored spell to make room for the captured one.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Brand
entries: Some marks are written on flesh. Yours is written on certainty.
Once you have claimed a creature with your Brand, distance becomes less useful, concealment less reliable, and escape increasingly difficult.
You gain the ability to place a supernatural mark called your Pact Brand upon another creature.

entries.name: Place the Brand
entries: As a Bonus Action, choose one creature you can see within 60 feet.
The creature becomes Branded by you until you dismiss the Brand, you Brand another creature, or the creature dies.
You can have only one Branded creature at a time.
The Brand can appear visibly on the creature in a form you choose, or remain completely invisible.
Placing the Brand doesn't require a saving throw and doesn't by itself Charm, damage, or otherwise control the creature.

entries.name: Hunter's Certainty
entries: While the Branded creature is on the same plane of existence as you, you always know its direction from you, its approximate distance from you, whether it is conscious or unconscious, and whether it is currently moving.
The creature gains no indication that you are sensing this information.

entries.name: Marked Beyond Sight
entries: You can perceive the Branded creature even when it is Invisible, Heavily Obscured, Hidden from you, or behind ordinary walls or other physical cover.
This doesn't allow you to see the surrounding area through those obstructions. You simply perceive the creature's exact position as a supernatural outline.
The Brand doesn't grant line of effect through barriers.

entries.name: Claim the Opening
entries: Once on each of your turns when you deal damage to the Branded creature, you can deal an additional {@damage 1d6} Force or Psychic damage, your choice.
You choose the damage type each time.

entries.name: Refuse Escape
entries: When the Branded creature willingly teleports or otherwise instantly moves to another space within 120 feet of you, you can use your Reaction to immediately move to an unoccupied space within 10 feet of it.
This movement isn't teleportation, and you don't provoke Opportunity Attacks from this movement.

entries.name: Level 5 — Relentless Mark
entries: Claim the Opening increases to {@damage 1d8}.
The Branded creature gains no benefit against you from being Invisible.
You can target it with attacks and effects that require you to see the target as long as your Brand allows you to perceive its exact position.

entries.name: Level 11 — Unbroken Pursuit
entries: You can maintain Brands on two creatures simultaneously.
When you use Place the Brand while already at this limit, choose which existing Brand ends.
Refuse Escape can trigger when a Branded creature teleports or instantly moves from anywhere within 300 feet of you.
When you follow it, you can appear within 5 feet of the creature instead of 10 feet.

entries.name: Level 17 — No Refuge
entries: You can maintain Brands on up to three creatures simultaneously.
Your Brand functions across planar boundaries. You always know which plane each Branded creature occupies.

entries.name: Follow Anywhere
entries: When a Branded creature teleports, travels to another plane, or is magically transported elsewhere, you can use your Reaction to follow it.
You appear in the nearest safe unoccupied space within 10 feet of the creature, even if doing so crosses planar boundaries.

entries.name: Final Claim
entries: Claim the Opening increases to {@damage 2d8}.
Once on each of your turns when you damage a Branded creature, you can also choose one of the following effects:

items: {@b Hamper.} Its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.
{@b Expose.} It can't benefit from Half Cover or Three-Quarters Cover against you until the start of your next turn.

{@b Anchor.} Until the start of your next turn, if it attempts to teleport or travel to another plane, you immediately know and can use Follow Anywhere even if you would normally be unable to perceive the attempt.

optionalfeature.name: Living Margins
entries: The words in your tome have grown restless.
Ink crawls between paragraphs. Pages turn without wind. When commanded, fragments of the book tear themselves free—not as paper, but as living extensions of the knowledge written within.
Your Pact Tome can manifest supernatural Living Pages that act as extensions of yourself.

entries.name: Awaken the Pages
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can cause a number of spectral pages equal to your Proficiency Bonus to emerge from your Pact Tome.
The Living Pages remain until you dismiss them, your Pact Tome ceases to exist, or you are Incapacitated.
They can appear as parchment, floating runes, strips of glowing text, black sheets covered in shifting script, or another form appropriate to your Tome.
The pages aren't creatures and can't be targeted or damaged individually.

entries.name: Wandering Script
entries: As part of your movement on your turn, you can move the Living Pages up to 60 feet to a point you can see.

items: They can fly and hover.
They can pass through spaces as narrow as 1 inch.
They can turn pages, open unlocked doors, pull levers, and perform simple object interactions.
They can carry unattended objects weighing no more than 10 pounds per Living Page.
They can write, erase, copy, or arrange ordinary text.
They can retrieve or return objects to you.

entries: You perceive the exact location of every Living Page.

entries.name: Eyes Between the Lines
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can perceive through any one of your Living Pages until the start of your next turn.
While doing so, you can see and hear from its position as though you occupied its space.
You retain awareness of your own surroundings.
A Living Page has Darkvision out to 60 feet for this purpose.

entries.name: Spell Through the Page
entries: When you cast a spell with a range other than Self, you can choose one Living Page within 60 feet as the spell's point of origin.
You still cast the spell and provide all components normally.
Range, areas of effect, and lines of effect are measured from the chosen Living Page.
If the spell requires you to see a target, you must be able to see it either normally or through that Living Page.
After originating a spell in this way, that Living Page disappears.

entries.name: Hand of the Tome
entries: When you cast a spell with a range of Touch, one Living Page can deliver it to a creature or object within 5 feet of that page.
The page disappears after delivering the spell.

entries.name: Written Relay
entries: You can write a message of up to 25 words into your Pact Tome and send one Living Page to a creature you know.
The page travels toward that creature by the most direct route it can navigate at a flying speed of 120 feet.
When it reaches the creature, your message appears upon the page in whatever language you wrote it.
The recipient can write a response of up to 25 words, after which the page returns to you.
There is no fixed maximum distance, but the page can't cross planar boundaries.

optionalfeature.name: Scripted Recursion
entries: Some spells are written to be cast once.
Yours are written to remember the shape of their own casting.
Your Pact Tome can preserve a magical pattern after you cast it, allowing the book to reproduce that spell again.

entries.name: Record the Casting
entries: When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher using a spell slot, you can cause your Pact Tome to record that exact casting as a Recursion Script.

The script records the spell, the level at which it was cast, any choices made as part of the spell that are determined when casting it, and the spellcasting ability, spell save DC, and spell attack bonus used.
The script doesn't record targets, locations, or directions unless the spell itself permanently requires those choices when cast.
You can have only one Recursion Script recorded at a time. Recording a new one erases the old script.

entries.name: Recast the Script
entries: While holding your Pact Tome, you can cast the recorded spell from the Recursion Script without expending a spell slot or providing any components.
You choose targets, points of origin, directions, and other choices that are normally made at the moment of casting.
The spell is cast at the same level stored in the script.
Once you use the Recursion Script, it disappears.

entries.name: Persistent Formula
entries: A Recursion Script remains in your Pact Tome until you use it, replace it, or willingly erase it.
Finishing a Short or Long Rest doesn't remove it.
The script also survives the destruction or recreation of your Pact Tome and reappears within the recreated Tome.

entries.name: Level 11 — Double Script
entries: You can maintain two Recursion Scripts at once.
Each script can hold a different spell or a different casting of the same spell.
Additionally, when you cast a spell recorded in one of your scripts using a spell slot normally, you can choose to refresh that script with the new casting instead of erasing it.

entries.name: Level 15 — Perfect Repetition
entries: When you use a Recursion Script, roll a d6.
On a 5 or 6, the script isn't erased.
You can immediately use it again later.
A script preserved this way can continue to preserve itself repeatedly.

entries.name: Level 17 — Recursive Chain
entries: You can maintain three Recursion Scripts at once.
Once on each of your turns, when you cast a spell from a Recursion Script with a casting time of an Action, you can immediately begin a Recursive Chain.
If you cast a different spell before the end of your next turn, you can choose to record that spell into the script you just consumed instead of losing the script completely.
The newly recorded spell can be of any level you are normally capable of casting.

entries.name: Level 19 — The Tome Casts Again
entries: Once per Long Rest, when you cast a spell from a Recursion Script, you can command the Tome to reproduce the script without consuming it.
The spell is cast normally from the script, but the Recursion Script remains intact automatically.
If Scripted Recursion would already preserve the script from another effect, that doesn't grant an additional casting.

optionalfeature.name: Unwritten Chapter
entries: There are pages in your tome that were never written.
They wait for knowledge you do not possess.
When need becomes great enough, the empty page supplies its own answer.
Your Pact Tome contains a supernatural section called the Unwritten Chapter.

entries.name: Write the Unknown
entries: When you finish a Long Rest, choose one spell from any spell list.
The spell appears within your Pact Tome as though written there by an unseen hand.
The spell remains in the Unwritten Chapter until you replace it after another Long Rest.
You don't need to have previously seen, learned, prepared, or encountered the spell.

entries.name: Borrowed Formula
entries: While the spell remains written in your Unwritten Chapter, you can cast it using any spell slots you possess of the appropriate level.
The spell counts as prepared for you.
It doesn't need to belong to any spell list normally available to you.
You use your normal spellcasting ability for it.
You can cast it at higher levels normally if you have higher-level spell slots.
