You provide the spell's components normally.

entries.name: The Tome Understands
entries: The Unwritten Chapter contains enough supernatural instruction for you to cast its spell correctly even if you don't understand its original magical tradition.
For example, the Tome could contain a divine prayer, primal invocation, occult formula, or arcane theorem without requiring you to adopt the tradition it came from.
The spell remains the spell it normally is; the Tome simply gives you a usable formula for it.

entries.name: Level 13 — Two Answers
entries: Your Unwritten Chapter can contain two spells at the same time.
When you finish a Long Rest, you can replace either or both.

entries.name: Level 17 — Forbidden Chapter
entries: Your Unwritten Chapter can contain three spells at the same time.
When you finish a Long Rest, you can replace any or all of them.

entries.name: Level 19 — The Missing Spell
entries: Once per Long Rest, when you encounter a problem and realize that a particular spell would solve it, you can use a Bonus Action to immediately replace one spell in your Unwritten Chapter with another spell of your choice.
You don't need to finish a Long Rest.
The newly written spell is immediately available to cast.
You can do this even during combat.

optionalfeature.name: Pages of Appraisal
entries: The tome does not merely record what something appears to be.
It watches. Compares. Corrects.
Every action becomes another line of evidence, until disguise gives way to understanding.
Your Pact Tome can create supernatural dossiers on creatures you encounter.

entries.name: Open a Dossier
entries: As a Bonus Action, choose one creature you can see within 60 feet.
A page in your Pact Tome becomes dedicated to that creature as its Dossier.
You can maintain a number of Dossiers equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If you exceed this limit, choose one existing Dossier to erase.
A Dossier remains until you erase it, even if the creature dies or leaves your plane of existence.

entries.name: Initial Appraisal
entries: When you create a Dossier, the Tome immediately records the creature's creature type, Size, current and maximum Hit Points, Armor Class, Speeds, senses, languages it can speak, damage Vulnerabilities, Resistances, and Immunities, and condition Immunities.
The creature isn't aware that this information has been recorded.

entries.name: Observed Truth
entries: Whenever a creature with a Dossier uses a trait, action, Bonus Action, Reaction, spell, supernatural ability, Legendary Action, or similar feature that you can perceive, the Tome permanently records that feature.

The entry includes enough information for you to understand what the feature does, its range and area, its damage or healing, its saving throw or attack roll if any, its recharge or usage limitation, whether it requires Concentration, and any trigger or condition required to use it.
You don't need to spend an action reading a feature already recorded by the Tome; you can recall its contents perfectly.

entries.name: Updating Record
entries: While a creature with a Dossier is within 120 feet of you, its page updates automatically.
You always know its current Hit Points, current conditions, whether it is concentrating, and whether it has expended or regained a feature already recorded in the Dossier.
The Tome doesn't reveal a feature it has never observed merely because that feature exists.

entries.name: Level 9 — Read the Pattern
entries: After observing a creature with a Dossier for at least 1 round, the Tome also records its Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores, its saving throw bonuses, its skill proficiencies and bonuses, its Proficiency Bonus, and its spellcasting ability, spell save DC, and spell attack bonus, if any.
Additionally, whenever the creature casts a spell you can perceive, the Tome records the spell's name and level before its effects resolve.

entries.name: Level 13 — Predictive Annotation
entries: Your Tome begins predicting behavior from everything it has recorded.
Once on each of your turns when you make an attack roll against a creature with a Dossier, you can gain Advantage on that roll.
Alternatively, when that creature makes a saving throw against one of your spells or abilities, you can impose Disadvantage on that saving throw.
You can use only one of these benefits per turn.

entries.name: Level 17 — Complete Dossier
entries: After you have observed a creature with a Dossier for at least 1 minute, the Tome completes its analysis.

It reveals every currently existing trait, action, spell, reaction, resistance, immunity, vulnerability, transformation, resource, and other game feature possessed by that creature, including those you haven't personally witnessed.

It also reveals which features are currently available or expended, any alternate forms it possesses, the conditions required to activate those forms or features, any regeneration, resurrection, or death-prevention abilities it possesses, and any specific method described in its statistics for bypassing, suppressing, or defeating one of its features.

entries.name: Exploit the Margin
entries: Once on each of your turns when you damage a creature whose Dossier is complete, you can choose one damage type dealt by that attack, spell, or effect.
For that instance of damage, the creature's Resistance to that damage type is ignored.
If it is Immune instead, treat that Immunity as Resistance for that instance.
This doesn't permanently alter the creature's defenses.

optionalfeature.name: Stolen Footnote
entries: Not every secret is a spell.
Some are written in muscle, blood, instinct, training, divinity, monstrous anatomy, or stranger things.
Your tome has never cared about the distinction.
Your Pact Tome can record a feature possessed or used by another creature and preserve it as a Stolen Footnote.

entries.name: Cite the Ability
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet uses or visibly demonstrates a feature, you can use your Reaction to record that feature in your Pact Tome after its use resolves. A passive or continuous feature can be recorded when you directly observe its effect or otherwise learn that the creature possesses it.

You can record a trait, Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, spell, Spellcasting feature, class feature, species feature, monster feature, Legendary Action, Lair Action, Mythic Action, Multiattack, transformation, movement mode, sense, aura, regeneration, resistance, immunity, vulnerability, or another game feature or statistic with a defined mechanical effect.
The Tome records the chosen feature as it exists for that creature. You don't need to understand how the creature performs it.
You can maintain one Stolen Footnote at a time. Recording another replaces the previous one.

entries.name: Use the Footnote
entries: While holding your Pact Tome, you can use the recorded feature as though it appeared among your own features.

If the feature normally uses an Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction, you use the same type of action. If it uses a special action economy you don't possess, such as a Legendary Action, Lair Action, or Mythic Action, you use it as a Bonus Action instead unless the feature itself already requires an Action or Reaction.

If the feature is passive or continuous, you can invoke it as a Bonus Action and gain its benefits for 1 minute, or until you are Incapacitated. If the feature represents a movement mode, sense, resistance, immunity, vulnerability, aura, regeneration, Armor Class calculation, or similar continuous statistic, it functions for that duration exactly as recorded, using the adaptations described below when necessary.

If the feature is a spell or Spellcasting feature, you can use it without needing the original creature's class, spell list, spellbook, focus, or other unique spellcasting structure. Any spell slot or unique resource supplied by the recorded feature is provided by the Footnote for that use. Components required by a spell are still required unless the recorded feature itself ignores them.
After you use or invoke the Stolen Footnote, it disappears from the Tome unless another part of this invocation preserves it.

entries.name: Translate the Feature
entries: Your Tome translates the recorded feature into a form you can perform. You don't need the anatomy, species, creature type, class, size, equipment, lair, legendary status, transformation, or physical structure normally required to use it.

The Tome creates a magical analogue whenever necessary. Spectral wings can perform a wing attack, spectral jaws can reproduce a bite, runes can reproduce a gaze, the Tome can supply a monstrous roar, and an effect tied to a lair can manifest from the Tome or the space around you.
If the feature requires an attack roll, use your spell attack modifier unless the recorded feature specifies another fixed bonus.
If it requires a saving throw, use your spell save DC unless the recorded feature specifies another fixed DC.

If it uses the original creature's ability modifier, Proficiency Bonus, level, Hit Dice, or similar personal statistic to calculate a number, use your corresponding statistic when possible. If no corresponding statistic exists, use your spellcasting ability modifier, your Proficiency Bonus, or your character level, whichever most closely matches the original calculation.

If the feature creates or depends on an object, body part, weapon, organ, limb, terrain element, or other prerequisite you don't possess, the Tome can manifest a temporary magical analogue that exists only for the feature's duration.
Copying a feature doesn't permanently change your creature type, body, statistics, class, species, or identity unless the feature itself explicitly changes one of those things.

entries.name: Everything Can Be Cited
entries: Stolen Footnote isn't limited by the origin of a feature. If it has a defined game effect and belongs to or is used by a creature you can observe, the Tome can record it.

This includes passive defenses, supernatural anatomy, special senses, alternate forms, innate spellcasting, entire activated traits, Legendary and Mythic features, and abilities that would normally be impossible for your body to reproduce.

If a recorded entry contains several linked effects as one feature, such as Multiattack or a transformation that grants a package of abilities, the Footnote records the complete feature rather than only one sentence from it.

entries.name: Level 13 — Two Footnotes
entries: Your Pact Tome can hold two Stolen Footnotes simultaneously. They can come from the same creature or different creatures.

If a recorded feature normally has limited uses, a Recharge roll, Legendary Action cost, Mythic requirement, or a resource unique to its original creature, your single use of the Stolen Footnote supplies that requirement automatically. You don't need the original creature's resource.

entries.name: Level 17 — Perfect Citation
entries: Your Tome can hold three Stolen Footnotes simultaneously.
When you use or invoke a Stolen Footnote, roll a d6. On a 5 or 6, the Footnote remains in your Tome instead of disappearing.

entries.name: Rewrite the Scale
entries: When you use a recorded feature, you can calculate any damage, healing, range, area, number of targets, or similar value that normally scales from the original creature's CR, level, Hit Dice, Proficiency Bonus, or similar progression using your character level or Proficiency Bonus instead, using the nearest equivalent progression represented by the feature.
If the feature doesn't scale, it remains unchanged.

entries.name: Level 19 — Plagiarism Perfected
entries: Once per Long Rest, when a creature you can see within 120 feet uses or reveals an eligible feature, you can record it without using your Reaction.
You can then immediately use or invoke that Stolen Footnote as part of the same trigger, provided the recorded feature can meaningfully function at that moment.
Doing so doesn't erase another Footnote if you have an empty Footnote slot.

optionalfeature.name: Wellspring of the Tome
entries: Every spell leaves something behind.
Power gathers between the lines, beneath the ink, and within the spaces no reader notices.
As the tome deepens, those remnants cease to be traces.
They become an entire second reservoir of magic.
Your Pact Tome develops its own reserve of magical power, granting you additional spell slots called Tome Slots.

entries.name: Tome Slots
entries: Tome Slots are additional spell slots separate from those granted by your classes, species, feats, magic items, or other features.
You can expend a Tome Slot whenever you would normally expend a spell slot.
A Tome Slot can also be used to upcast a spell normally.
You regain all expended Tome Slots when you finish a Long Rest.
Destroying, dismissing, or recreating your Pact Tome doesn't restore expended Tome Slots.

entries.name: Level 5 — First Reservoir
entries: You gain one 1st-level Tome Slot, one 2nd-level Tome Slot, and one 3rd-level Tome Slot.

entries.name: Level 9 — Deep Reservoir
entries: You additionally gain one 4th-level Tome Slot and one 5th-level Tome Slot.
You now have one additional spell slot of every level from 1st through 5th.

entries.name: Level 13 — Greater Reservoir
entries: You additionally gain one 6th-level Tome Slot and one 7th-level Tome Slot.
You now have one additional spell slot of every level from 1st through 7th.

entries.name: Level 17 — Endless Reservoir
entries: You additionally gain one 8th-level Tome Slot and one 9th-level Tome Slot.
You now have one additional spell slot of every level from 1st through 9th.

entries.name: Reflow the Ink
entries: When you finish a Short Rest, you can restore expended Tome Slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed your Proficiency Bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier.
For example, with a Proficiency Bonus of +6 and a spellcasting ability modifier of +5, you could restore up to 11 total levels of Tome Slots.
Once you use Reflow the Ink, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Level 19 — Overflowing Archive
entries: You gain a second Tome Slot of each of the following levels: 6th, 7th, 8th, and 9th.

entries.name: Bottomless Page
entries: Once per Long Rest, when you expend a Tome Slot of 6th level or higher, you can cause the Tome to restore that slot immediately after the spell resolves.
You choose to use Bottomless Page after the spell resolves.

optionalfeature.name: Ascending Formula
entries: Most spell formulas end exactly where the power invested in them ends.
Your tome has learned to keep writing.
One more line. One more circle. One more impossible step beyond what the spell slot should have been able to sustain.
While holding your Pact Tome, you can use its accumulated knowledge to cast spells at a higher level than the spell slot you expend.

entries.name: Overcast
entries: When you cast a spell using a spell slot, you can cause your Pact Tome to increase the spell's effective spell level by 1.

For example, a spell cast using a 2nd-level slot functions as though cast with a 3rd-level slot, a spell cast using a 4th-level slot functions as though cast with a 5th-level slot, and a spell cast using an 8th-level slot functions as though cast with a 9th-level slot.
You still expend only the original spell slot.

The spell uses its increased level for all purposes, including At Higher Levels effects, damage and healing scaling, number of targets, duration or area increases, interactions with effects that check spell level, and any other feature that checks the spell's level.
Overcast can't increase a spell beyond 9th level unless Formula Beyond Measure specifically allows otherwise.
You can use Overcast a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Level 11 — Deep Formula
entries: When you use Overcast, you can increase the spell's effective level by up to 2 levels instead of 1.
Using either a +1 or +2 increase expends only one use of Overcast.
For example, a spell cast using a 3rd-level slot can function as though cast using a 5th-level slot.

entries.name: Level 15 — Efficient Ascension
entries: Once on each of your turns when you use Overcast to increase a spell by only 1 level, roll a d6 after the spell resolves.
On a 4–6, the use of Overcast isn't expended.
This doesn't restore the spell slot.

entries.name: Excess Formula
entries: If a spell has no benefit from being cast at one of the intermediate levels you pass through, that doesn't prevent you from Overcasting it.
For example, a spell that gains a new effect only at 6th level can be cast using a 4th-level slot and increased by 2 levels to gain that 6th-level benefit.

entries.name: Level 17 — Grand Overcast
entries: You can increase a spell by up to 3 levels with a single use of Overcast.
For example, a 3rd-level slot can produce a 6th-level casting, a 5th-level slot can produce an 8th-level casting, and a 6th-level slot can produce a 9th-level casting.
Additionally, once per Long Rest, you can use Overcast without expending one of its uses.

entries.name: Level 19 — Formula Beyond Measure
entries: Once per Long Rest, when you cast a spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, you can invoke Formula Beyond Measure.
The spell is treated as though it were cast using a 9th-level spell slot, regardless of the slot actually expended.
This doesn't expend a use of Overcast.

entries.name: Overflow Beyond Ninth
entries: If you expend an actual 9th-level spell slot, you can instead use Formula Beyond Measure to treat the casting as 10th level solely for determining numerical or scalable effects that explicitly increase when cast using a higher-level spell slot.
This doesn't create a 10th-level spell, doesn't allow you to learn or cast spells above 9th level, and doesn't bypass restrictions that specifically require something other than spell level.
For example, a spell that deals one additional damage die for each slot level above its base level gains one additional step of scaling beyond its normal 9th-level casting.

optionalfeature.name: Condensed Formula
entries: Most spell formulas waste power.
Tradition calls the excess necessary. Your tome calls it poor notation.
Line by line, the formula contracts until the same miracle fits inside a smaller measure of magic.
Your Pact Tome can compress spells into more efficient forms, allowing you to cast them using lower-level spell slots without weakening the resulting spell.

entries.name: Spell Compression
entries: When you cast a spell of 2nd level or higher that is written in your Pact Tome, you can cast it using a spell slot 1 level lower than the spell's normal level.
The spell still functions as a spell of its original level.
For example, a 2nd-level spell can use a 1st-level slot, a 4th-level spell can use a 3rd-level slot, and a 7th-level spell can use a 6th-level slot.

For every purpose other than the slot actually expended, the spell retains its normal level. This includes damage and healing, saving throws and attack rolls, Counterspell and Dispel Magic interactions, effects that check the spell's level, Concentration, duration, area, and number of targets.
You can use Spell Compression a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
A spell can never be compressed below a 1st-level spell slot.

entries.name: Level 13 — Deep Compression
entries: You can reduce the required spell slot by up to 2 levels instead of 1.
For example, a 3rd-level spell can use a 1st-level slot, a 5th-level spell can use a 3rd-level slot, and a 9th-level spell can use a 7th-level slot.
Using either one or two levels of compression expends only one use.

entries.name: Compressed Upcasting
entries: You can also apply Spell Compression to an upcast spell.
Determine the level at which you want the spell to function, then reduce the slot actually expended.
For example, you could cast a 3rd-level spell as a 6th-level casting while expending only a 4th-level spell slot.
The spell functions as a 6th-level spell for all purposes.

entries.name: Level 17 — Perfect Compression
entries: You can reduce the required slot by up to 3 levels.
For example, a 4th-level spell can use a 1st-level slot, a 6th-level spell can use a 3rd-level slot, an 8th-level spell can use a 5th-level slot, and a 9th-level spell can use a 6th-level slot.
Additionally, the first time after each Long Rest that you use Spell Compression, it doesn't expend one of your uses.

entries.name: Efficient Notation
entries: When you use Spell Compression and expend a spell slot of 3rd level or lower, roll a d6 after the spell resolves.
On a 5 or 6, the use of Spell Compression isn't expended.
The spell slot is still expended normally.

entries.name: Level 19 — Formula Without Waste
entries: Your mastery of compressed spellcraft becomes extreme.
Once per Long Rest, when you cast a spell written in your Pact Tome, you can use Perfect Formula.

entries.name: Perfect Formula
entries: Choose the level at which the spell will function, up to 9th level.
You expend a spell slot only half that level, rounded up.
The spell functions at its full chosen level for every purpose.
Perfect Formula doesn't expend a use of Spell Compression.

optionalfeature.name: Sovereign Armament
entries: Your pact weapon no longer behaves like an ordinary weapon enchanted by magic. It recognizes only one authority: yours. Its shape, balance, and method of killing rearrange themselves around your intent. In your hands, a single weapon can answer problems that would normally demand an entire arsenal.
Whenever you summon or bond with your Pact Weapon, you can cause it to take the form of any Simple or Martial melee or ranged weapon. You are proficient with every form it takes.

Changing its form requires no action, and you can do so immediately before or after any attack you make with it. A magical weapon bonded through Pact of the Blade retains its magical properties regardless of the form, unless a property logically requires its original form.

Whenever the weapon changes form, choose up to two of the following properties for it: Finesse, Light, Reach, Thrown (30/90), Two-Handed, or Versatile (1d10). If it already has a property you choose, choose another instead. You can also remove the Heavy property whenever you change its form.

While you wield it, the Pact Weapon ignores ordinary limitations of shape. You can use it even when its form would normally be impractical for your Size, and changing its form never causes you to drop it.
If the weapon requires ammunition, it creates the mundane ammunition needed for each attack as part of that attack. The ammunition disappears after the attack resolves.

entries.name: Level 5
entries: Your Pact Weapon gains a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls unless it already has an equal or greater bonus.
Whenever you hit with it, you can choose for the attack to deal Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, or Force damage regardless of the weapon's form.

entries.name: Level 11
entries: You can have three of the listed weapon properties on your Pact Weapon at the same time.
Immediately before each attack, you can independently change its form, damage type, and chosen weapon properties for that attack. Its inherent magical properties remain through these transformations.

entries.name: Level 17
entries: Your Pact Weapon gains a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls unless it already has an equal or greater bonus.
It can have any number of the listed weapon properties at the same time.
Its Reach increases by 5 feet.
Its normal and long ranges are doubled whenever it is in a ranged or Thrown form.
Its attacks ignore Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, and Force damage.
It can't be forcibly removed from your grasp while you are conscious.
If it leaves your hand, it can return to you immediately after the attack or effect resolves, requiring no action.

optionalfeature.name: Severing Edge
entries: Your pact weapon has learned to cut things that were never meant to possess an edge. A ward can be split. A curse can be opened. A spell can be wounded until its structure collapses. Where ordinary steel meets magic and stops, your weapon continues.
Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with your Pact Weapon, you can choose one spell or magical effect currently affecting that creature that you are aware of.

Make an ability check using your spellcasting ability. The DC equals 10 + the spell's level. On a success, that spell or magical effect ends on the creature as though successfully dispelled. If the effect has no spell level, the GM determines an equivalent level for this purpose.

When your Pact Weapon damages a creature that is concentrating, the creature has Disadvantage on the Constitution saving throw it makes to maintain Concentration from that damage. If the attack is a Critical Hit, the creature instead automatically fails that Concentration saving throw.

entries.name: Level 11
entries: Your Pact Weapon can strike magical effects directly.
As an Action, you can make one attack with your Pact Weapon against a magical barrier, ward, conjured structure, magical restraint, magical portal, or similar magical manifestation you can perceive.

On a hit, choose one: deal the weapon's normal damage to the manifestation if it can take damage; make a spellcasting ability check against DC 10 + the effect's spell level to end it as though successfully dispelled; or suppress one of its magical properties until the start of your next turn.

If the effect has no spell level, the GM determines an equivalent level for the ability check. A manifestation with no AC has an AC equal to 10 + its spell level, or a value determined by the GM if it has no spell level.

entries.name: Level 17
entries: Once per Long Rest, when you hit a creature or magical manifestation with your Pact Weapon, choose one magical effect affecting the target that you are aware of.
That effect ends immediately without an ability check if it was created by a spell of level 8 or lower.
For a 9th-level spell, Artifact, deity-created effect, or magic of comparable power, make a spellcasting ability check against DC 19 instead. On a success, the effect ends on that target.

optionalfeature.name: Spell-Eater
entries: Magic that fails to take hold of you doesn't simply disperse. You tear the dying spell from the Weave, swallow its structure whole, and keep it inside yourself until you decide what to do with it.

When a creature casts a spell of level 1 or higher that targets you or includes you in its area, you can use your Reaction to devour that spell after it fails to affect you because its spell attack misses you, you succeed on its saving throw and suffer no effect from it, or another feature causes the spell to have no effect on you.
You can keep one spell devoured this way at a time. Devouring another spell replaces the one you were already keeping. A spell you keep this way remains available until you finish a Long Rest.

While you are keeping a spell this way, you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You use your own spellcasting ability, spell attack modifier, and spell save DC, use the level at which the spell was originally cast, and make any choices normally made by the caster.
You must still provide any Material component that has a listed cost or is consumed by the spell. After you cast the spell, you are no longer keeping it.

entries.name: Level 5
entries: You can devour a spell of up to 3rd level.

entries.name: Level 11
entries: You can devour a spell of up to 6th level.
You can keep up to two spells devoured this way at the same time.

entries.name: Level 17
entries: You can devour spells of any level.
You can keep up to three spells devoured this way at the same time.
When you successfully devour a spell that targets only you, you can cause it to be completely consumed. If it would normally produce a lingering effect after resolving, that effect isn't created.

The weapon never seems to finish an attack at the same moment as its wielder. Each successful strike leaves behind a pale imitation of itself, suspended for a heartbeat before completing the attack again.
You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
Whenever you hit a creature with an attack using this weapon, a delayed copy of that attack remains behind.
At the start of your next turn, every delayed attack repeats against the same target if that target is still within the weapon's normal reach or range.

items: Roll a new attack roll using the same attack bonus as the original attack.
The repeated attack requires no Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction.
On a hit, it deals the weapon's normal damage plus 1d8 Force damage.
It otherwise counts as an attack made with the weapon.
A repeated ranged attack doesn't expend ammunition.
A repeated attack can't create another delayed attack.

If the original target is no longer a valid target, you can redirect the repeated attack to another creature within 5 feet of the original target's last position, provided that creature is within the weapon's normal reach or range.

entries: There is no limit to the number of delayed attacks you can have at one time.
The armor never absorbs an impact cleanly. Every strike leaves a faint pressure beneath its surface, as though the force is waiting for somewhere else to go.
You gain a +2 bonus to AC while wearing this magic armor.
Whenever you take Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, or Force damage, the armor records the amount of damage you actually took after Resistance and other reductions.

Before the end of your next turn, the next time you hit a creature with an attack, you can release the stored force through that attack. The target takes additional Force damage equal to half the recorded damage, rounded up.
If you take qualifying damage multiple times before releasing it, the amounts are added together.
There is no limit to how much damage can be accumulated this way, but all stored damage disappears at the end of your next turn if you haven't released it.
If the attack used to release the stored force is a Critical Hit, the additional Force damage is instead equal to the full amount of damage recorded.
